# Stufe 0 — Pre-flight: Environment-Validierung (`doctor.py`)

## Zweck

Das Environment ist laut Nutzer **bereits eingerichtet** (Linux, ROCm, PyTorch-ROCm-Build,
AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX). Diese Stufe **installiert nichts** und ändert nichts — sie
**validiert** nur und meldet klar PASS/FAIL mit Remediation-Hinweisen. Ziel: vor dem
Training (Stufe 5) sicherstellen, dass die GPU wirklich nutzbar ist, statt es anzunehmen.

> Wichtig für Claude Code: **Keine** `pip install` / `uv add` von torch ausführen. Wenn
> ein Pflicht-Check fehlschlägt, den Befund melden und Rücksprache halten — nicht
> versuchen, ROCm/PyTorch eigenmächtig „zu reparieren". Reine App-Abhängigkeiten
> (opencv, python-chess, typer, pyyaml) dürfen normal installiert werden.

## CLI

```
chesslab doctor [--gpu] [--camera 0] [--json]
```

- ohne Flags: Basis-Checks (Python, App-Deps, Konfig-Pfade).
- `--gpu`: zusätzlich die komplette ROCm/PyTorch-GPU-Validierung (Pflicht vor Stufe 5).
- `--camera N`: Kamera-Check für Index N (öffnen + ein Frame lesen).
- `--json`: maschinenlesbarer Report zusätzlich zur menschenlesbaren Ausgabe.

Exit-Code: `0` nur wenn **alle angeforderten** Pflicht-Checks bestehen, sonst `!= 0`.

## Checks

### A) Basis (immer)
1. Python `>= 3.11`.
2. Import der App-Deps: `cv2`, `numpy`, `PIL`, `chess`, `typer`, `yaml`. Versionen loggen.
3. Daten-/Konfig-Verzeichnisse existieren oder werden angelegt (`data/...`).

### B) GPU / ROCm (`--gpu`, Pflicht vor Training)
Reihenfolge so, dass die Diagnose den Fehler eingrenzt:

1. `import torch` gelingt; `torch.__version__` loggen. **Erwartung:** enthält `+rocm`
   (z. B. `2.x.y+rocm6.2`). Enthält es stattdessen `+cu...`, ist der **falsche
   (CUDA-)Build** installiert -> FAIL mit klarem Hinweis.
2. `torch.version.hip is not None` -> bestätigt ROCm-Build. (`torch.version.cuda` ist
   beim ROCm-Build typischerweise `None`.) FAIL, wenn `hip` None ist.
3. `torch.cuda.is_available()` ist `True`. (Unter ROCm wird die `torch.cuda.*`-API
   bewusst wiederverwendet — das ist korrekt, nicht NVIDIA.) FAIL sonst.
4. `torch.cuda.device_count() >= 1`.
5. `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)` loggen. **Erwartung:** enthält `7900`, `Radeon` oder
   `AMD`. Andernfalls WARN (Name kann je nach Treiber generisch sein), kein harter FAIL.
6. `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory` loggen. **Erwartung:** ~24 GB
   (>= 20 GB als Schwelle). Darunter WARN.
7. **Echter Compute-Test (der entscheidende):**
   ```python
   x = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   y = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   z = (x @ y).sum().item()        # erzwingt Sync + Rücktransfer
   torch.cuda.synchronize()
   ```
   Läuft das ohne Exception und ist `z` endlich -> PASS. Crasht es (häufig bei
   gfx-Mismatch) -> FAIL mit Hinweis auf gfx-Target (siehe unten).
8. Optionaler System-Check via `subprocess` (nicht Pflicht, nur Info): `rocm-smi`
   und/oder `rocminfo` aufrufen, ROCm-Version und `gfx`-Target des Agents loggen. Fehlt
   das Binary -> WARN, kein FAIL (PyTorch-Checks sind maßgeblich).

### C) Kamera (`--camera N`)
1. `cv2.VideoCapture(N)` öffnet (unter Linux normales V4L2-Backend).
2. Mindestens ein Frame `read()` liefert ein nicht-leeres Bild; Auflösung loggen.
3. Hinweis ausgeben, ob `DISPLAY` gesetzt ist (für `cv2.imshow` in Stufe 1/3 nötig).
   Fehlt `DISPLAY` -> WARN: Kalibrierung/Aufnahme braucht eine GUI-Session.

## 7900 XTX / gfx1100 — Diagnosehinweise (in FAIL-Meldungen einbauen)

- Die 7900 XTX ist **gfx1100** und in aktuellen ROCm-Versionen offiziell unterstützt —
  `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` sollte **nicht** nötig sein. Auf einer unterstützten Karte
  ein Override zu setzen kann sogar schaden. Nur als allerletzten Fallback erwähnen
  (z. B. `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0`), nicht automatisch setzen.
- Falscher PyTorch-Build (CUDA statt ROCm) ist der häufigste Stolperstein: erkennbar an
  `+cu` in der Version bzw. `torch.version.hip is None`. Remediation-Hinweis: ROCm-Wheel
  vom `rocm`-Index neu installieren — aber **nur nach Rücksprache**, nicht automatisch.
- `torch.cuda.is_available() == False` trotz ROCm-Build: oft Treiber-/Permissions-Problem
  (User nicht in Gruppe `render`/`video`, oder `/dev/kfd` & `/dev/dri` nicht zugreifbar).
  Als Hinweis ausgeben, nicht selbst fixen.

## Report-Format

Menschenlesbar, eine Zeile pro Check: `[PASS] / [WARN] / [FAIL] <Check> — <Detail>`.
Am Ende eine Summenzeile. Bei `--json` zusätzlich:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": [
    {"name": "torch.rocm_build", "status": "pass", "detail": "2.4.1+rocm6.2"},
    {"name": "torch.cuda.is_available", "status": "pass", "detail": "true"},
    {"name": "gpu.compute", "status": "pass", "detail": "matmul 2048x2048 ok"},
    {"name": "gpu.name", "status": "pass", "detail": "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX"}
  ]
}
```

## Akzeptanzkriterien (Definition of Done)

- `chesslab doctor` (ohne `--gpu`) läuft auch ohne GPU/Kamera durch und prüft Basis-Deps.
- `chesslab doctor --gpu` gibt für jeden GPU-Check eine eigene PASS/WARN/FAIL-Zeile aus,
  inklusive des echten Matmul-Compute-Tests, und exit-codet korrekt.
- Bei falschem (CUDA-)Build erscheint eine **eindeutige** FAIL-Meldung, die den Build als
  Ursache benennt — kein generischer Stacktrace.
- `chesslab doctor --camera 0` öffnet die Kamera und liest einen Frame oder meldet sauber
  den Grund.
- Stufe 5 (`train`) ruft intern denselben GPU-Validierungspfad auf und bricht mit
  klarer Meldung ab, falls die GPU nicht nutzbar ist (statt still auf CPU zu fallen).

# Stage 0 — Pre-flight: Environment Validation (`doctor.py`)

## Purpose

The environment is **already set up** per the user (Linux, ROCm, PyTorch-ROCm-build,
AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX). This stage **installs nothing** and changes nothing — it only
**validates** and clearly reports PASS/FAIL with remediation hints. Goal: before
training (Stage 5), ensure the GPU is actually usable instead of assuming it.

> Important for Claude Code: **Do not** run `pip install` / `uv add` of torch. If
> a mandatory check fails, report the finding and consult — do not
> attempt to „fix" ROCm/PyTorch on your own. Pure app dependencies
> (opencv, python-chess, typer, pyyaml) may be installed normally.

## CLI

```
chesslab doctor [--gpu] [--camera 0] [--json]
```

- without flags: base checks (Python, app deps, config paths).
- `--gpu`: additionally runs the full ROCm/PyTorch GPU validation (mandatory before Stage 5).
- `--camera N`: camera check for index N (open + read one frame).
- `--json`: machine-readable report in addition to human-readable output.

Exit code: `0` only if **all requested** mandatory checks pass, otherwise `!= 0`.

## Checks

### A) Base (always)
1. Python `>= 3.11`.
2. Import app deps: `cv2`, `numpy`, `PIL`, `chess`, `typer`, `yaml`. Log versions.
3. Data/config directories exist or are created (`data/...`).

### B) GPU / ROCm (`--gpu`, mandatory before training)
Ordered so diagnostics can narrow down the error:

1. `import torch` succeeds; log `torch.__version__`. **Expected:** contains `+rocm`
   (e.g. `2.x.y+rocm6.2`). If it instead contains `+cu...`, the **wrong
   (CUDA) build** is installed -> FAIL with clear hint.
2. `torch.version.hip is not None` -> confirms ROCm build. (`torch.version.cuda` is
   typically `None` in a ROCm build.) FAIL if `hip` is None.
3. `torch.cuda.is_available()` is `True`. (Under ROCm the `torch.cuda.*` API is
   deliberately reused — this is correct, not NVIDIA.) FAIL otherwise.
4. `torch.cuda.device_count() >= 1`.
5. Log `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)`. **Expected:** contains `7900`, `Radeon` or
   `AMD`. Otherwise WARN (name may be generic depending on driver), not a hard FAIL.
6. Log `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory`. **Expected:** ~24 GB
   (>= 20 GB threshold). Below that WARN.
7. **Real compute test (the decisive one):**
   ```python
   x = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   y = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   z = (x @ y).sum().item()        # forces sync + transfer back
   torch.cuda.synchronize()
   ```
   If this runs without exception and `z` is finite -> PASS. If it crashes (common with
   gfx mismatch) -> FAIL with hint about gfx target (see below).
8. Optional system check via `subprocess` (not mandatory, info only): run `rocm-smi`
   and/or `rocminfo`, log ROCm version and the agent's `gfx` target. If the
   binary is missing -> WARN, not FAIL (PyTorch checks are authoritative).

### C) Camera (`--camera N`)
1. `cv2.VideoCapture(N)` opens (standard V4L2 backend on Linux).
2. At least one `read()` frame returns a non-empty image; log resolution.
3. Output a hint about whether `DISPLAY` is set (needed for `cv2.imshow` in Stage 1/3).
   If `DISPLAY` is missing -> WARN: calibration/capture needs a GUI session.

## 7900 XTX / gfx1100 — Diagnostic Hints (embed in FAIL messages)

- The 7900 XTX is **gfx1100** and officially supported in current ROCm versions —
  `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` should **not** be necessary. Setting an override on a
  supported card can actually cause harm. Mention only as a last-resort fallback
  (e.g. `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0`), do not set it automatically.
- Wrong PyTorch build (CUDA instead of ROCm) is the most common stumbling block:
  recognizable by `+cu` in the version or `torch.version.hip is None`. Remediation hint:
  reinstall the ROCm wheel from the `rocm` index — but **only after consulting**,
  not automatically.
- `torch.cuda.is_available() == False` despite ROCm build: often a driver/permissions
  issue (user not in `render`/`video` group, or `/dev/kfd` & `/dev/dri` not accessible).
  Output as a hint, do not fix it yourself.

## Report Format

Human-readable, one line per check: `[PASS] / [WARN] / [FAIL] <Check> — <Detail>`.
A summary line at the end. With `--json` additionally:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": [
    {"name": "torch.rocm_build", "status": "pass", "detail": "2.4.1+rocm6.2"},
    {"name": "torch.cuda.is_available", "status": "pass", "detail": "true"},
    {"name": "gpu.compute", "status": "pass", "detail": "matmul 2048x2048 ok"},
    {"name": "gpu.name", "status": "pass", "detail": "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX"}
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)

- `chesslab doctor` (without `--gpu`) runs without GPU/camera and checks base deps.
- `chesslab doctor --gpu` prints a separate PASS/WARN/FAIL line for each GPU check,
  including the real matmul compute test, and exits with the correct code.
- If the wrong (CUDA) build is detected, a **clear** FAIL message appears that names
  the build as the cause — no generic stacktrace.
- `chesslab doctor --camera 0` opens the camera and reads a frame, or cleanly reports
  the reason.
- Stage 5 (`train`) internally calls the same GPU validation path and aborts with a
  clear message if the GPU is not usable (instead of silently falling back to CPU).

# Stage 0 — Pre-flight: Environment Validation (`doctor.py`)

## Purpose

The environment is **already set up** per the user (Linux, ROCm, PyTorch-ROCm-build,
AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX). This stage **installs nothing** and changes nothing — it only
**validates** and clearly reports PASS/FAIL with remediation hints. Goal: before
training (Stage 5), ensure the GPU is actually usable instead of assuming it.

> Important for Claude Code: **Do not** run `pip install` / `uv add` of torch. If
> a mandatory check fails, report the finding and consult — do not
> attempt to „fix" ROCm/PyTorch on your own. Pure app dependencies
> (opencv, python-chess, typer, pyyaml) may be installed normally.

## CLI

```
chesslab doctor [--gpu] [--camera 0] [--json]
```

- without flags: base checks (Python, app deps, config paths).
- `--gpu`: additionally runs the full ROCm/PyTorch GPU validation (mandatory before Stage 5).
- `--camera N`: camera check for index N (open + read one frame).
- `--json`: machine-readable report in addition to human-readable output.

Exit code: `0` only if **all requested** mandatory checks pass, otherwise `!= 0`.

## Checks

### A) Base (always)
1. Python `>= 3.11`.
2. Import app deps: `cv2`, `numpy`, `PIL`, `chess`, `typer`, `yaml`. Log versions.
3. Data/config directories exist or are created (`data/...`).

### B) GPU / ROCm (`--gpu`, mandatory before training)
Ordered so diagnostics can narrow down the error:

1. `import torch` succeeds; log `torch.__version__`. **Expected:** contains `+rocm`
   (e.g. `2.x.y+rocm6.2`). If it instead contains `+cu...`, the **wrong
   (CUDA) build** is installed -> FAIL with clear hint.
2. `torch.version.hip is not None` -> confirms ROCm build. (`torch.version.cuda` is
   typically `None` in a ROCm build.) FAIL if `hip` is None.
3. `torch.cuda.is_available()` is `True`. (Under ROCm the `torch.cuda.*` API is
   deliberately reused — this is correct, not NVIDIA.) FAIL otherwise.
4. `torch.cuda.device_count() >= 1`.
5. Log `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)`. **Expected:** contains `7900`, `Radeon` or
   `AMD`. Otherwise WARN (name may be generic depending on driver), not a hard FAIL.
6. Log `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory`. **Expected:** ~24 GB
   (>= 20 GB threshold). Below that WARN.
7. **Real compute test (the decisive one):**
   ```python
   x = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   y = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device="cuda")
   z = (x @ y).sum().item()        # forces sync + transfer back
   torch.cuda.synchronize()
   ```
   If this runs without exception and `z` is finite -> PASS. If it crashes (common with
   gfx mismatch) -> FAIL with hint about gfx target (see below).
8. Optional system check via `subprocess` (not mandatory, info only): run `rocm-smi`
   and/or `rocminfo`, log ROCm version and the agent's `gfx` target. If the
   binary is missing -> WARN, not FAIL (PyTorch checks are authoritative).

### C) Camera (`--camera N`)
1. `cv2.VideoCapture(N)` opens (standard V4L2 backend on Linux).
2. At least one `read()` frame returns a non-empty image; log resolution.
3. Output a hint about whether `DISPLAY` is set (needed for `cv2.imshow` in Stage 1/3).
   If `DISPLAY` is missing -> WARN: calibration/capture needs a GUI session.

## 7900 XTX / gfx1100 — Diagnostic Hints (embed in FAIL messages)

- The 7900 XTX is **gfx1100** and officially supported in current ROCm versions —
  `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` should **not** be necessary. Setting an override on a
  supported card can actually cause harm. Mention only as a last-resort fallback
  (e.g. `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0`), do not set it automatically.
- Wrong PyTorch build (CUDA instead of ROCm) is the most common stumbling block:
  recognizable by `+cu` in the version or `torch.version.hip is None`. Remediation hint:
  reinstall the ROCm wheel from the `rocm` index — but **only after consulting**,
  not automatically.
- `torch.cuda.is_available() == False` despite ROCm build: often a driver/permissions
  issue (user not in `render`/`video` group, or `/dev/kfd` & `/dev/dri` not accessible).
  Output as a hint, do not fix it yourself.

## Report Format

Human-readable, one line per check: `[PASS] / [WARN] / [FAIL] <Check> — <Detail>`.
A summary line at the end. With `--json` additionally:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": [
    {"name": "torch.rocm_build", "status": "pass", "detail": "2.4.1+rocm6.2"},
    {"name": "torch.cuda.is_available", "status": "pass", "detail": "true"},
    {"name": "gpu.compute", "status": "pass", "detail": "matmul 2048x2048 ok"},
    {"name": "gpu.name", "status": "pass", "detail": "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX"}
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)

- `chesslab doctor` (without `--gpu`) runs without GPU/camera and checks base deps.
- `chesslab doctor --gpu` prints a separate PASS/WARN/FAIL line for each GPU check,
  including the real matmul compute test, and exits with the correct code.
- If the wrong (CUDA) build is detected, a **clear** FAIL message appears that names
  the build as the cause — no generic stacktrace.
- `chesslab doctor --camera 0` opens the camera and reads a frame, or cleanly reports
  the reason.
- Stage 5 (`train`) internally calls the same GPU validation path and aborts with a
  clear message if the GPU is not usable (instead of silently falling back to CPU).

# Stufe 5 — Training-Handoff (`training/`)

## Zweck

Ein Per-Square-Klassifikationsmodell (13 Klassen) auf dem Datensatz trainieren,
aussagekräftig evaluieren und exportieren — lauffähig auf der **AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
über ROCm**. Das Modell ist das eigentliche Liefer-Artefakt für die spätere Inferenz-App.

## GPU-Vorbedingung (ROCm)

- **Vor jedem Training** den GPU-Validierungspfad aus Stufe 0 aufrufen
  (`doctor --gpu`-Logik). Ist die GPU nicht nutzbar -> **abbrechen mit klarer Meldung**,
  **nicht** still auf CPU zurückfallen.
- Geräte-Handle über die normale `torch.cuda`-API beziehen (`device = "cuda"`). Unter dem
  ROCm-Build ist das korrekt und adressiert die Radeon-GPU.
- AMP/`torch.autocast` mit `device_type="cuda"` ist auf RDNA3 nutzbar; falls Instabilität
  auftritt, per Flag `--no-amp` abschaltbar machen. `channels_last` kann helfen, optional.
- 24 GB VRAM sind reichlich für ein kleines CNN bei 96x128-Crops -> großzügige Batchsize
  möglich (Default z. B. 256, per `--batch-size` anpassbar).

## Modell (`training/model.py`)

Zwei wählbare Backbones, gleicher 13-Klassen-Kopf:

1. **`smallcnn` (Default):** kompaktes Conv-Netz (z. B. 4–5 Conv-Blöcke mit BatchNorm +
   ReLU, GlobalAvgPool, Linear -> 13). Schnell, reicht für die Aufgabe meist völlig.
2. **`mobilenet_v3_small`:** torchvision-Backbone, Kopf auf 13 Klassen ersetzt.
   Optional ImageNet-Gewichte als Start (Fine-Tuning).

Input: `out_size` aus dem Datensatz (z. B. 96x128, H>W). Normalisierung dokumentieren und
**identisch** für Train/Eval/Export verwenden (die Inferenz-App muss sie spiegeln).

## Daten (`training/data.py`)

- Liest `data/manifests/squares.jsonl` + `data/manifests/split.json`, filtert Crops nach
  Session-Zugehörigkeit des jeweiligen Splits.
- Augmentation **nur auf train**, gemäß Policy aus Stufe 4 (Helligkeit/Kontrast/Gamma,
  leichter Blur, kleines Jitter; **kein** Flip/Rotation). Val/Test nur Resize+Normalize.
- Klassen-Gewichte aus `split.json` an den Loss weiterreichen; alternativ `WeightedRandomSampler`.
- `num_workers` sinnvoll setzen; `pin_memory=True`.

## Training (`training/train.py`)

### CLI
```
chesslab train [--backbone smallcnn] [--epochs 30] [--batch-size 256] [--lr 3e-4]
               [--no-amp] [--seed 42] [--out data/models/run-<ts>]
```

### Loop
- Optimizer AdamW, Cross-Entropy mit Klassen-Gewichten, Cosine- oder Step-LR-Schedule.
- Pro Epoche: Train-Loss, Val-Loss, Val-Accuracy, **Val-Board-Accuracy** (s. u.) loggen.
- Checkpoint nach bester **Board-Accuracy** speichern (nicht nach Square-Accuracy — die
  ist durch `empty` aufgebläht und irreführend).
- Early Stopping (Geduld konfigurierbar). Run-Verzeichnis enthält: `best.pt`, `last.pt`,
  `metrics.jsonl`, `config.json` (alle Hyperparameter + Klassenliste + Normalisierung).

## Evaluation (`training/evaluate.py`)

### CLI
```
chesslab eval --run data/models/run-<ts> [--split test]
```

Metriken — in dieser Reihenfolge, weil sie unterschiedlich aussagekräftig sind:

1. **Board-Accuracy (Hauptmetrik):** Anteil der Frames, deren **alle 64 Felder** korrekt
   klassifiziert wurden. Das ist die Zahl, die im Echtbetrieb zählt — ein einzelner
   Fehler macht die FEN falsch. Dazu Crops je Frame (über `session_id`+`frame`+`square`
   aus dem Manifest) rekonstruieren.
2. **Per-Klassen-Accuracy / Recall** für alle 13 Klassen.
3. **Confusion-Matrix**, mit besonderem Blick auf **König↔Dame** und Figur↔`empty`
   (häufigste Verwechslungen). Als Text und als PNG speichern.
4. Square-Accuracy gesamt (nur als Kontext, nicht als Zielmetrik).

## Export (`training/` / `chesslab export`)

```
chesslab export --run data/models/run-<ts> [--format torchscript|onnx]
```
- Exportiert `best.pt` nach **TorchScript** und/oder **ONNX**.
- Legt eine `model_card.json` daneben: Klassenliste (geordnet), Input-`out_size`,
  Normalisierungs-Parameter, Trainings-Metriken, ROCm/Torch-Version, Datum.
- Diese Artefakte sind der saubere Übergabepunkt an die Inferenz-App.

## Akzeptanzkriterien (Definition of Done)

- `train` bricht ohne nutzbare ROCm-GPU klar ab (kein stiller CPU-Fallback) und trainiert
  sonst auf der 7900 XTX (VRAM-Nutzung sichtbar, z. B. via `rocm-smi`).
- `metrics.jsonl` enthält je Epoche Board-Accuracy; bestes Checkpoint danach ausgewählt.
- `eval` gibt Board-Accuracy, Per-Klassen-Recall und eine Confusion-Matrix (Text+PNG) aus.
- `export` erzeugt ladbares TorchScript/ONNX + `model_card.json` mit korrekter
  Klassenliste und Normalisierung.
- Ein Smoke-Run (1–2 Epochen auf wenigen Sessions) läuft end-to-end ohne Fehler durch.

---

## Hinweis: Folgeprojekt Inferenz-App (NICHT in diesem Repo)

Das hier exportierte Modell + `model_card.json` werden von einer separaten Live-App
konsumiert. Deren Kernbausteine (zur Orientierung, hier bewusst ausgelassen):

- Echtzeit-Webcam -> dieselbe Homographie/Crops -> Modell -> 64 Labels -> FEN.
- **Temporale Stabilität:** Stellung erst übernehmen, wenn N aufeinanderfolgende Frames
  übereinstimmen (filtert Hände überm Brett / Jitter).
- **Legalitäts-Fusion:** neue Stellung gegen die legalen Folgezüge der vorherigen prüfen;
  inkonsistente Erkennungen verwerfen/korrigieren. Macht aus „gutem Klassifikator"
  verlässliches Partie-Logging.
- **PGN-/Verlauf-Export** + optionale Stockfish-Analyse für die gemeinsame Nachbesprechung.

Beim Bau dieses Repos darauf achten, dass Homographie-Anwendung, Crop-Logik und
Normalisierung als wiederverwendbare Funktionen vorliegen, damit die App sie 1:1
übernehmen kann.

# Stage 5 — Training Handoff (`training/`)

## Purpose

Train a per-square classification model (13 classes) on the dataset,
evaluate it meaningfully and export it — runnable on the **AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
via ROCm**. The model is the actual deliverable artifact for the downstream inference app.

## GPU Prerequisite (ROCm)

- **Before every training run** invoke the GPU validation path from Stage 0
  (`doctor --gpu` logic). If the GPU is not usable -> **abort with a clear message**,
  **do not** silently fall back to CPU.
- Obtain the device handle via the normal `torch.cuda` API (`device = "cuda"`). Under the
  ROCm build this is correct and addresses the Radeon GPU.
- AMP/`torch.autocast` with `device_type="cuda"` is usable on RDNA3; if instability
  occurs, make it switchable via the `--no-amp` flag. `channels_last` can help, optional.
- 24 GB VRAM is plentiful for a small CNN with 96x128 crops -> generous batch sizes
  possible (default e.g. 256, adjustable via `--batch-size`).

## Model (`training/model.py`)

Two selectable backbones, same 13-class head:

1. **`smallcnn` (Default):** compact Conv net (e.g. 4–5 Conv blocks with BatchNorm +
   ReLU, GlobalAvgPool, Linear -> 13). Fast, usually sufficient for the task.
2. **`mobilenet_v3_small`:** torchvision backbone, head replaced for 13 classes.
   Optional ImageNet weights as starting point (fine-tuning).

Input: `out_size` from the dataset (e.g. 96x128, H>W). Document normalization and use
it **identically** for train/eval/export (the inference app must mirror it).

## Data (`training/data.py`)

- Reads `data/manifests/squares.jsonl` + `data/manifests/split.json`, filters crops by
  session membership of the respective split.
- Augmentation **on train only**, according to the policy from Stage 4 (brightness/contrast/gamma,
  light blur, small jitter; **no** flip/rotation). Val/Test only Resize+Normalize.
- Pass class weights from `split.json` to the loss; alternatively `WeightedRandomSampler`.
- Set `num_workers` sensibly; `pin_memory=True`.

## Training (`training/train.py`)

### CLI
```
chesslab train [--backbone smallcnn] [--epochs 30] [--batch-size 256] [--lr 3e-4]
               [--no-amp] [--seed 42] [--out data/models/run-<ts>]
```

### Loop
- Optimizer AdamW, Cross-Entropy with class weights, Cosine or Step LR schedule.
- Per epoch: log Train-Loss, Val-Loss, Val-Accuracy, **Val-Board-Accuracy** (see below).
- Save checkpoint based on best **Board-Accuracy** (not Square-Accuracy — it
  is inflated by `empty` and misleading).
- Early Stopping (configurable patience). Run directory contains: `best.pt`, `last.pt`,
  `metrics.jsonl`, `config.json` (all hyperparameters + class list + normalization).

## Evaluation (`training/evaluate.py`)

### CLI
```
chesslab eval --run data/models/run-<ts> [--split test]
```

Metrics — in this order, because they have different significance:

1. **Board-Accuracy (primary metric):** proportion of frames where **all 64 squares** were
   classified correctly. This is the number that counts in real operation — a single
   error makes the FEN wrong. Reconstruct crops per frame (via `session_id`+`frame`+`square`
   from the manifest).
2. **Per-class accuracy / recall** for all 13 classes.
3. **Confusion matrix**, with special attention to **King↔Queen** and piece↔`empty`
   (most common confusions). Save as text and as PNG.
4. Overall Square-Accuracy (for context only, not as target metric).

## Export (`training/` / `chesslab export`)

```
chesslab export --run data/models/run-<ts> [--format torchscript|onnx]
```
- Exports `best.pt` to **TorchScript** and/or **ONNX**.
- Places a `model_card.json` alongside: class list (ordered), input `out_size`,
  normalization parameters, training metrics, ROCm/Torch version, date.
- These artifacts are the clean handoff point to the inference app.

## Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)

- `train` aborts clearly without a usable ROCm GPU (no silent CPU fallback) and otherwise
  trains on the 7900 XTX (VRAM usage visible, e.g. via `rocm-smi`).
- `metrics.jsonl` contains Board-Accuracy per epoch; best checkpoint selected accordingly.
- `eval` outputs Board-Accuracy, per-class recall, and a confusion matrix (text + PNG).
- `export` produces loadable TorchScript/ONNX + `model_card.json` with correct
  class list and normalization.
- A smoke run (1–2 epochs on a few sessions) runs end-to-end without errors.

---

## Note: Downstream Inference App (NOT in this repo)

The model exported here + `model_card.json` are consumed by a separate live app.
Its core building blocks (for orientation, intentionally omitted here):

- Real-time webcam -> same homography/crops -> model -> 64 labels -> FEN.
- **Temporal stability:** only adopt a position when N consecutive frames
  agree (filters hands over board / jitter).
- **Legality fusion:** check new position against legal follow-up moves of the previous one;
  discard/correct inconsistent detections. Turns a "good classifier" into
  reliable game logging.
- **PGN / history export** + optional Stockfish analysis for joint post-mortem.

When building this repo, ensure that homography application, crop logic, and
normalization are provided as reusable functions so that the app can adopt them 1:1.

# Synthetische Daten-Pipeline

Vollständige Pipeline vom 3D-Scan zur gelabelten Trainingsdaten-Quelle:
Turntable-Fotos → RealityScan → Isolierung → Render → Ingest → Training.

## Asset-Erwartungen

- **Blender-Szene:** `synth_assets/Chess Scene.blend` (Brett, Kamera, Beleuchtung)
- **Figuren-Vorlagen:** `synth_pieces/<X>.obj` + `<X>.png` (Textur)
  - Namensschema: `wP.obj`/`wP.png` (weißer Bauer), `bN.obj`/`bN.png` (schwarzer Springer),
    oder `P.obj`/`P.png` (farblos, wird dann für beide Farben verwendet).
  - Figuren ohne Scan fallen auf prozedurale Staunton-Vorlagen aus der .blend zurück.

## Ecken-Reihenfolge (VERTRAG — NICHT ÄNDERN)

Das JSON je Rendering enthält `corners: [a8, h8, h1, a1]` in **dieser Reihenfolge**.
Eine abweichende Reihenfolge vertauscht alle Labels stillschweigend (Spiegelung/Rotation).
Wächter-Test: `tests/test_ingest_synthetic.py::test_synthetic_ingest_orientation`.

## 1. Turntable-Aufnahme

```bash
python synth/capture_turntable.py --piece P --out data/turntable/P/
```

**Anti-Flicker-Hinweis:** Raumlicht dimmen, Bildstabilisierung der Kamera deaktivieren,
Weißabgleich und Belichtung fixieren (kein Automatik-Modus). Kamera auf Stativ.

## 2. RealityScan (Cloud)

Fotos hochladen → Mesh + Textur herunterladen. Ausgabe ist eine `.obj` + `.png`/`.jpg`.

## 3. Vorbereiten (isolieren + dezimieren + Qualitäts-Report) — `chesslab synth prepare`

**Empfohlener Weg — Blender muss nie geöffnet werden.** Scans nach `<in>/<Figur>/` legen
(Figurenname = Ordnername: `P`, `wN`, …; darin die RealityScan-Ausgabe — bevorzugt das rohe
`.obj` + `*_diffuse.png`; `.glb` geht auch, referenziert seine Textur aber meist extern,
also die diffuse-PNG mit in den Ordner):

```bash
uv run chesslab synth prepare --in scans_export/ --out synth_pieces/
```

Je Figur passiert automatisch (alle Schritte als Toggles):
- **Isolieren:** Unterlage per PCA finden, Figur-Cluster behalten (`--keep-radius`, Default 1.9),
  aufrecht stellen (Basis z=0, Achse +Z).
- **Aufräumen:** nur größte zusammenhängende Komponente (`--no-keep-largest` schaltet ab),

```bash

```bash

```

- `--pieces-dir` — Piece templates (default: `synth_pieces/`)
- `--n` — Number of renderings (default: 200)
- `--seed` — Seed (default: 42)
- `--fens` — FEN list (otherwise fallback to starting position)

```bash

    --python synth/render_chessboard.py \

       --fens data/synth_fens.txt --pieces synth_pieces

```bash

```

```bash

```
The overlay PNGs show the rectified crop + FEN label — verify that the pieces land on the
correct squares.

## 7. Training

```bash
uv run chesslab train --dataset synth --head twostage --backbone mobilenet_v3_small
```

Or pretrain → finetune with the synth dataset as the first curriculum stage.

     4│ **sessionbasierter** Split (gegen Data Leakage) und eine Augmentation-Policy. Die reinen
     5│ Funktionen sind headless getestet; die CLI-Wrapper lösen Pfade aus `config`.
     6│ """
     7│ 
     8│ from __future__ import annotations
     9│ 
    10│ import json
    11│ import random
    12│ from collections import Counter
    13│ from pathlib import Path
    14│

    17│ CLASSES = config.CLASSES
    18│ 
    19│ 
    20│ # --- Manifest laden -------------------------------------------------------------------
    21│ 
    22│ def load_manifest(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    23│     from .ioutil import read_jsonl
    24│ 
    25│     path = Path(path)
    26│     if not path.exists():
    27│         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Manifest nicht gefunden: {path}. Erst `chesslab slice` ausführen.")
    28│     return read_jsonl(path)
    29│ 
    30│ 
    31│ # --- stats ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32│ 
    33│ def compute_stats(rows: list[dict], min_samples: int = config.MIN_CLASS_SAMPLES) -> dict:
    34│     counts = dict.fromkeys(CLASSES, 0)
    35│     light = dict.fromkeys(CLASSES, 0)
    36│     dark = dict.fromkeys(CLASSES, 0)
    37│     per_session: Counter = Counter()
    38│ 
    39│     for r in rows:
    40│         lab = r["label"]
    41│         counts[lab] = counts.get(lab, 0) + 1
    42│         if r.get("square_color") == "light":
    43│             light[lab] += 1
    44│         else:
    45│             dark[lab] += 1
    46│         per_session[r["session_id"]] += 1
    47│ 
    48│     warnings: list[str] = []
    49│     for c in CLASSES:
    50│         if c in config.OPTIONAL_CLASSES:    # empty/occluded dürfen fehlen (nicht aus FEN)
    51│             continue
    52│         n = counts[c]
    53│         if n == 0:
    54│             warnings.append(f"Klasse {c}: 0 Beispiele.")
    55│         elif n < min_samples:
    56│             warnings.append(f"Klasse {c}: nur {n} (< {min_samples}).")
    57│         if n > 0 and (light[c] == 0 or dark[c] == 0):
    58│             only = "dunkel" if light[c] == 0 else "hell"
    59│             warnings.append(f"Klasse {c}: nur auf {only}en Feldern vorhanden.")
    60│ 
    61│     return {
    62│         "total": len(rows),
    63│         "num_sessions": len(per_session),
    64│         "per_session": dict(per_session),
    65│         "counts": counts,
    66│         "light": light,
    67│         "dark": dark,
    68│         "warnings": warnings,
    69│     }
    70│ 
    71│ 
    72│ def render_stats(stats: dict) -> str:
    73│     lines = [
    74│         f"Crops gesamt: {stats['total']}  |  Sessions: {stats['num_sessions']}",
    75│         f"{'Klasse':<7}{'count':>8}{'hell':>8}{'dunkel':>8}",
    76│     ]
    77│     for c in CLASSES:
    78│         lines.append(f"{c:<7}{stats['counts'][c]:>8}{stats['light'][c]:>8}{stats['dark'][c]:>8}")
    79│     if stats["warnings"]:
    80│         lines.append("Warnungen:")
    81│         lines.extend(f"  ! {w}" for w in stats["warnings"])
    82│     else:
    83│         lines.append("Keine Warnungen.")
    84│     return "\n".join(lines)
    85│ 
    86│ 
    87│ # --- Klassenbalance -------------------------------------------------------------------
    88│ 
    89│ def subsample_classes(rows: list[dict], max_empty_ratio: float | None = None,
    90│                       max_class_ratio: float | None = None, seed: int = config.SEED) -> list[dict]:
    91│     """Überrepräsentierte Klassen seeded herunterregeln, um die Verteilung auszugleichen.
    92│ 
    93│     - `max_class_ratio R`: jede **Figuren**klasse auf höchstens R * kleinste Figurenklasse
    94│       begrenzen (regelt z.B. die Bauern zu den seltenen Figuren herunter).
    95│     - `max_empty_ratio R`: `empty` auf R * größte (gedeckelte) Figurenklasse begrenzen.
    96│     Reihenfolge: erst Figuren deckeln, dann `empty` relativ zur neuen größten Figurenklasse.
    97│     """
    98│     rng = random.Random(seed)
    99│     by_label: dict[str, list] = {}
   100│     for r in rows:
   101│         by_label.setdefault(r["label"], []).append(r)
   102│ 
   103│     piece_counts = {c: len(v) for c, v in by_label.items() if c != "empty"}
   104│     piece_cap = None
   105│     if max_class_ratio is not None and piece_counts:
   106│         piece_cap = int(round(max_class_ratio * min(piece_counts.values())))
   107│ 
   108│     kept: list[dict] = []
   109│     eff_piece: dict[str, int] = {}
   110│     for c, v in by_label.items():
   111│         if c == "empty":
   112│             continue
   113│         if piece_cap is not None and len(v) > piece_cap:
   114│             v = rng.sample(v, piece_cap)
   115│         eff_piece[c] = len(v)
   116│         kept.extend(v)
   117│ 
   118│     empties = by_label.get("empty", [])
   119│     if max_empty_ratio is not None and eff_piece:
   120│         empty_cap = int(round(max_empty_ratio * max(eff_piece.values())))
   121│         if len(empties) > empty_cap:
   122│             empties = rng.sample(empties, empty_cap)
   123│     kept.extend(empties)
   124│     return kept
   125│ 
   126│ 
   127│ def subsample_empty(rows: list[dict], max_empty_ratio: float | None, seed: int) -> list[dict]:

   129│     return subsample_classes(rows, max_empty_ratio=max_empty_ratio, max_class_ratio=None, seed=seed)

   132│ def compute_class_weights(counts: dict) -> dict:
   133│     """Invers zur Häufigkeit. Größte Klasse -> kleinstes Gewicht. Absente Klassen -> 0.0."""
   134│     present = {c: n for c, n in counts.items() if n > 0}
   135│     weights = dict.fromkeys(CLASSES, 0.0)
   136│     if not present:

   139│     k = len(present)

when crop parameters change — without re-recording.

so that Stage 1/3 and the later inference app crop identically.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import cv2

from . import config, geometry3d, photometric
from .calibration import (
    CalibrationProfile,
    board_corners_for_frame,
    crop_border_px,
    load_profile,
    make_tracker,
    square_to_crop_box,
    warp_board_for_crops,
)
from .imgops import resize_keep_aspect
from .state import GameState

_FILES = "abcdefgh"



def _profile_for_session(meta: dict, profile: str | None):
    """Resolve the calibration profile for a session; reconstruct for legacy ingests.

    Older `chesslab ingest` runs built their placeholder profile only in memory and
    never saved it — re-slicing such a session would fail. The warp uses the per-frame
    `corners` from the log anyway, so a reconstructed placeholder is equivalent up to
    the rectified resolution (ingest default board_size=900)."""
    name = profile or meta["profile"]
    try:
        return load_profile(name)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        if meta.get("mode") != "ingested":
            raise
        from .ingest import ingestion_profile

        print(f"[WARN] profile '{name}' missing — reconstructing the ingest placeholder "
              "profile (board_size=900; warp uses per-frame corners).")
        return ingestion_profile(name, board_size=900)

def label_to_fen_char(label: str) -> str | None:
    """Class label -> FEN piece letter ('wP'->'P', 'bN'->'n'); empty/occluded/empty -> None."""
    if not label or label in ("empty", "occluded") or len(label) != 2:
        return None
    return label[1].upper() if label[0] == "w" else label[1].lower()


def labels_to_fen(labels: dict) -> str:
    """64 Per-Square Labels -> FEN Position Part (occluded counts as empty).

    Counterpart to ``config.label_from_piece`` (Piece → Label); here Label → FEN string.
    """
    rows = []
    for rank in range(8, 0, -1):
        run_empty, row = 0, ""
        for f in "abcdefgh":
            ch = label_to_fen_char(labels.get(f"{f}{rank}", "empty"))
            if ch is None:
                run_empty += 1
            else:
                if run_empty:
                    row += str(run_empty); run_empty = 0
                row += ch
        if run_empty:
            row += str(run_empty)
        rows.append(row)
    return "/".join(rows)


def parse_out_size(s: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """'96x128' -> (96, 128) = (W, H)."""
    try:
        w, h = s.lower().split("x")
        return int(w), int(h)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise ValueError(f"invalid out-size {s!r}, expected WxH (e.g. 96x128).") from e


def square_color(square: str) -> str:
    """Deterministic square color: a1=dark. (file_idx + rank_idx) % 2."""
    sq = square.strip().lower()
    file_idx = _FILES.index(sq[0])
    rank_idx = int(sq[1]) - 1
    return "dark" if (file_idx + rank_idx) % 2 == 0 else "light"


def all_squares() -> list[str]:
    return [f"{f}{r}" for r in range(1, 9) for f in _FILES]


# Transition alias: `resize_keep_aspect` now lives in `imgops` (resolves the
# import cycle with `geometry3d`). No longer referenced by anyone; can be
# removed in the next cleanup pass.
_resize_keep_aspect = resize_keep_aspect


def crop_square(board_warped, square: str, profile: CalibrationProfile, out_size: tuple[int, int]):
    """Extract one square-crop from the **bordered** board (`warp_board_for_crops`).

    `square_to_crop_box` returns the box in board coordinates [0, board_size]; since the data warp
    is offset by `B = crop_border_px(profile)`, the box is shifted by +B into the canvas.
    This ensures edge squares have actual content for their pad_side/pad_up extension. Overhang is
    filled with black (constant geometry across all 64 squares), then scaled losslessly to out_size.
    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = square_to_crop_box(square, profile, clamp=False)
    b = crop_border_px(profile)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = x0 + b, y0 + b, x1 + b, y1 + b
    if x1 <= x0:
        x1 = x0 + 1
    if y1 <= y0:
        y1 = y0 + 1
    H, W = board_warped.shape[:2]
    xa, ya, xb, yb = max(0, x0), max(0, y0), min(W, x1), min(H, y1)
    region = board_warped[ya:yb, xa:xb]
    pad_t, pad_b, pad_l, pad_r = ya - y0, y1 - yb, xa - x0, x1 - xb
    if pad_t or pad_b or pad_l or pad_r:       # fill overhanging areas with black
        region = cv2.copyMakeBorder(region, pad_t, pad_b, pad_l, pad_r,
                                    cv2.BORDER_CONSTANT, value=(0, 0, 0))
    return resize_keep_aspect(region, out_size)


def crops_for_frame(frame, corners, profile: CalibrationProfile, *, geometry: str = "warp",
                    photometry: str = "none",
                    piece_height_cells: float = config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS,
                    out_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
                    with_meta: bool = False):
    """64 Crops (order `all_squares()`) for ONE frame — IDENTICAL to the training slice:
    bordered warp OR box3d, then `preprocess_crop`. Single Source for live inference so
    the model sees exactly the same crop live as during training.

    `with_meta=True`: returns (crops, meta) where meta = {"used_box3d": list[bool]} indicates per square
    whether the crop was produced via box3d (True) or warp (False). Used by `slice_session`
    for the `pose_ok` flag in the manifest (de-duplication, Rework 01).
    """
    out = tuple(out_size) if out_size else tuple(profile.crop.out_size)
    box3d = geometry == "box3d"
    cell = profile.board_size / 8.0
    pose = None
    up = 1.0
    K = dist = None
    if box3d:
        fh, fw = frame.shape[:2]
        K, dist = geometry3d.intrinsics(profile, (fw, fh))
        pose = geometry3d.estimate_pose(corners, K, dist, profile.board_size, profile.margin)
        if pose is not None:
            up = geometry3d.up_sign(pose[0], pose[1])
    ph_units = float(piece_height_cells) * cell
    ps_units = config.EXP_BOX3D_PAD_SIDE_CELLS * cell
    warped = warp_board_for_crops(frame, profile, corners)   # warp-Crop + box3d-Fallback
    crops = []
    used_box3d = []
    for square in all_squares():
        crop = None
        is_box3d = False
        if box3d and pose is not None:
            crop = geometry3d.crop_square_3d(frame, square, K, dist, pose[0], pose[1], profile,
                                             piece_height_units=ph_units, pad_side_units=ps_units,
                                             up=up, out_size=out)
            is_box3d = crop is not None
        if crop is None:
            crop = crop_square(warped, square, profile, out)
        if photometry != "none":
            crop = photometric.preprocess_crop(crop, photometry)
        crops.append(crop)
        used_box3d.append(is_box3d)
    return (crops, {"used_box3d": used_box3d}) if with_meta else crops


def variant_of_run(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[str, str, float]:
    """(geometry, photometry, piece_height_cells) of a model run — from its dataset manifest
    (the crops carry their preprocessing tags). This tells live inference how to crop.
    Default (warp, none) for untagged legacy manifests."""
    cfg_p = run_dir / "config.json"
    cfg = json.loads(cfg_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if cfg_p.exists() else {}
    ds = cfg.get("dataset")
    if ds:
        from .dataset_build import dataset_dir
        man = dataset_dir(ds) / "manifest.jsonl"
    else:
        man = config.DATA.manifests / "squares.jsonl"
    if man.exists():
        for line in man.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                r = json.loads(line)
                return (r.get("geometry", "warp"), r.get("photometry", "none"),
                        float(r.get("piece_height_cells", config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS)))
    return ("warp", "none", config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS)


def read_session_meta(session_dir: Path) -> dict:
    import yaml

    p = session_dir / "session.yaml"
    if not p.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"session.yaml missing in {session_dir}")
    with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return yaml.safe_load(fh)


def read_log(session_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
    from .ioutil import read_jsonl

    p = session_dir / "log.jsonl"
    if not p.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"log.jsonl missing in {session_dir}")
    return read_jsonl(p)


def _effective_profile(profile: CalibrationProfile, pad_up, pad_side) -> CalibrationProfile:
    prof = copy.deepcopy(profile)
    if pad_up is not None:
        prof.crop.pad_up = float(pad_up)
    if pad_side is not None:
        prof.crop.pad_side = float(pad_side)
    return prof


def _replace_session_in_manifest(manifest_path: Path, session_id: str, new_lines: list[str]) -> None:
    """Remove previous lines of this session, then append new ones (idempotent re-slice)."""
    kept: list[str] = []
    if manifest_path.exists():
        for line in manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            if json.loads(line).get("session_id") != session_id:
                kept.append(line)
    manifest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with manifest_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for ln in kept + new_lines:
            fh.write(ln + "\n")


def load_corrections(path: Path) -> dict[tuple[str, str, str], str]:
    """Load human label corrections: {(session_id, frame, square): label}. Last wins."""
    out: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        return out
    for line in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        c = json.loads(line)
        out[(c["session_id"], str(c["frame"]), c["square"])] = c["label"]
    return out


def upsert_corrections(items: list[dict], path: Path) -> int:
    """Merge corrections (session_id, frame, square, label) and rewrite. Returns total count."""
    merged = load_corrections(path)
    for it in items:
        merged[(it["session_id"], str(it["frame"]), it["square"])] = it["label"]
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for (sid, frame, square), label in merged.items():
            fh.write(json.dumps({"session_id": sid, "frame": frame, "square": square,
                                 "label": label, "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()},
                                ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return len(merged)


def slice_session(
    session_dir: Path,
    *,
    profile: CalibrationProfile,
    manifest_path: Path,
    squares_root: Path,
    pad_up: float | None = None,
    pad_side: float | None = None,
    out_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    label_overrides: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] | None = None,
    geometry_mode: str = "warp",
    photometry: str = "none",
    piece_height_cells: float = config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS,
) -> dict:
    """Slice one session: 64 crops per logged position + manifest lines. Pure I/O.

    `label_overrides` replaces the FEN-derived label per (session, frame, square) with
    a human correction (web relabel). Returns the number of applied overrides.

    `geometry_mode`: "warp" (top-down crop, baseline) or "box3d" (3D box from the original frame
    via per-frame pose). `photometry`: deterministic filter (none/clahe/grayworld/gamma), baked
    INTO the PNGs (train/inference parity). `piece_height_cells`: extrusion height for box3d.
    """
    session_dir = Path(session_dir)
    meta = read_session_meta(session_dir)
    session_id = meta["session_id"]
    log = read_log(session_dir)

    prof = _effective_profile(profile, pad_up, pad_side)
    out = tuple(out_size) if out_size else tuple(prof.crop.out_size)
    box3d = geometry_mode == "box3d"

    new_lines: list[str] = []
    n_crops = 0
    n_overrides = 0
    n_skipped = 0
    n_fallback = 0   # box3d: squares that fell back to warp (pose/projection failed)
    tracker = make_tracker(prof)   # per session: seeded from profile, markers held per frame
    for entry in log:
        frame_path = session_dir / entry["frame"]
        frame = cv2.imread(str(frame_path))
        if frame is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Frame not readable: {frame_path}")
        corners = entry.get("corners")
        if not corners:
            # Fallback (sessions without saved corners): per frame from the markers.
            corners = board_corners_for_frame(frame, prof, tracker)
            if corners is None:
                n_skipped += 1   # no markers in frame -> not usable, skip
                continue

        # crops_for_frame as single source (Rework 01: de-duplication).
        crops, meta = crops_for_frame(
            frame, corners, prof, geometry=geometry_mode, photometry=photometry,
            piece_height_cells=piece_height_cells, out_size=out, with_meta=True)
        used_box3d_list = meta["used_box3d"]
        if box3d:
            n_fallback += sum(1 for v in used_box3d_list if not v)

        explicit = entry.get("labels")          # Inference/Active-Learning: explicit 64 labels
        gs = None if explicit else GameState(entry["fen"])
        frame_stem = Path(entry["frame"]).stem  # '0007'
        squares = all_squares()
        for i, square in enumerate(squares):
            label = explicit.get(square, "empty") if explicit else gs.label_for(square)
            if label_overrides:
                corrected = label_overrides.get((session_id, frame_stem, square))
                if corrected is not None and corrected != label:
                    label = corrected
                    n_overrides += 1
            crop = crops[i]
            out_dir = squares_root / label
            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fname = f"{session_id}_{frame_stem}_{square}.png"
            cv2.imwrite(str(out_dir / fname), crop)
            row = {
                "path": str((out_dir / fname).as_posix()),
                "label": label,
                "session_id": session_id,
                "frame": frame_stem,
                "ply": entry.get("ply"),
                "square": square,
                "square_color": square_color(square),
                "fen": entry["fen"],
                "out_size": [out[0], out[1]],
                "geometry": geometry_mode,
                "photometry": photometry,
                "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
            }
            if box3d:
                row["piece_height_cells"] = float(piece_height_cells)
                row["pose_ok"] = used_box3d_list[i]
            new_lines.append(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False))
            n_crops += 1

    _replace_session_in_manifest(manifest_path, session_id, new_lines)
    return {"session_id": session_id, "frames": len(log), "crops": n_crops,
            "overrides": n_overrides, "skipped": n_skipped, "fallback": n_fallback}


# --- CLI layer (resolves defaults from config) ---------------------------------------------

def _session_ids_with_logs() -> list[str]:
    root = config.DATA.sessions
    if not root.exists():
        return []
    return sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir() if (p / "log.jsonl").exists())


def variant_paths(variant_tag: str | None) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    """(manifest_path, squares_root) for a variant. `None` = current default paths; otherwise
    `data/manifests/squares__<tag>.jsonl` + `data/squares__<tag>/`, so variants coexist."""
    if not variant_tag:
        return config.DATA.manifests / "squares.jsonl", config.DATA.squares
    suffix = f"__{variant_tag}"
    return config.DATA.manifests / f"squares{suffix}.jsonl", config.DATA.root / f"squares{suffix}"


def run_slice(
    session: str | None = None,
    slice_all: bool = False,
    profile: str | None = None,
    pad_up: float | None = None,
    pad_side: float | None = None,
    out_size: str | None = None,
    preview: str | None = None,
    geometry_mode: str = "warp",
    photometry: str = "none",
    piece_height_cells: float = config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS,
    variant_tag: str | None = None,
) -> int:
    out_size_t = parse_out_size(out_size) if out_size else None

    if preview:
        return _preview_session(preview, profile)

    if slice_all:
        sids = _session_ids_with_logs()
    elif session:
        sids = [session]
    else:
        print("[FAIL] specify --session <id> or --all.")
        return 1
    if not sids:
        print("No sessions with log.jsonl found.")
        return 0

    manifest_path, squares_root = variant_paths(variant_tag)
    corrections = load_corrections(config.DATA.corrections)  # apply human relabels
    rc = 0
    for sid in sids:
        session_dir = config.DATA.sessions / sid
        try:
            meta = read_session_meta(session_dir)
            prof = _profile_for_session(meta, profile)
            stats = slice_session(
                session_dir, profile=prof, manifest_path=manifest_path, squares_root=squares_root,
                pad_up=pad_up, pad_side=pad_side, out_size=out_size_t, label_overrides=corrections,
                geometry_mode=geometry_mode, photometry=photometry, piece_height_cells=piece_height_cells,
            )
            extra = f" ({stats['overrides']} corrections)" if stats.get("overrides") else ""
            if stats.get("skipped"):
                extra += f" [{stats['skipped']} frames without markers skipped]"
            if stats.get("fallback"):
                extra += f" [{stats['fallback']} box3d->warp fallbacks]"
            print(f"[OK] {sid}: {stats['frames']} Frames -> {stats['crops']} Crops{extra}.")
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"[FAIL] {sid}: {e}")
            rc = 1
    return rc


def _preview_session(session_id: str, profile: str | None) -> int:
    """Debug: slice the first position and show label vs. visible crop side by side."""
    session_dir = config.DATA.sessions / session_id
    try:
        meta = read_session_meta(session_dir)
        prof = _profile_for_session(meta, profile)
        log = read_log(session_dir)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"[FAIL] {e}")
        return 1
    if not log:
        print("[FAIL] empty log.")
        return 1
    frame = cv2.imread(str(session_dir / log[0]["frame"]))
    corners = log[0].get("corners") or board_corners_for_frame(frame, prof, make_tracker(prof))
    if corners is None:
        print("[FAIL] no markers detected in the frame.")
        return 1
    warped = warp_board_for_crops(frame, prof, corners)   # same bordered crop path as slice
    gs = GameState(log[0]["fen"])
    out = tuple(prof.crop.out_size)
    cols = []
    import numpy as np

    for square in ("a8", "e1", "d8", "h1"):
        crop = crop_square(warped, square, prof, out)
        canvas = np.zeros((out[1] + 24, out[0], 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        canvas[:out[1]] = crop
        cv2.putText(canvas, f"{square}:{gs.label_for(square)}", (2, out[1] + 16),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.45, (0, 255, 0), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cols.append(canvas)
    cv2.imshow("chesslab slice --preview (q closes)", np.hstack(cols))
    while (cv2.waitKey(20) & 0xFF) != ord("q"):
        pass
    cv2.destroyAllWindows()
    return 0

   469│ class MarkerTracker:

   471│ 
   472│     Eigenschaften (Parameter aus `config.TRACKER`):

   474│     - **Glättung**: echte Bewegung -> EMA mit `smooth_alpha` statt hartem Schnappen.
   475│     - **Ausreißer / Selbstkorrektur**: ein Einzel-Frame-Sprung > `jump_reject_px` wird zunächst
   476│       gehalten; erst wenn die neue Lage über `jump_confirm_frames` Frames stabil bleibt, wird die
   477│       Ecke neu gesetzt. So überleben Fehl-Detektionen nicht, ein echtes Verschieben aber schon.
   478│     - **Alterung**: pro Frame steigt das Alter jeder Ecke; eine Live-Detektion setzt es auf 0.
   479│       Ab `max_held_frames` ohne Sicht gilt eine Ecke als `stale` (nur fürs Feedback, sie bleibt nutzbar).
   480│     - **Seed**: `seed()` belegt Ecken aus einem Kalibrierprofil vor (Status `seed`), sodass die
   481│       Box bei fixer Kamera sofort und perspektivtreu steht — eine Live-Detektion ersetzt den Seed.
   482│     """

   495│                 self.pos[i] = [float(q[0]), float(q[1])]
   496│                 self.age[i] = self.p.max_held_frames           # Seed gilt sofort als "alt"/unbestätigt
   497│                 self.seeded.add(int(i))

   501│             self.age[i] = self.age.get(i, 0) + 1

   505│             if prev is None:                                   # neuer Marker -> direkt übernehmen
   506│                 self.pos[i] = p
   507│                 self.age[i] = 0
   508│                 self.seeded.discard(i)
   509│                 self._pending.pop(i, None)
   510│                 continue
   511│             d = abs(p[0] - prev[0]) + abs(p[1] - prev[1])      # L1-Distanz zur aktuellen Lage

   513│                 self.age[i] = 0
   514│                 self.seeded.discard(i)
   515│                 self._pending.pop(i, None)
   516│                 continue
   517│             if i in self.seeded:                               # erste echte Detektion ersetzt den Seed
   518│                 self.pos[i] = p                                # -> SNAPpen statt EMA-blenden (sonst
   519│                 self.age[i] = 0                                #    bleibt die Ecke 65% beim Seed =
   520│                 self.seeded.discard(i)                         #    versetztes Raster, Fallstrick im
   521│                 self._pending.pop(i, None)                     #    Marker-Fallback-Slicing)

"""Stufe 5 — gemeinsame Eval-Mechanik (von train.py und evaluate.py genutzt)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch

from .data import board_accuracy


def get_device(require_gpu: bool):
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        return torch.device("cuda")
    if require_gpu:
        raise RuntimeError("keine nutzbare GPU (torch.cuda.is_available()==False).")
    return torch.device("cpu")


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate_dataset(model, dataset, device, criterion=None, batch_size: int = 256, num_workers: int = 4) -> dict:
    """Square-Accuracy, Board-Accuracy, Loss und rohe (true, pred)-Arrays für eine Datenmenge."""
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

    loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False,
                        num_workers=num_workers, pin_memory=True)
    model.eval()
    trues: list[int] = []
    preds: list[int] = []
    loss_sum = 0.0
    n = 0
    for x, y in loader:
        x = x.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        y = y.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        logits = model(x)
        if criterion is not None:
            loss_sum += float(criterion(logits, y)) * x.size(0)
        p = logits.argmax(1)
        trues.extend(y.cpu().tolist())
        preds.extend(p.cpu().tolist())
        n += x.size(0)

    trues_a = np.array(trues)
    preds_a = np.array(preds)
    square_acc = float((trues_a == preds_a).mean()) if n else 0.0

    # Macro-Recall: Mittel der Per-Klassen-Trefferquote über vorhandene Klassen.
    # Aussagekräftig auch wenn board_acc=0 (kleine/schwere Datensätze) und ignoriert die
    # empty-Dominanz -> bessere Checkpoint-/Early-Stop-Metrik als die rohe square_acc.
    n_classes = len(getattr(dataset, "c2i", {})) or (int(max(trues_a.max(), preds_a.max())) + 1 if n else 1)
    cm = confusion_matrix(trues_a, preds_a, n_classes) if n else np.zeros((1, 1))
    present = cm.sum(axis=1) > 0
    macro_recall = float(per_class_recall(cm)[present].mean()) if present.any() else 0.0

    # Board-Accuracy: Crops über (session, frame) gruppieren (dataset.rows ist ausgerichtet).
    items = [((r["session_id"], str(r["frame"])), bool(t == p))
             for r, t, p in zip(dataset.rows, trues, preds, strict=False)]
    board_acc = board_accuracy(items)

    return {
        "loss": loss_sum / n if (criterion is not None and n) else None,
        "square_acc": square_acc,
        "macro_recall": macro_recall,
        "board_acc": board_acc,
        "trues": trues_a,
        "preds": preds_a,
    }


def confusion_matrix(trues: np.ndarray, preds: np.ndarray, n_classes: int) -> np.ndarray:
    cm = np.zeros((n_classes, n_classes), dtype=np.int64)
    for t, p in zip(trues, preds, strict=False):
        cm[t, p] += 1
    return cm


def per_class_recall(cm: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    totals = cm.sum(axis=1)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        recall = np.where(totals > 0, np.diag(cm) / np.maximum(totals, 1), 0.0)
    return recall


def save_confusion_png(cm: np.ndarray, classes: list[str], path) -> None:
    import cv2

    n = len(classes)
    cell = 44
    pad = 70
    size = pad + n * cell
    img = np.full((size, size, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
    row_tot = cm.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True).clip(min=1)
    norm = cm / row_tot
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            inten = int(255 * (1 - norm[i, j]))
            y0, x0 = pad + i * cell, pad + j * cell
            cv2.rectangle(img, (x0, y0), (x0 + cell, y0 + cell), (255, inten, inten), -1)
            cv2.rectangle(img, (x0, y0), (x0 + cell, y0 + cell), (220, 220, 220), 1)
            if cm[i, j]:
                cv2.putText(img, str(int(cm[i, j])), (x0 + 4, y0 + cell // 2 + 4),
                            cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.35, (0, 0, 0), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.putText(img, classes[i], (4, pad + i * cell + cell // 2 + 4),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.putText(img, classes[i], (pad + i * cell + 4, pad - 6),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
    cv2.imwrite(str(path), img)


def render_confusion_text(cm: np.ndarray, classes: list[str]) -> str:
    lines = ["confusion (rows=true, cols=pred):", "        " + " ".join(f"{c:>5}" for c in classes)]
    for i, c in enumerate(classes):
        lines.append(f"{c:>7} " + " ".join(f"{cm[i, j]:>5}" for j in range(len(classes))))
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Stufe 5 — Modell. Zwei wählbare Backbones, gleicher 13-Klassen-Kopf."""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


def _gn_groups(channels: int) -> int:
    """Größte Gruppenzahl <= 8, die `channels` teilt (GroupNorm braucht einen Teiler)."""
    g = min(8, channels)
    while g > 1 and channels % g:
        g -= 1
    return g


def _norm_layer(norm: str, channels: int) -> nn.Module:
    """Normalisierungs-Layer. groupnorm umgeht den MIOpen/HIPRTC-BatchNorm-Bug auf ROCm-Windows."""
    if norm == "groupnorm":
        return nn.GroupNorm(num_groups=_gn_groups(channels), num_channels=channels)
    if norm == "none":
        return nn.Identity()
    return nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)


def _convert_bn_to_gn(module: nn.Module) -> nn.Module:
    """Alle BatchNorm2d (z.B. in torchvision-Backbones) durch GroupNorm ersetzen — sonst crasht
    MIOpen auf ROCm-Windows (`miopenStatusUnknownError`). Pretrained-Gewichte des Rumpfs bleiben,
    nur die Norm-Statistik wird neu (GN hat keine running stats)."""
    for name, child in module.named_children():
        if isinstance(child, nn.BatchNorm2d):
            setattr(module, name, nn.GroupNorm(_gn_groups(child.num_features), child.num_features))
        else:
            _convert_bn_to_gn(child)
    return module


class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    """Kompaktes Conv-Netz: 4 Conv-Blöcke (Norm+ReLU+MaxPool), GlobalAvgPool, Linear -> classes."""

    def __init__(self, num_classes: int, in_channels: int = 3, norm: str = "batchnorm") -> None:
        super().__init__()
        chans = [32, 64, 128, 256]
        layers: list[nn.Module] = []
        c_in = in_channels
        for c_out in chans:
            layers += [
                nn.Conv2d(c_in, c_out, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
                _norm_layer(norm, c_out),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            ]
            c_in = c_out
        self.features = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], num_classes)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.pool(x).flatten(1)
        return self.head(x)


_TYPE_ORDER = ("empty", "occluded", "P", "N", "B", "R", "Q", "K")


class FactoredHead(nn.Module):
    """Entkoppelter Kopf: Typ-Kopf (8: empty/occluded/P/N/B/R/Q/K) + Farb-Kopf (2: w/b), additiv zu
    den 14 kombinierten Klassen-Logits (`logit_wP = typ[P] + farbe[w]`; empty/occluded ohne Farbterm).

    Vorteil: `typ[P]` teilt sich über weiße UND schwarze Bauern -> der Typ-Kopf sieht je Typ doppelt
    so viele Beispiele (Pooling). Ausgabe sind GANZ NORMALE 14-Klassen-Logits in `classes`-Reihenfolge,
    daher bleibt alles Nachgelagerte (Loss/Board-Acc/Eval/Inferenz) unverändert.
    """

    def __init__(self, feat_dim: int, classes: list[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.type_head = nn.Linear(feat_dim, len(_TYPE_ORDER))
        self.color_head = nn.Linear(feat_dim, 2)
        t_idx, c_idx = [], []
        for cls in classes:
            if cls in ("empty", "occluded"):
                t_idx.append(_TYPE_ORDER.index(cls))
                c_idx.append(-1)
            else:
                t_idx.append(_TYPE_ORDER.index(cls[1]))   # 'wP'->'P'
                c_idx.append(0 if cls[0] == "w" else 1)
        self.register_buffer("t_idx", torch.tensor(t_idx, dtype=torch.long))
        self.register_buffer("c_idx", torch.tensor(c_idx, dtype=torch.long))
        self.register_buffer("c_mask", (self.c_idx >= 0).float())

    def forward(self, feat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        tl = self.type_head(feat)                                  # [B, 8]
        cl = self.color_head(feat)                                 # [B, 2]
        out = tl.index_select(1, self.t_idx)                       # [B, 14] Typ-Logit je Klasse
        color_term = cl.index_select(1, self.c_idx.clamp(min=0))   # [B, 14]
        return out + color_term * self.c_mask                      # Farbe nur für echte Figuren


class HierarchicalHead(nn.Module):
    """Zweistufiger Kopf (Occupancy→Piece): ein Occupancy-Kopf (2: leer/besetzt) + ein Figuren-Kopf
    (13: die besetzten Klassen, d.h. alle außer `empty`, inkl. `occluded`). Die Ausgabe sind
    **rekonstruierte Log-Wahrscheinlichkeiten** über die 14 `classes` in genau ihrer Reihenfolge:

        out[empty]    = log P(empty)                          = log_softmax(occ)[leer]
        out[piece c]  = log P(besetzt) + log P(c | besetzt)   = log_softmax(occ)[besetzt]
                                                                 + log_softmax(piece)[c]

    Damit gilt `exp(out)` summiert je Zeile zu 1, `softmax(out)=P` (Inferenz unverändert) und
    `CrossEntropyLoss(out, y)` ist exakt die zweistufige Joint-NLL: für `empty`-Ziele hängt der Loss
    nur am Occupancy-Kopf, für besetzte Ziele an beiden — der Figuren-Kopf bekommt also **nur auf
    besetzten Feldern Gradient** (das chesscog-Prinzip), ganz ohne Sonderfall im Trainingsloop.
    """

    def __init__(self, feat_dim: int, classes: list[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        piece_classes = [c for c in classes if c != "empty"]   # 13 besetzte Klassen, Reihenfolge wie classes
        self.occ_head = nn.Linear(feat_dim, 2)                  # [B, 2] leer / besetzt
        self.piece_head = nn.Linear(feat_dim, len(piece_classes))  # [B, 13]
        occ_idx, piece_idx, occ_mask = [], [], []
        for c in classes:
            if c == "empty":
                occ_idx.append(0); piece_idx.append(0); occ_mask.append(0.0)
            else:
                occ_idx.append(1); piece_idx.append(piece_classes.index(c)); occ_mask.append(1.0)
        self.register_buffer("occ_idx", torch.tensor(occ_idx, dtype=torch.long))      # [14] -> {0,1}
        self.register_buffer("piece_idx", torch.tensor(piece_idx, dtype=torch.long))  # [14] -> 0..12
        self.register_buffer("occ_mask", torch.tensor(occ_mask, dtype=torch.float32)) # [14] 0 für empty

    def forward(self, feat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        occ = F.log_softmax(self.occ_head(feat), dim=1)            # [B, 2]
        pc = F.log_softmax(self.piece_head(feat), dim=1)           # [B, 13]
        occ_term = occ.index_select(1, self.occ_idx)               # [B, 14] log P(leer/besetzt)
        piece_term = pc.index_select(1, self.piece_idx)            # [B, 14] log P(c | besetzt)
        return occ_term + piece_term * self.occ_mask               # [B, 14] Log-Probs


class DecoupledModel(nn.Module):
    """Backbone als Feature-Extraktor + entkoppelter Kopf (`FactoredHead` Typ×Farbe oder
    `HierarchicalHead` Occupancy→Piece). Gibt in jedem Fall 14 Werte pro Feld aus (Logits bzw.
    Log-Probs), sodass alles Nachgelagerte (Loss/Board-Acc/Eval/Inferenz) unverändert bleibt."""

    def __init__(self, backbone: str, classes: list[str], pretrained: bool, norm: str,
                 head: str = "factored") -> None:
        super().__init__()
        if backbone == "smallcnn":
            base = SmallCNN(len(classes), norm=norm)
            self.features, self.pool, self._mobile = base.features, base.pool, None
            feat_dim = 256
        elif backbone == "mobilenet_v3_small":
            from torchvision import models

            weights = models.MobileNet_V3_Small_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 if pretrained else None
            m = models.mobilenet_v3_small(weights=weights)
            feat_dim = m.classifier[-1].in_features
            m.classifier[-1] = nn.Identity()           # Modell gibt jetzt Features aus
            if norm == "groupnorm":
                _convert_bn_to_gn(m)
            self._mobile, self.features, self.pool = m, None, None
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unbekanntes backbone {backbone!r} (smallcnn | mobilenet_v3_small).")
        self.head = HierarchicalHead(feat_dim, classes) if head == "twostage" else FactoredHead(feat_dim, classes)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        feat = self._mobile(x) if self._mobile is not None else self.pool(self.features(x)).flatten(1)
        return self.head(feat)


def build_model(backbone: str, num_classes: int, pretrained: bool = False,
                norm: str = "batchnorm", head: str = "combined",
                classes: list[str] | None = None) -> nn.Module:
    """`head="combined"`: ein 14-Klassen-Linear-Kopf. `head="factored"`: entkoppelter Typ+Farbe-Kopf.
    `head="twostage"`: zweistufiger Occupancy→Piece-Kopf (`HierarchicalHead`). `factored`/`twostage`
    brauchen die `classes`-Liste für das Index-Mapping."""
    if head in ("factored", "twostage"):
        from .. import config

        return DecoupledModel(backbone, classes or config.CLASSES, pretrained, norm, head=head)
    if head != "combined":
        raise ValueError(f"unbekannter head {head!r} (combined | factored | twostage).")
    if backbone == "smallcnn":
        return SmallCNN(num_classes, norm=norm)
    if backbone == "mobilenet_v3_small":
        from torchvision import models

        weights = models.MobileNet_V3_Small_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 if pretrained else None
        m = models.mobilenet_v3_small(weights=weights)
        in_f = m.classifier[-1].in_features
        m.classifier[-1] = nn.Linear(in_f, num_classes)
        if norm == "groupnorm":     # ROCm-Windows: MobileNet-BatchNorm -> GroupNorm, sonst MIOpen-Crash
            _convert_bn_to_gn(m)
        return m
    raise ValueError(f"unbekanntes backbone {backbone!r} (smallcnn | mobilenet_v3_small).")

from __future__ import annotations

from .. import config

def load_run(run_dir: Path):
    """Modell + Run-config aus einem Run-Verzeichnis laden (best.pt, sonst last.pt).

    Öffentlich, weil `chesslab.serving.load_run` (die kanonische Inference-Facade,
    siehe specs/rework/01-serving-facade.md) diese Funktion mit einem Cache davor aufruft.
    """
    import torch

    from .model import build_model

    cfg = json.loads((run_dir / "config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    model = build_model(cfg["backbone"], len(cfg["classes"]), norm=cfg.get("norm", "batchnorm"),
                        head=cfg.get("head", "combined"), classes=cfg["classes"])
    ckpt = run_dir / "best.pt"
    if not ckpt.exists():
        ckpt = run_dir / "last.pt"
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(ckpt, map_location="cpu"))
    return model, cfg

def run_export(run: str, fmt: str = "torchscript") -> int:
    import torch

    from .data import build_model_card

    run_dir = Path(run)
    if not (run_dir / "config.json").exists():
        print(f"[FAIL] kein config.json in {run_dir}.")

    model, cfg = _load_run(run_dir)

        metrics = json.loads(eval_test.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    card = build_model_card(

        torch_version=torch.__version__, hip_version=getattr(torch.version, "hip", None),

    print(f"[OK] exportiert: {', '.join(written)} + model_card.json -> {run_dir}")
    return 0

class MarkerTracker:
    """Tracks a smoothed, occlusion/jitter-resilient position per marker.

    Properties (parameters from `config.TRACKER`):
    - **Dead zone**: detected movement <= `move_threshold` -> freeze position (stable box).
    - **Smoothing**: real movement -> EMA with `smooth_alpha` instead of hard snapping.
    - **Outlier / self-correction**: a single-frame jump > `jump_reject_px` is initially
      held; only when the new position stays stable over `jump_confirm_frames` frames is the

    - **Seed**: `seed()` pre-populates corners from a calibration profile (status `seed`), so the
      box stands immediately and perspective-accurately with a fixed camera — a live detection replaces the seed.
    """

# Design-Patterns im Projekt

Bestandsaufnahme der bewusst oder implizit verwendeten Muster, mit Bewertung der Anwendung.

## Korrekt angewendet

### Pipeline / Staged Architecture (Kern)
Die gesamte Kern-Library ist eine dateibasierte Pipeline mit klaren Stufen-Contracts
(Profil-YAML → Session-JSONL → Manifest-JSONL → split.json → Run-Verzeichnis). Jede Stufe ist
einzeln wiederholbar (`collect` und `slice` getrennt → Re-Slicing ohne Neuaufnahme). Das ist die
tragende Architekturentscheidung des Projekts und funktioniert gut.
**Dateien:** collect.py, labeling.py, dataset.py, training/

### Adapter (ingest_adapters/)
Sauberes Plugin-Muster: einheitlicher Contract `iter_items(root) -> Iterator[ImportItem]`,
`ImportItem`-Dataclass als Schema, drei Implementierungen (chesscog, chessred, synthetic), die
unterschiedliche Ecken-Reihenfolgen/FEN-Formate auf das interne Format normalisieren. Zustandslos,
funktional, gut testbar (chesscog/chessred getestet; synthetic noch nicht — siehe Issues C3).
**Dateien:** ingest_adapters/__init__.py, chesscog.py, chessred.py, synthetic.py

### Single Source of Truth (config.py)
Klassenliste `CLASSES`, Crop-Defaults, Augment-Policy, Photometrie-Defaults, `Paths`-Abstraktion —
alles genau einmal definiert, überall importiert. `Paths` als Parameter macht Tests isolierbar.
Das CLAUDE.md-Prinzip „Konfig vor Code" wird weitgehend gelebt.
**Einschränkung:** Crop-Parameter existieren zusätzlich als `calibration.CropParams` (Duplikat, M5).

### Lazy Import (torch, UI)
torch wird konsequent erst in Funktionen importiert (web/inference.py, training/*), damit
CLI/Web ohne GPU-Stack starten; OpenCV-GUI ebenso. Bewusste, dokumentierte Entscheidung
(Memory: „lazy torch"). Korrekt angewendet.
**Gegenbeispiel:** der Lazy-Import in geometry3d.py:159 ist kein Feature, sondern kaschiert
einen Import-Zyklus (M1).

### Strategy (Trainings-Köpfe & Photometrie)
Modell-Köpfe (`combined` / `factored` / `twostage`) und Photometrie-Operatoren
(`none`/`clahe`/`gamma`/`grayworld`) sind als austauschbare Strategien über Config-Strings
gewählt und im Bake-off (`experiment.py`) systematisch gekreuzt. Saubere Anwendung; das
Bake-off-Grid ist praktisch ein kleines Experiment-Framework.
**Dateien:** training/model.py:68–137, photometric.py, experiment.py

### Guarded Shared State + Producer/Consumer (move_tracker)
`MoveTracker`: Capture-Daemon-Thread produziert Zustand (Board, Overlays, Note), FastAPI-Handler
konsumieren unter einem gemeinsamen `threading.Lock`. Innerhalb der Klasse konsequent; das Muster
endet aber an der Klassengrenze (`_STATE`-Dict der App ist ungeschützt, H1).

### Smoothing/Tracker-Objekt (MarkerTracker)
EMA-Glättung + Dead-Zone + Halten bei Okklusion + Seed aus Kalibrierung als eigenes zustandsbehaftetes
Objekt, wiederverwendet von Web-Kamera und move_tracker (live_align). Gute Wiederverwendung; die
Zustandslogik ist komplex genug, dass sie Dokumentation/Tests verdient.

## Implizit vorhanden / verbesserungswürdig

### Singleton via Modul-Globals (Web-Layer) — Anti-Pattern in dieser Form
`_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`, `_INFER`, `_MANUAL`, `CAMERA`, `_STATE` sind Modul-Level-Singletons.
Für ein lokales Tool pragmatisch, aber ohne Locks und ohne Lebenszyklus (kein Timeout, kein
Cleanup beim Feature-Wechsel). Empfehlung: beibehalten, aber je Dict ein Lock + explizite
Reset-Semantik (H1).

### Model-Run als Artefakt-Contract (Run-Verzeichnis)
`data/models/<run>/` mit `config.json` + `best.pt` fungiert als implizites
„Model-Registry"-Pattern. Gut: Konsumenten laden Modell **und** Preprocessing-Config zusammen.
Schlecht: der Lade-Einstieg ist privat (`_load_run`, H4) und die Preprocessing-Anwendung
(Photometrie!) ist nicht Teil des Contracts (C1).

### Fehlende Muster, die sich anbieten
- **Observer/Voter-Seam im move_tracker:** Frame-Diff und (geplanter) CNN-Beobachter als
  gleichförmige Kandidaten-Lieferanten `(move, score)`, kombiniert von einer Voting-Instanz (M3).
- **Facade für „Frame → modellfertige Crops":** eine Funktion, die Geometrie + Photometrie aus
  der Run-Config kapselt — beseitigt die Train/Serve-Duplikation (C1/R1).
- **Schema-Objekte für Wire-Formate:** Pydantic-Modelle für API-Bodies (M2) und ein dokumentiertes
  Manifest-/Session-Schema (M5) — heute leben die Schemata nur im Writer-Code.
