"""Shared camera module for the web UI.

ONE camera instance (`CAMERA`), ONE MJPEG helper (`mjpeg`) and ONE source for
per-frame board geometry (`BoardTracker`: corners + warp). Calibration, collect and inference
all use the same code here — no more duplicated camera/corner/encode code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import ssl
import threading
import time
import urllib.request

import cv2
import numpy as np

from ..calibration import (
    CalibrationProfile,
    board_corners_for_frame,
    make_tracker,
    open_camera,
    warp_from_corners,
)

_BOUNDARY = b"--frame\r\nContent-Type: image/jpeg\r\n\r\n"

# Env override: if this variable is set (e.g. an IP cam URL), ALL camera paths in the
# web UI use this source instead of the integer index selected in the UI. This allows
# connecting a phone/network camera without frontend changes. Example:
#   set CHESSLAB_CAMERA_SOURCE=https://<PHONE-IP>:4444/video/snapshot   (Android IP Camera)
CAMERA_SOURCE_ENV = "CHESSLAB_CAMERA_SOURCE"


class _UrlSnapshotCapture:
    """cv2.VideoCapture-compatible frame grabber for a JPEG snapshot URL (e.g. Android IP Camera
    `/video/snapshot`). `cv2.VideoCapture` fails on self-signed HTTPS — so we fetch the bytes
    ourselves via urllib (TLS verification off) and decode with `cv2.imdecode`. Polls one
    image per `read()` (sufficient for calibration/collect preview at a few FPS)."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, timeout: float = 4.0) -> None:
        self.url = url
        self.timeout = timeout
        self._ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
        self._ctx.check_hostname = False
        self._ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE     # accept self-signed cert
        self._ok = True

    def isOpened(self) -> bool:
        return self._ok

    def read(self):
        if not self._ok:
            return False, None
        try:
            data = urllib.request.urlopen(self.url, timeout=self.timeout, context=self._ctx).read()
            img = cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(data, np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
            return (img is not None), img
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — network/timeout: treat like an empty frame
            return False, None

    def release(self) -> None:
        self._ok = False


class _UrlMjpegCapture:
    """cv2.VideoCapture-compatible reader for an MJPEG stream (multipart/x-mixed-replace),
    e.g. Android IP Camera `/video/m.jpeg`. Holds ONE open connection (self-signed HTTPS
    via urllib, TLS verification off) and extracts the next JPEG on each `read()` by looking
    for SOI/EOI markers (0xFFD8 … 0xFFD9) in the buffer — much smoother than single snapshots."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, timeout: float = 10.0) -> None:
        self.url = url
        self.timeout = timeout
        ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
        self._stream = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=timeout, context=ctx)
        self._buf = bytearray()
        self._ok = True

    def isOpened(self) -> bool:
        return self._ok

    def read(self):
        if not self._ok:
            return False, None
        try:
            while True:
                a = self._buf.find(b"\xff\xd8")               # JPEG start
                b = self._buf.find(b"\xff\xd9", a + 2) if a != -1 else -1  # JPEG end
                if a != -1 and b != -1:
                    jpg = bytes(self._buf[a:b + 2])
                    del self._buf[:b + 2]
                    img = cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(jpg, np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
                    return (img is not None), img
                chunk = self._stream.read(16384)
                if not chunk:
                    return False, None
                self._buf.extend(chunk)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — network/timeout: treat like an empty frame
            return False, None

    def release(self) -> None:
        self._ok = False
        try:
            self._stream.close()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass


class LatestFrame:
    """Grab-latest wrapper: continuously reads from a `cv2.VideoCapture`-compatible
    source in the background and keeps only the NEWEST frame in a single-slot buffer. This way
    a slow consumer (move tracker with CNN/encode) always gets the most recent image, instead of
    working through an ever-growing backlog from the socket/JPEG buffer.

    `read()` returns `(ok, frame)` of the latest frame immediately (no network blocking);
    `release()` stops the reader thread and releases the underlying source."""

    def __init__(self, cap, poll: float = 0.001) -> None:
        self._cap = cap
        self._poll = poll
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._frame = None
        self._ok = False
        self._running = True
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

    def _loop(self) -> None:
        while self._running:
            ok, f = self._cap.read()
            if ok and f is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    self._frame, self._ok = f, True
            else:
                # Source (still) empty/broken: wait briefly so the loop doesn't spin hot.
                time.sleep(0.01)

    def isOpened(self) -> bool:
        return getattr(self._cap, "isOpened", lambda: True)()

    def read(self):
        with self._lock:
            if not self._ok or self._frame is None:
                return False, None
            return True, self._frame.copy()

    def release(self) -> None:
        self._running = False
        if self._thread.is_alive():
            self._thread.join(timeout=1.0)
        if hasattr(self._cap, "release"):
            self._cap.release()


def _is_url(source) -> bool:
    return isinstance(source, str) and "://" in source


def open_source(source):
    """Open source: URL -> MJPEG stream reader or snapshot grabber (both HTTPS/self-signed-
    capable); otherwise local index/path via `open_camera` (DSHOW on Windows). If the URL
    contains 'snapshot' -> single-image poll, otherwise multipart MJPEG stream (smoother)."""
    if _is_url(source):
        if "snapshot" in source.lower():
            return _UrlSnapshotCapture(source)
        return _UrlMjpegCapture(source)
    return open_camera(source)


_open_source = open_source  # backward-compat alias (move_tracker used this before phase 06)


def effective_source(index):
    """Effective source for a UI-selected index: env override (URL) wins, otherwise the index.
    Returns a hashable key (URL string or int)."""
    env = os.environ.get(CAMERA_SOURCE_ENV, "").strip()
    if env:
        return env
    return index


# Optional HIGH-RESOLUTION capture source: the live preview runs smoothly over the (possibly
# downscaled) stream, but SAVED frames are pulled from this snapshot URL
# (full sensor resolution). Markers are re-detected on the snapshot during capture -> stream and
# capture sources may differ in resolution/orientation. Example:
#   set CHESSLAB_CAMERA_CAPTURE=https://<PHONE-IP>:4444/video/snapshot
CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENV = "CHESSLAB_CAMERA_CAPTURE"


def capture_url() -> str | None:
    """High-resolution snapshot URL for saving, if set; otherwise None (-> use live frame)."""
    return os.environ.get(CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENV, "").strip() or None


class Camera:
    """Thread-safe, shared camera. `ensure(index)` opens (or switches) the source;
    `read()` returns the latest frame (or None). `markers_*` reflect the calibration status."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.cap = None
        self.index = None
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.markers_found = False
        self.markers_count = 0
        self.markers_live = 0
        self.markers_held = 0

    def ensure(self, index) -> None:
        src = effective_source(index)   # Env override (IP cam URL) wins over the UI index
        with self.lock:
            if self.cap is not None and self.index == src:
                return
            if self.cap is not None:
                self.cap.release()
            self.cap = _open_source(src)
            self.index = src

    def read(self):
        with self.lock:
            if self.cap is None:
                return None
            ok, f = self.cap.read()
            return f if ok else None

    def grab_capture(self):
        """Get frame FOR SAVING -> (frame, is_hires). If a capture URL is set
        (`CHESSLAB_CAMERA_CAPTURE`), a single high-resolution snapshot is fetched from there
        (is_hires=True); otherwise the current live frame (is_hires=False). When is_hires, the
        caller MUST re-detect markers/corners on THIS frame (different resolution/orientation
        than the preview)."""
        url = capture_url()
        if url:
            ok, f = _UrlSnapshotCapture(url, timeout=6.0).read()
            if ok and f is not None:
                return f, True
        return self.read(), False

    def release(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            if self.cap is not None:
                self.cap.release()
            self.cap = None
            self.index = None

    @property
    def open(self) -> bool:
        return self.cap is not None


# A single instance for the whole app.
CAMERA = Camera()


def encode_jpeg(img, quality: int = 80) -> bytes | None:
    ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, int(quality)])
    return buf.tobytes() if ok else None


def mjpeg(frames, idle: float = 0.05):
    """`frames`: iterator of BGR images (np.ndarray) or None (= no frame -> wait briefly).
    Wraps JPEG encode + multipart boundary + StreamingResponse — the caller only provides images."""
    from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

    def gen():
        for img in frames:
            if img is None:
                time.sleep(idle)
                continue
            data = encode_jpeg(img)
            if data is not None:
                yield _BOUNDARY + data + b"\r\n"

    return StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type="multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=frame")


class BoardTracker:
    """Per-stream: marker tracker seeded from the profile + last known corners.

    ``process(frame)`` -> (warped | None, corners | None). Exactly **one** place for
    corner detection and unwarping — collect and inference share this logic, and the
    last live-shown corners (``last_corners``) are what gets saved during capture.

    Thread-safe: ``last_corners`` is written under its own lock; ``corners()`` returns
    a copy.
    """

    def __init__(self, profile: CalibrationProfile) -> None:
        self.profile = profile
        self.tracker = make_tracker(profile)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self.last_corners = None

    def process(self, frame):
        corners = board_corners_for_frame(frame, self.profile, self.tracker)
        if corners is not None:
            with self._lock:
                self.last_corners = corners
        warped = warp_from_corners(frame, self.profile, corners) if corners is not None else None
        return warped, corners

    def corners(self):
        """Copy of the last known corners (thread-safe)."""
        with self._lock:
            return list(self.last_corners) if self.last_corners is not None else None

"""Turntable scan controller for the web UI (tab "Scan").

ONE grab thread keeps the latest frame from the selected source (phone IP cam URL or USB index)
and saves — when "recording" — the mouse-set crop from the frontend at the desired
interval as `scans/<name>/NNN.jpg`. The live preview shows the same frame downscaled with
the crop overlaid. Pure photogrammetry input (RealityScan) — independent of calibration/
camera singleton of the rest of the app, so scanning doesn't disturb collect/inference.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import cv2

from .camera import _open_source, _UrlSnapshotCapture

# scans/ lives at the repo level (next to data/) — anchored via file location, independent of cwd.
SCANS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scans"


def _open(source, width: int, height: int):
    """USB index -> DSHOW+MJPG+requested resolution (otherwise the driver caps at 640×480);
    URL -> shared snapshot/MJPEG reader from camera.py (HTTPS/self-signed-capable)."""
    s = str(source).strip()
    if s.isdigit():
        import platform
        backend = cv2.CAP_DSHOW if platform.system() == "Windows" else cv2.CAP_ANY
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(int(s), backend)
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FOURCC, cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"MJPG"))
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH, width)
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT, height)
        for _ in range(6):
            cap.read()
        return cap
    return _open_source(s)


def _next_index(out_dir: Path) -> int:
    """Next free NNN number in the folder — so "Ring 2" automatically appends to Ring 1."""
    n = -1
    for p in out_dir.glob("*.jpg"):
        try:
            n = max(n, int(p.stem))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return n + 1


class ScanController:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.cap = None
        self.source = ""
        self.thread: threading.Thread | None = None
        self.stop_flag = False

        # Separate CAPTURE source: the live preview runs over the smooth stream
        # (`source`, usually …/video/m.jpeg), but SAVED photos are pulled from this
        # snapshot URL (…/video/snapshot, clean single images). Empty -> photos
        # come from the live frame. The crop drawn on the preview is scaled to the
        # snapshot resolution (if it differs from the stream).
        self.capture_source = ""
        self.capture_cap = None

        # Demand control: the physical camera is only grabbed when preview is shown
        # or recording is active. `configured` = source selected (UI panel open); the real
        # `cap` is opened lazily / released after `idle_timeout` seconds of inactivity.
        self.configured = False
        self._cfg = ("0", 2880, 2160)          # (source, width, height) for lazy re-open
        self._last_demand = 0.0                # last preview fetch (recording = continuous demand)
        self.idle_timeout = 12.0

        self.frame = None                 # last full-res BGR frame
        self.frame_size = (0, 0)          # (w, h) of the source
        self.frame_id = 0
        self.error = ""

        self.recording = False
        self.out_name = ""
        self.out_dir: Path | None = None
        self.index = 0                    # next file number
        self.saved_run = 0                # saved in this recording run
        self._last_save = 0.0

        # Config (set via frontend)
        self.crop: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None   # (x0,y0,x1,y1) full-res
        self.interval = 0.8
        self.count = 0                    # 0 = unlimited (until stop)
        self.quality = 92

    # -- Source open / close -------------------------------------------------
    def open(self, source, width: int = 2880, height: int = 2160, capture_source: str = "") -> dict:
        """SELECT source + test once. After that the loop only holds the camera on demand
        (preview/recording) and releases it automatically when idle.

        `capture_source` (optional): snapshot URL from which images are saved during recording —
        the preview stays on the smooth `source` stream."""
        self.close()
        cap = _open(source, width, height)     # Test open: fails early if the source is broken
        ok, img = cap.read()
        if not ok or img is None:
            try:
                cap.release()
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
            raise RuntimeError(f"No frames from {source!r}. Check source/URL/app.")
        cap_src = str(capture_source or "").strip()
        capture_cap = None
        if cap_src:
            probe = _UrlSnapshotCapture(cap_src)   # Test snapshot once -> early, clear error
            ok_s, _ = probe.read()
            if not ok_s:
                try:
                    cap.release()
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    pass
                raise RuntimeError(f"Snapshot source {cap_src!r} does not deliver an image. Check URL.")
            capture_cap = probe
        with self.lock:
            self.cap = cap                     # stays open initially (preview starts immediately)
            self.configured = True
            self._cfg = (str(source), int(width), int(height))
            self.source = str(source)
            self.capture_source = cap_src
            self.capture_cap = capture_cap
            self.frame = img
            self.frame_size = (img.shape[1], img.shape[0])
            self.frame_id += 1
            self.error = ""
            self.stop_flag = False
            self._last_demand = time.time()
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        return self.status()

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.stop_flag = True
        t = self.thread
        if t is not None:
            t.join(timeout=2.0)
        with self.lock:
            self.recording = False
            self.configured = False
            self._release_cap_locked()
            if self.capture_cap is not None:
                try:
                    self.capture_cap.release()
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    pass
            self.capture_cap = None
            self.thread = None

    def _release_cap_locked(self) -> None:
        if self.cap is not None:
            try:
                self.cap.release()
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
        self.cap = None

    # -- Grab / save loop ---------------------------------------------------
    def _loop(self) -> None:
        while not self.stop_flag:
            now = time.time()
            with self.lock:
                demand = self.recording or (now - self._last_demand) < self.idle_timeout
                cap = self.cap
                if not demand and cap is not None:      # Idle -> release camera
                    self._release_cap_locked()
                    self.frame = None                   # Preview should not show old image
                    cap = None

            if demand and cap is None:                  # Demand but camera released -> lazy open
                try:
                    new = _open(*self._cfg)
                    ok, img = new.read()
                    if not ok or img is None:
                        new.release()
                        raise RuntimeError("no frame")
                except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                    with self.lock:
                        self.error = f"Re-open failed: {e}"
                    time.sleep(0.3)
                    continue
                with self.lock:
                    self.cap = new
                    self.error = ""
                cap = new

            if cap is None:                             # Parked: wait until demand reappears
                time.sleep(0.15)
                continue

            ok, img = cap.read()
            if not ok or img is None:
                with self.lock:
                    self.error = "no frame"
                time.sleep(0.1)
                continue
            ctx = None
            with self.lock:
                self.frame = img
                self.frame_size = (img.shape[1], img.shape[0])
                self.frame_id += 1
                self.error = ""
                if self.recording and (time.time() - self._last_save) >= self.interval:
                    ctx = (self.crop, self.frame_size, self.out_dir,
                           self.index, self.quality, self.capture_cap)
            if ctx is not None:
                self._save_photo(img, *ctx)     # Snapshot fetch + write WITHOUT lock

    def _save_photo(self, live_img, crop, prev_size, out_dir, index, quality, capture_cap) -> None:
        """Save one photo. If a snapshot source is set (`capture_cap`), the saved image comes
        from there and the crop drawn on the preview is scaled to the snapshot size; otherwise
        the live frame is saved. Runs deliberately WITHOUT lock (network fetch), counters are
        updated under lock at the end."""
        img = live_img
        sx = sy = 1.0
        if capture_cap is not None:
            ok, snap = capture_cap.read()
            if ok and snap is not None:
                img = snap
                pw, ph = prev_size
                if pw and ph:                    # Crop (preview coords) -> snapshot coords
                    sx, sy = snap.shape[1] / pw, snap.shape[0] / ph
            else:
                with self.lock:
                    self.error = "Snapshot failed — live frame saved"
        out = img
        if crop is not None:
            pw, ph = prev_size
            ap = (pw / ph) if ph else 0.0
            asp = (img.shape[1] / img.shape[0]) if img.shape[0] else 0.0
            # Only relevant for the snapshot path: if the snapshot orientation does not match
            # the preview (e.g. preview landscape, snapshot portrait), the preview crop would be
            # distorted and misplaced. In that case save the full snapshot + warn instead of
            # silently cropping garbage. For the live frame (no capture_cap) the coords always
            # match -> no check needed.
            aspect_mismatch = (capture_cap is not None and ap and asp
                               and abs(ap - asp) > 0.15 * asp)
            if aspect_mismatch:
                with self.lock:
                    self.error = ("Preview/snapshot have different orientations — full snapshot "
                                  "saved. Set both sources to the same resolution/orientation.")
            else:
                box = (crop[0] * sx, crop[1] * sy, crop[2] * sx, crop[3] * sy)
                x0, y0, x1, y1 = self._clamp(box, img.shape[1], img.shape[0])
                if x1 - x0 >= 8 and y1 - y0 >= 8:
                    out = img[y0:y1, x0:x1]
        assert out_dir is not None
        cv2.imwrite(str(out_dir / f"{index:03d}.jpg"), out,
                    [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, int(quality)])
        with self.lock:
            self.index += 1
            self.saved_run += 1
            self._last_save = time.time()
            if self.count and self.saved_run >= self.count:
                self.recording = False

    @staticmethod
    def _clamp(box, w, h):
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
        x0, x1 = sorted((max(0, min(w, int(x0))), max(0, min(w, int(x1)))))
        y0, y1 = sorted((max(0, min(h, int(y0))), max(0, min(h, int(y1)))))
        return x0, y0, x1, y1

    # -- Config / recording -------------------------------------------------
    def configure(self, crop=None, interval=None, count=None, quality=None, out=None) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            if crop is not None:
                self.crop = tuple(int(v) for v in crop) if crop else None
            if interval is not None:
                self.interval = max(0.0, float(interval))
            if count is not None:
                self.count = max(0, int(count))
            if quality is not None:
                self.quality = int(quality)
            if out is not None:
                self.out_name = str(out).strip()
        return self.status()

    def start(self, out: str | None = None) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            if not self.configured:
                raise RuntimeError("no source open — connect first.")
            name = (out or self.out_name).strip()
            if not name:
                raise RuntimeError("target name missing (e.g. 'pawn').")
            if self.crop is None:
                raise RuntimeError("no crop set — draw a box on the live image.")
            self.out_name = name
            self.out_dir = SCANS_ROOT / name
            self.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            self.index = _next_index(self.out_dir)     # appends to existing rings
            self.saved_run = 0
            self._last_save = 0.0                       # first photo immediately
            self.recording = True
        return self.status()

    def stop(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            self.recording = False
        return self.status()

    # -- Preview / Status ---------------------------------------------------
    def preview(self, maxside: int = 900, last_id: int = -1):
        """(bgr_image, frame_id) of the latest frame, downscaled + crop box drawn.
        Returns (None, id) when no new frame is available (caller then waits briefly)."""
        with self.lock:
            self._last_demand = time.time()    # preview fetch = demand (keeps camera alive)
            img = self.frame
            fid = self.frame_id
            crop = self.crop
            rec = self.recording
        if img is None or fid == last_id:
            return None, fid
        h, w = img.shape[:2]
        sc = min(1.0, maxside / max(w, h))
        small = cv2.resize(img, (int(w * sc), int(h * sc))) if sc < 1.0 else img.copy()
        if crop is not None:
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = self._clamp(crop, w, h)
            col = (0, 200, 0) if rec else (0, 180, 255)
            cv2.rectangle(small, (int(x0 * sc), int(y0 * sc)), (int(x1 * sc), int(y1 * sc)), col, 2)
        return small, fid

    def status(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            total = len(list(self.out_dir.glob("*.jpg"))) if self.out_dir else 0
            return {
                "open": self.configured,        # source selected (UI panel open)
                "grabbing": self.cap is not None,  # camera currently physically active (otherwise parked)
                "source": self.source,
                "capture_source": self.capture_source,
                "frame_size": list(self.frame_size),
                "recording": self.recording,
                "out": self.out_name,
                "crop": list(self.crop) if self.crop else None,
                "interval": self.interval,
                "count": self.count,
                "quality": self.quality,
                "saved_run": self.saved_run,
                "total": total,
                "index": self.index,
                "error": self.error,
                "default_source": os.environ.get("CHESSLAB_CAMERA_SOURCE", "").strip(),
                "default_capture": os.environ.get("CHESSLAB_CAMERA_CAPTURE", "").strip(),
            }


SCANNER = ScanController()

"""Training router: /api/split, /api/train*, /api/runs*"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException

from ..schemas import SplitRequest, TrainRequest
from ..state import TRAIN, train_derive_and_update
from ..util import _img_url, _read_jsonl, _run_dirs

log = logging.getLogger("chesslab.web")
router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/api/split")
def split(req: SplitRequest):
    from ... import config
    from ... import dataset as dataset_mod

    rc = dataset_mod.run_split(val_frac=config.DEFAULT_VAL_FRAC, test_frac=config.DEFAULT_TEST_FRAC,
                                max_empty_ratio=req.max_empty_ratio, seed=req.seed,
                                max_class_ratio=req.max_class_ratio,
                                allow_degenerate=req.allow_degenerate)
    if rc != 0:
        raise HTTPException(400, "Split failed — dataset degenerated (set --allow-degenerate in the web tab).")
    return {"ok": True}


@router.post("/api/train")
def train(req: TrainRequest):
    from ... import config
    from ... import dataset as dataset_mod
    from ... import dataset_build as dataset_build_mod

    t_proc = TRAIN.get("proc")
    if t_proc is not None and t_proc.poll() is None:
        raise HTTPException(409, "a training is already running.")
    if req.resume and not (config.DATA.models / req.resume / "config.json").exists():
        raise HTTPException(400, f"Resume run '{req.resume}' not found.")

    # Preferred path: train on a built, named dataset (its own split).
    if req.dataset:
        dd = dataset_build_mod.dataset_dir(req.dataset)
        if not (dd / "split.json").exists():
            raise HTTPException(400, f"Dataset '{req.dataset}' not built — build it first in the datasets tab.")
        sp = json.loads((dd / "split.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if sp["counts"]["train"] == 0:
            raise HTTPException(400, "train split empty — the dataset needs at least 2-3 separate "
                                "sessions (split per session against data leakage).")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "chesslab.cli", "train", "--backbone", req.backbone,
               "--epochs", str(req.epochs), "--batch-size", str(req.batch_size), "--lr", str(req.lr),
               "--patience", str(req.patience), "--dataset", req.dataset, "--head", req.head]
        if req.resume:
            cmd += ["--resume", req.resume]
        if req.no_amp:
            cmd.append("--no-amp")
        config.DATA.models.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        before = {d.name for d in _run_dirs()}
        log_path = config.DATA.models / "web_train.log"
        log_fh = open(log_path, "w", encoding="utf-8")
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=log_fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, cwd=str(Path.cwd()))
        log_fh.close()   # Child holds its own duplicated handle; release Windows lock (H3)
        TRAIN.update(proc=proc, log=log_path, cmd=" ".join(cmd), before=before,
                     state="running")
        return {"ok": True, "cmd": TRAIN.get("cmd")}

    # Legacy path (global manifest/split) — kept for backward compatibility.
    from ...manifest_cache import manifest_stats
    manifest_sessions = set(manifest_stats(config.DATA.manifests / "squares.jsonl")["crops_by_session"])
    if not manifest_sessions:
        raise HTTPException(400, "No dataset — first capture and slice in the 'Collect' tab.")
    split_file = config.DATA.manifests / "split.json"

    def _split_sessions() -> set[str] | None:
        if not split_file.exists():
            return None
        try:
            sp = json.loads(split_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            return {s for sids in sp["splits"].values() for s in sids}
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            log.warning("split.json not readable — will be regenerated.", exc_info=True)
            return None

    if _split_sessions() != manifest_sessions:
        rc = dataset_mod.run_split(val_frac=config.DEFAULT_VAL_FRAC, test_frac=config.DEFAULT_TEST_FRAC,
                                    max_empty_ratio=config.DEFAULT_MAX_EMPTY_RATIO, seed=config.SEED,
                                    max_class_ratio=None, allow_degenerate=False)
        if rc != 0:
            raise HTTPException(400,
                "Split failed — dataset is degenerated (classes only in one session or "
                "val/test split empty). Capture more sessions with random piece-line assignments, "
                "or rebuild in the datasets tab with 'Allow degenerate' enabled.")

    split = json.loads(split_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if split["counts"]["train"] == 0:
        raise HTTPException(400,
            f"Too few sessions for clean training (currently {len(manifest_sessions)}). "
            "Train/val/test are split per session to avoid data leakage — you need "
            "at least 2-3 separate capture sessions. Capture more games, slice "
            "them, and start again.")
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "chesslab.cli", "train", "--backbone", req.backbone,
           "--epochs", str(req.epochs), "--batch-size", str(req.batch_size), "--head", req.head]
    if req.no_amp:
        cmd.append("--no-amp")
    log_path = config.DATA.models / "web_train.log"
    config.DATA.models.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    before = {d.name for d in _run_dirs()}
    log_fh = open(log_path, "w", encoding="utf-8")
    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=log_fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, cwd=str(Path.cwd()))
    log_fh.close()   # Child holds its own duplicated handle; release Windows lock (H3)
    TRAIN.update(proc=proc, log=log_path, cmd=" ".join(cmd), before=before,
                 state="running")
    return {"ok": True, "cmd": TRAIN.get("cmd")}


@router.get("/api/train/status")
def train_status():
    # State derivation (running/done/crashed/stopped/idle) lives atomically in web/state.py —
    # an abnormally terminated training (abort/crash) must remain visible so the
    # frontend continues to show partial progress instead of hiding it (because rc!=0).
    t = train_derive_and_update()
    state = t["_derived_state"]
    proc = t.get("proc")
    rc = proc.poll() if proc is not None else None
    running = state == "running"
    # Latest run directory (possibly the one just started) + its metrics.
    run, metrics = None, []
    dirs = _run_dirs()
    if dirs:
        run = dirs[-1].name
        metrics = _read_jsonl(dirs[-1] / "metrics.jsonl")
    tail = ""
    if t.get("log") and Path(t["log"]).exists():
        tail = "\n".join(Path(t["log"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()[-8:])
    return {"running": running, "state": state, "run": run, "metrics": metrics,
            "log_tail": tail, "returncode": rc}


@router.post("/api/train/stop")
def train_stop():
    """Stop a running (or stuck-after-GPU/MIOpen-crash) training + release state.
    The run directory with metrics written so far is preserved (partial progress)."""
    proc = TRAIN.get("proc")
    killed = False
    if proc is not None and proc.poll() is None:
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=3)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            log.warning("Training process did not respond to terminate — kill.")
            proc.kill()
        killed = True
    # Return the latest (just-aborted) run directory so the frontend can load its
    # partial metrics.
    dirs = _run_dirs()
    run = dirs[-1].name if dirs else None
    TRAIN.update(proc=None, state="stopped")
    return {"ok": True, "killed": killed, "run": run}


@router.get("/api/runs")
def runs():
    import json


    out = []
    for d in _run_dirs():
        cfg = json.loads((d / "config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        metrics = _read_jsonl(d / "metrics.jsonl")
        ev = d / "eval_test.json"
        test_board = (json.loads(ev.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("board_acc") if ev.exists() else None)
        out.append({
            "run": d.name, "backbone": cfg.get("backbone"), "dataset": cfg.get("dataset"),
            "n_classes": len(cfg.get("classes", [])), "resumed_from": cfg.get("resumed_from"),
            "has_occluded": "occluded" in cfg.get("classes", []),
            "epochs_done": len(metrics),
            "best_board_acc": max((m.get("val_board_acc", 0) for m in metrics), default=0),
            "best_square_acc": max((m.get("val_acc", 0) for m in metrics), default=0),
            "best_macro_recall": max((m.get("val_macro_recall", 0) for m in metrics), default=0),
            "test_board_acc": test_board,
            "last": metrics[-1] if metrics else None,
        })
    return sorted(out, key=lambda r: r["run"], reverse=True)   # newest first


@router.delete("/api/runs/{run}")
def run_delete(run: str):
    import shutil

    from ... import config, serving

    d = config.DATA.models / run
    if "/" in run or "\\" in run or ".." in run or not (d / "config.json").exists():
        raise HTTPException(404, f"Run '{run}' not found.")
    serving.clear_cache()
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return {"ok": True, "run": run}


@router.get("/api/runs/{run}/metrics")
def run_metrics(run: str):
    from ... import config

    return {"run": run, "metrics": _read_jsonl(config.DATA.models / run / "metrics.jsonl")}


@router.get("/api/runs/{run}/eval")
def run_eval(run: str):
    import json

    from ... import config

    d = config.DATA.models / run
    evals = {}
    for f in sorted(d.glob("eval_*.json")):
        split = f.stem.replace("eval_", "")
        evals[split] = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        png = d / f"confusion_{split}.png"
        if png.exists():
            evals[split]["confusion_png"] = _img_url(png.as_posix())
    return {"run": run, "evals": evals}

     1│ """Stage 4 — named, curated datasets.
     2│ 
     3│ A **dataset** is a view on the global crop pool (`data/manifests/squares.jsonl`):
     4│ a selection of sessions + dedup and split policy. Building creates under
     5│ `data/datasets/<name>/` a filtered, deduplicated `manifest.jsonl`, a
     6│ session-based `split.json` and `stats.json`. Crops for rot=0 reference the global
     7│ pool (no copying); only rotation-augmented crops are materialized in the dataset folder.
     8│ 
     9│ Dedup against the recording-induced surplus of nearly identical crops (never-moved pieces on
    10│ fixed camera):
    11│   1. Metadata cap per `(session_id, square, label)` — fast, deterministic.
    12│   2. Perceptual hash (dhash) — discards visually near-duplicates within a class.
    13│ 
    14│ Rotation augmentation (90/180/270°) is optional and deliberately AFTER dedup (4x the
    15│ *curated* crops). It contradicts the fixed-camera assumption (CLAUDE.md) and is a toggle.
    16│ Testable headless: all functions take `paths=config.DATA`.
    17│ """

    19│ from __future__ import annotations

    22│ import random

    33│ 
    34│ def _safe_name(name: str) -> str:

    37│         raise ValueError(f"invalid dataset name: {name!r}")

    39│ 
    40│ 
    41│ def dataset_dir(name: str, paths: config.Paths | None = None) -> Path:
    42│     return (paths or config.DATA).datasets / _safe_name(name)
    43│ 
    44│ 
    45│ # --- Perceptual hash (dhash, 64-bit) --------------------------------------------------
    46│ 
    47│ def dhash(img, size: int = 8) -> int:
    48│     """Difference-Hash: Bild auf (size+1 x size) grau, horizontale Nachbardifferenzen -> 64-bit."""
    49│     import cv2
    50│ 
    51│     g = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) if img.ndim == 3 else img
    52│     r = cv2.resize(g, (size + 1, size), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    53│     diff = r[:, 1:] > r[:, :-1]
    54│     bits = 0
    55│     for v in diff.flatten():
    56│         bits = (bits << 1) | int(bool(v))
    57│     return bits
    58│ 
    59│ 
    60│ def _hamming(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    61│     return bin(a ^ b).count("1")
    62│ 
    63│ 
    64│ # --- Dedup ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    65│ 
    66│ def dedup_metadata(rows: list[dict], cap: int | None, seed: int = config.SEED) -> list[dict]:
    67│     """Max. `cap` Crops je (session_id, square, label) behalten (seeded). cap<=0/None -> alle."""
    68│     if not cap or cap <= 0:
    69│         return list(rows)
    70│     rng = random.Random(seed)
    71│     groups: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    72│     for r in rows:
    73│         groups.setdefault((r["session_id"], r["square"], r["label"]), []).append(r)
    74│     kept: list[dict] = []
    75│     for g in groups.values():
    76│         if len(g) > cap:
    77│             g = sorted(g, key=lambda r: str(r.get("frame", "")))   # deterministisch
    78│             g = rng.sample(g, cap)
    79│         kept.extend(g)
    80│     return kept
    81│ 
    82│ 
    83│ def dedup_phash(rows: list[dict], hamming: int) -> list[dict]:
    84│     """Innerhalb jeder Klasse visuell fast gleiche Crops verwerfen (dhash, Hamming <= Schwelle)."""
    85│     import cv2
    86│ 
    87│     if hamming is None or hamming < 0:
    88│         return list(rows)
    89│     by_label: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    90│     for r in rows:
    91│         by_label.setdefault(r["label"], []).append(r)
    92│     kept: list[dict] = []
    93│     for g in by_label.values():

    95│         for r in sorted(g, key=lambda r: (str(r.get("session_id")), str(r.get("frame")), r.get("square", ""))):

    97│             if img is None:
    98│                 kept.append(r)                  # nicht lesbar -> behalten, nicht still verlieren
    99│                 continue
   100│             h = dhash(img)

   102│                 continue                        # zu ähnlich -> verwerfen
   103│             seen.append(h)
   104│             kept.append(r)
   105│     return kept
   106│

   112│     90/180/270 werden als neue Dateien unter `squares_dir/<label>/` materialisiert."""

   118│     out: list[dict] = []
   119│     for r in rows:

   122│             if deg == 0:
   123│                 nr["rot"] = 0
   124│                 out.append(nr)
   125│                 continue
   126│             img = cv2.imread(r["path"])

   129│             rimg = cv2.rotate(img, _ROT_CODES[deg])

   211│                                    force_train=force_train, precomputed_splits=splits)
   212│     errors, _warnings = dataset_mod.validate_split(split, rows)

     1│ """Stufe 7 (Teil 1) — geteilte photometrische Aufbereitung.

     3│ Layout: pro Sample `<id>.png` + `<id>.json` (in Unterordnern `train/val/test`). Jede JSON enthält:
     4│ - `corners`: 4 [x,y]-Bildpunkte der Brettecken, **ungeordnet** (chesscog sortiert sie selbst).
     5│ - `fen`: vollständige FEN.
     6│ - `white_turn`: bool — die Render-Perspektive ist die des ziehenden Spielers, d. h. bei `True` steht
     7│   **Weiß unten** (geometrisch oben-links = a8), bei `False` ist das Brett um 180° gedreht.
     8│ 
     9│ Wir sortieren die Ecken geometrisch zu `[TL, TR, BR, BL]` und mappen je nach `white_turn` auf unsere
    10│ Reihenfolge `[a8, h8, h1, a1]`. **Vor dem großen Pretrain mit `--debug-overlay` prüfen** — sitzt die
    11│ Orientierung falsch (gespiegelte Labels), ist `white_turn` invers zu interpretieren (eine Zeile).
    12│ """
    13│ 
    14│ from __future__ import annotations
    15│ 
    16│ import json
    17│ from collections.abc import Iterator
    18│ from pathlib import Path
    19│ 
    20│ from ..ingest import ImportItem
    21│ 
    22│ 
    23│ def sort_corner_points(pts) -> list[list[float]]:
    24│     """4 Punkte → `[top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left]` (Bildkoordinaten, robust über
    25│     Summe/Differenz — rotationsstabil für nicht-degenerierte Vierecke)."""
    26│     p = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in pts]
    27│     tl = min(p, key=lambda q: q[0] + q[1])
    28│     br = max(p, key=lambda q: q[0] + q[1])
    29│     tr = max(p, key=lambda q: q[0] - q[1])
    30│     bl = min(p, key=lambda q: q[0] - q[1])
    31│     return [list(tl), list(tr), list(br), list(bl)]
    32│ 
    33│ 
    34│ def order_corners(corners, white_turn: bool) -> list[list[float]]:
    35│     """Geometrisch sortierte Ecken → unsere Reihenfolge `[a8, h8, h1, a1]`.
    36│     Weiß unten: `[TL,TR,BR,BL] == [a8,h8,h1,a1]`. Schwarz unten: um 180° gedreht."""
    37│     s = sort_corner_points(corners)            # [TL, TR, BR, BL]
    38│     if white_turn:
    39│         return s
    40│     return s[2:] + s[:2]                        # 180°: [BR, BL, TL, TR] == [a8, h8, h1, a1]

    44│     root = Path(root)

    52│             d = json.loads(jf.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    53│             corners = d["corners"]
    54│             fen = d["fen"]
    55│             white = bool(d.get("white_turn", True))
    56│         except (KeyError, ValueError, OSError):
    57│             continue
    58│         if not corners or len(corners) != 4:
    59│             continue
    60│         yield ImportItem(image_path=img, corners=order_corners(corners, white), fen=fen,
    61│                          group=f"chesscog-{jf.parent.name}", meta={"white_turn": white})

1	"""Stage 4 — named, curated datasets.
     2	
     3	A **dataset** is a view on the global crop pool (`data/manifests/squares.jsonl`):
     4	a selection of sessions + dedup and split policy. Building creates under
     5	`data/datasets/<name>/` a filtered, deduplicated `manifest.jsonl`, a
     6	session-based `split.json` and `stats.json`. Crops for rot=0 reference the global
     7	pool (no copying); only rotation-augmented crops are materialized in the dataset folder.
     8	
     9	Dedup against the recording-induced surplus of nearly identical crops (never-moved pieces on
    10	fixed camera):
    11	  1. Metadata cap per `(session_id, square, label)` — fast, deterministic.
    12	  2. Perceptual hash (dhash) — discards visually near-duplicates within a class.
    13	
    14	Rotation augmentation (90/180/270°) is optional and deliberately AFTER dedup (4x the
    15	*curated* crops). It contradicts the fixed-camera assumption (CLAUDE.md) and is a toggle.
    16	Testable headless: all functions take `paths=config.DATA`.
    17	"""
    18	
    19	from __future__ import annotations
    20	
    21	import json
    22	import random
    23	import shutil
    24	from collections import Counter
    25	from datetime import UTC, datetime
    26	from pathlib import Path

    34	def _safe_name(name: str) -> str:
    35	    n = (name or "").strip()
    36	    if not n or "/" in n or "\\" in n or ".." in n:
    37	        raise ValueError(f"invalid dataset name: {name!r}")
    38	    return n
    39	
    40	
    41	def dataset_dir(name: str, paths: config.Paths | None = None) -> Path:
    42	    return (paths or config.DATA).datasets / _safe_name(name)
    43	
    44	
    45	# --- Perceptual hash (dhash, 64-bit) --------------------------------------------------
    46	
    47	def dhash(img, size: int = 8) -> int:
    48	    """Difference-Hash: Bild auf (size+1 x size) grau, horizontale Nachbardifferenzen -> 64-bit."""
    49	    import cv2
    50	
    51	    g = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) if img.ndim == 3 else img
    52	    r = cv2.resize(g, (size + 1, size), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    53	    diff = r[:, 1:] > r[:, :-1]
    54	    bits = 0
    55	    for v in diff.flatten():
    56	        bits = (bits << 1) | int(bool(v))
    57	    return bits
    58	
    59	
    60	def _hamming(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    61	    return bin(a ^ b).count("1")
    62	
    63	
    64	# --- Dedup ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    65	
    66	def dedup_metadata(rows: list[dict], cap: int | None, seed: int = config.SEED) -> list[dict]:
    67	    """Max. `cap` Crops je (session_id, square, label) behalten (seeded). cap<=0/None -> alle."""
    68	    if not cap or cap <= 0:
    69	        return list(rows)
    70	    rng = random.Random(seed)
    71	    groups: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    72	    for r in rows:
    73	        groups.setdefault((r["session_id"], r["square"], r["label"]), []).append(r)
    74	    kept: list[dict] = []
    75	    for g in groups.values():
    76	        if len(g) > cap:
    77	            g = sorted(g, key=lambda r: str(r.get("frame", "")))   # deterministisch
    78	            g = rng.sample(g, cap)
    79	        kept.extend(g)

content.content:
"""Adapter for the **chesscog** rendered dataset (Wölflein & Bringmann, OSF DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/XF3KA).

Layout: per sample `<id>.png` + `<id>.json` (in subdirectories `train/val/test`). Each JSON contains:
- `corners`: 4 [x,y] image points of the board corners, **unordered** (chesscog sorts them itself).
- `fen`: full FEN.
- `white_turn`: bool — the render perspective is that of the player to move, i.e. when `True` **White is
  at the bottom** (geometrically top-left = a8), when `False` the board is rotated 180°.

We sort the corners geometrically to `[TL, TR, BR, BL]` and depending on `white_turn` map to our
order `[a8, h8, h1, a1]`. **Verify with `--debug-overlay` before large pretrain** — if the
orientation is wrong (reflected labels), then `white_turn` should be interpreted inversely (one line).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path

from ..ingest import ImportItem


def sort_corner_points(pts) -> list[list[float]]:
    """4 points → `[top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left]` (image coordinates, robust via
    sum/difference — rotation-stable for non-degenerate quadrilaterals)."""
    p = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in pts]
    tl = min(p, key=lambda q: q[0] + q[1])
    br = max(p, key=lambda q: q[0] + q[1])
    tr = max(p, key=lambda q: q[0] - q[1])
    bl = min(p, key=lambda q: q[0] - q[1])
    return [list(tl), list(tr), list(br), list(bl)]


def order_corners(corners, white_turn: bool) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Geometrisch sortierte Ecken → unsere Reihenfolge `[a8, h8, h1, a1]`.
    Weiß unten: `[TL,TR,BR,BL] == [a8,h8,h1,a1]`. Schwarz unten: um 180° gedreht."""
    s = sort_corner_points(corners)            # [TL, TR, BR, BL]
    if white_turn:
        return s
    return s[2:] + s[:2]                        # 180°: [BR, BL, TL, TR] == [a8, h8, h1, a1]


def iter_items(root: Path) -> Iterator[ImportItem]:
    root = Path(root)
    for jf in sorted(root.rglob("*.json")):
        if "__MACOSX" in jf.parts or jf.name.startswith("._"):
            continue                       # skip AppleDouble junk from Mac zips
        img = jf.with_suffix(".png")
        if not img.exists():
            continue
        try:
            d = json.loads(jf.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            corners = d["corners"]
            fen = d["fen"]
            white = bool(d.get("white_turn", True))
        except (KeyError, ValueError, OSError):
            continue
        if not corners or len(corners) != 4:
            continue
        yield ImportItem(image_path=img, corners=order_corners(corners, white), fen=fen,
                         group=f"chesscog-{jf.parent.name}", meta={"white_turn": white})

"""Typer entrypoint. One CLI `chesslab`; each stage adds its own subcommands."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import typer

from . import calibration as calibration_mod
from . import collect as collect_mod
from . import config
from . import dataset as dataset_mod
from . import doctor as doctor_mod
from . import labeling as labeling_mod

app = typer.Typer(
    name="chesslab",
    help="Build an auto-labeled chess-piece dataset and train a per-square model.",
    no_args_is_help=True,
    add_completion=False,
)

calibrate_app = typer.Typer(help="Stage 1 — Calibrate camera/board geometry.", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(calibrate_app, name="calibrate")

collect_app = typer.Typer(help="Stage 3 — Capture positions (raw frame + FEN into session log).", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(collect_app, name="collect")

dataset_app = typer.Typer(help="Stage 4 — Dataset consistency.", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(dataset_app, name="dataset")

experiment_app = typer.Typer(help="Stage 7 — Geometry×Photometry bake-off.", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(experiment_app, name="experiment")

synth_app = typer.Typer(help="Synthetic data pipeline (Blender renderer).", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(synth_app, name="synth")


@app.callback()
def _root() -> None:
    """chesslab — staged tool; each stage adds subcommands. See `chesslab --help`."""


@app.command()
def doctor(
    gpu: bool = typer.Option(False, "--gpu", help="Also run ROCm/PyTorch GPU validation (required before training)."),
    camera: int | None = typer.Option(None, "--camera", help="Camera check for index N (open + read one frame)."),
    json_out: bool = typer.Option(False, "--json", help="Also output machine-readable JSON report."),
) -> None:
    """Pre-flight: validate Python, app deps, optional GPU (ROCm) and camera."""
    code = doctor_mod.run(gpu=gpu, camera=camera, json_out=json_out)
    raise typer.Exit(code)


@calibrate_app.command("check")
def calibrate_check(
    profile: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PROFILE, "--profile", help="Profile name."),
    camera: int = typer.Option(0, "--camera", help="Camera index."),
) -> None:
    """Live overlay of the 8×8 grid on the camera image for visual inspection."""
    raise typer.Exit(calibration_mod.calibrate_check(camera=camera, profile=profile))


@calibrate_app.command("list")
def calibrate_list() -> None:
    """List existing calibration profiles."""
    raise typer.Exit(calibration_mod.calibrate_list())


@calibrate_app.command("markers")
def calibrate_markers(
    out: str = typer.Option("data/calibration/markers.png", "--out", help="Target PNG of the marker sheet."),
    dict_name: str = typer.Option("DICT_4X4_50", "--dict", help="ArUco-Dictionary."),
    marker_px: int = typer.Option(300, "--marker-px"),
) -> None:
    """Generate printable ArUco marker sheet (glue onto a8/h8/h1/a1)."""
    p = calibration_mod.generate_markers(out, dict_name=dict_name, marker_px=marker_px)
    print(f"[OK] Marker sheet: {p} — print out, cut out, glue one marker centered on each "
          "corner a8/h8/h1/a1. Then run `chesslab calibrate auto`.")


@calibrate_app.command("auto")
def calibrate_auto(
    camera: int = typer.Option(0, "--camera"),
    profile: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PROFILE, "--profile"),
    board_size: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_BOARD_SIZE, "--board-size"),
    dict_name: str = typer.Option("DICT_4X4_50", "--dict"),
    margin: float = typer.Option(0.06, "--margin", help="Fraction by which markers sit OUTSIDE the board (adjust live in --preview with w/e)."),
    min_markers: int = typer.Option(4, "--min-markers", help="Required markers (4 = robust; 2/3 only useful with top-down camera)."),
    preview: bool = typer.Option(False, "--preview", help="Show marker box + board box live (adjust with w/e, s=save)."),
) -> None:
    """Auto-calibrate via ArUco markers (markers outside, board inset; no clicking)."""
    raise typer.Exit(calibration_mod.calibrate_auto(camera=camera, profile=profile, board_size=board_size,
                                                    dict_name=dict_name, margin=margin, preview=preview,
                                                    min_markers=min_markers))


@collect_app.command("pgn")
def collect_pgn(
    pgn: str = typer.Option(..., "--pgn", help="PGN file."),
    profile: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PROFILE, "--profile"),
    camera: int = typer.Option(0, "--camera"),
    every: int = typer.Option(1, "--every", help="Only capture every Nth half-move."),
    session: str = typer.Option(None, "--session", help="Session ID (default: timestamp)."),
    ui: bool = typer.Option(False, "--ui", help="Show live dashboard (Stage 6)."),
    target: int = typer.Option(config.UI_TARGET_PER_CLASS, "--target", help="Target samples per class (UI)."),
) -> None:
    """PGN replay: physically replay a game, capture after each half-move."""
    raise typer.Exit(collect_mod.collect_pgn(pgn=pgn, profile=profile, camera=camera, every=every,
                                             session=session, ui=ui, target=target))


@collect_app.command("live")
def collect_live(
    start_fen: str = typer.Option(None, "--start-fen", help="Starting position as FEN (otherwise initial position)."),
    profile: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PROFILE, "--profile"),
    camera: int = typer.Option(0, "--camera"),
    session: str = typer.Option(None, "--session"),
    ui: bool = typer.Option(False, "--ui", help="Show live dashboard (Stage 6)."),
    target: int = typer.Option(config.UI_TARGET_PER_CLASS, "--target", help="Target samples per class (UI)."),
) -> None:
    """Free play: type move (SAN/UCI), then capture."""
    raise typer.Exit(collect_mod.collect_live(start_fen=start_fen, profile=profile, camera=camera,
                                              session=session, ui=ui, target=target))


@collect_app.command("play")
def collect_play(
    strategy: str = typer.Option("random", "--strategy", help="random | stockfish | coverage | sweep"),
    max_plies: int = typer.Option(40, "--max-plies", help="Max. half-moves of the generated game (random/stockfish)."),
    seed: int = typer.Option(config.SEED, "--seed", help="Seed for strategy=random."),
    stockfish_path: str = typer.Option(None, "--stockfish-path", help="Path to the UCI binary (for stockfish)."),
    start_fen: str = typer.Option(None, "--start-fen", help="Starting position (otherwise initial position)."),
    profile: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PROFILE, "--profile"),
    camera: int = typer.Option(0, "--camera"),
    session: str = typer.Option(None, "--session"),
    ui: bool = typer.Option(False, "--ui", help="Show live dashboard (Stage 6)."),
    target: int = typer.Option(config.UI_TARGET_PER_CLASS, "--target"),
    sets: int = typer.Option(1, "--sets", help="Number of physical piece sets (coverage/sweep): ×N per class."),
    count: int = typer.Option(20, "--count", help="Number of dense setups (only strategy=coverage)."),
    passes: int = typer.Option(1, "--passes", help="sweep: repetitions per color (per pass 8 photos)."),
    pieces: str = typer.Option("special", "--pieces", help="sweep: special | pawn | all."),
    together: bool = typer.Option(False, "--together", help="sweep: both colors simultaneously (half the photo count)."),
    offset: int = typer.Option(0, "--offset", help="sweep: shift rank→piece mapping (0..7)."),
    auto_offset: bool = typer.Option(False, "--auto-offset", help="sweep: offset automatically (cycled across sessions)."),
) -> None:
    """Engine plays the game (random/stockfish), coverage: dense setups targeting rare classes,
    or sweep: piece row systematically moves across the board. You reposition and photograph."""
    raise typer.Exit(collect_mod.collect_play(strategy=strategy, max_plies=max_plies, seed=seed,
                                              stockfish_path=stockfish_path, start_fen=start_fen,
                                              profile=profile, camera=camera, session=session,
                                              ui=ui, target=target, sets=sets, count=count,
                                              passes=passes, pieces=pieces, together=together,
                                              offset=offset, auto_offset=auto_offset))


@app.command("ui")
def ui_cmd(
    sessions: str = typer.Option(None, "--sessions", help="Sessions directory (default: data/sessions)."),
    manifest: str = typer.Option(None, "--manifest", help="Optional manifest (informational only)."),
    target: int = typer.Option(config.UI_TARGET_PER_CLASS, "--target"),
) -> None:
    """Stage 6 — Training data dashboard standalone (without active capture)."""
    from .collect_ui import run_ui

    raise typer.Exit(run_ui(sessions_dir=sessions, manifest=manifest, target_per_class=target))


@app.command("slice")
def slice_cmd(
    session: str = typer.Option(None, "--session", help="Slice session ID."),
    all_sessions: bool = typer.Option(False, "--all", help="Slice all sessions."),
    profile: str = typer.Option(None, "--profile", help="Override profile (default: from session.yaml)."),
    pad_up: float = typer.Option(None, "--pad-up", help="Override crop height upward."),
    pad_side: float = typer.Option(None, "--pad-side", help="Override side crop extension."),
    out_size: str = typer.Option(None, "--out-size", help="Crop size WxH, e.g. 96x128."),
    preview: str = typer.Option(None, "--preview", help="Session ID: visually check label vs crop."),
    geometry: str = typer.Option("warp", "--geometry", help="Crop geometry: warp | box3d."),
    photometry: str = typer.Option("none", "--photometry", help="Filter: none | clahe | grayworld | gamma."),
    piece_height: float = typer.Option(config.EXP_PIECE_HEIGHT_CELLS, "--piece-height",
                                       help="box3d: extrusion height in cells."),
    variant_tag: str = typer.Option(None, "--variant-tag",
                                    help="Store crops/manifest with variant tag (squares__<tag>/)."),
) -> None:
    """Session logs -> 64 labeled square crops per position + manifest."""
    raise typer.Exit(labeling_mod.run_slice(
        session=session, slice_all=all_sessions, profile=profile,
        pad_up=pad_up, pad_side=pad_side, out_size=out_size, preview=preview,
        geometry_mode=geometry, photometry=photometry, piece_height_cells=piece_height,
        variant_tag=variant_tag,
    ))


def _csv_list(s: str) -> list[str]:
    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(",") if x.strip()]


@experiment_app.command("run")
def experiment_run(
    sessions: str = typer.Option(..., "--sessions", help="Comma-separated session IDs."),
    geometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.EXP_GEOMETRIES), "--geometries", help="e.g. warp,box3d."),
    photometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.PHOTOMETRY_METHODS), "--photometries",
                                     help="e.g. none,clahe,grayworld,gamma."),
    heads: str = typer.Option("combined", "--heads", help="Model heads: combined,factored,twostage."),
    epochs: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_EPOCHS, "--epochs"),
    seed: int = typer.Option(config.SEED, "--seed"),
    backbone: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_BACKBONE, "--backbone"),
    eval_split: str = typer.Option("test", "--eval-split", help="Metric split: test | val (val for <3 sessions)."),
    force: bool = typer.Option(False, "--force", help="All stages fresh (otherwise skip completed ones)."),
) -> None:
    """Full grid train Geometry×Photometry×Head + comparison table by board accuracy."""
    from . import experiment as experiment_mod

    raise typer.Exit(experiment_mod.run_experiment(
        _csv_list(sessions), _csv_list(geometries), _csv_list(photometries), _csv_list(heads),
        epochs=epochs, seed=seed, backbone=backbone, eval_split=eval_split, force=force))


@experiment_app.command("table")
def experiment_table(
    sessions: str = typer.Option(..., "--sessions", help="Comma-separated session IDs."),
    geometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.EXP_GEOMETRIES), "--geometries"),
    photometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.PHOTOMETRY_METHODS), "--photometries"),
    heads: str = typer.Option("combined", "--heads"),
    eval_split: str = typer.Option("test", "--eval-split"),
) -> None:
    """Rebuild comparison table from already-trained runs (no re-training)."""
    from . import experiment as experiment_mod

    raise typer.Exit(experiment_mod.rebuild_table(
        _csv_list(sessions), _csv_list(geometries), _csv_list(photometries), _csv_list(heads),
        eval_split=eval_split))


@experiment_app.command("list")
def experiment_list(
    sessions: str = typer.Option("", "--sessions", help="(optional, irrelevant for table columns)."),
    geometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.EXP_GEOMETRIES), "--geometries"),
    photometries: str = typer.Option(",".join(config.PHOTOMETRY_METHODS), "--photometries"),
    heads: str = typer.Option("combined", "--heads"),
) -> None:
    """Status per variant: sliced / dataset / train / eval."""
    from . import experiment as experiment_mod

    raise typer.Exit(experiment_mod.variant_status(
        _csv_list(sessions), _csv_list(geometries), _csv_list(photometries), _csv_list(heads)))


@app.command("stats")
def stats_cmd(
    manifest: str = typer.Option(None, "--manifest", help="Manifest path (default: data/manifests/squares.jsonl)."),
    json_out: bool = typer.Option(False, "--json"),
) -> None:
    """Dataset report: 13-class distribution + light/dark coverage + warnings."""
    raise typer.Exit(dataset_mod.run_stats(manifest=manifest, json_out=json_out))


@app.command("split")
def split_cmd(
    val_frac: float = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_VAL_FRAC, "--val-frac"),
    test_frac: float = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_TEST_FRAC, "--test-frac"),
    max_empty_ratio: float = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_MAX_EMPTY_RATIO, "--max-empty-ratio"),
    max_class_ratio: float | None = typer.Option(None, "--max-class-ratio", help="Cap each piece class at R * smallest class (balances pawns downward; train only)."),
    seed: int = typer.Option(config.SEED, "--seed"),
    allow_degenerate: bool = typer.Option(False, "--allow-degenerate", help="Allow degenerate split (class only in one session etc.)."),
) -> None:
    """Session-based split (against data leakage) + class balancing (train only) -> split.json."""
    raise typer.Exit(dataset_mod.run_split(val_frac=val_frac, test_frac=test_frac,
                                           max_empty_ratio=max_empty_ratio, seed=seed,
                                           max_class_ratio=max_class_ratio,
                                           allow_degenerate=allow_degenerate))


@dataset_app.command("verify")
def dataset_verify() -> None:
    """Consistency checks: files exist/loadable, out_size, labels, split disjointness."""
    raise typer.Exit(dataset_mod.run_verify())


@app.command("ingest")
def ingest_cmd(
    adapter: str = typer.Argument(..., help="chesscog | chessred | synthetic (external/synthetic dataset)."),
    root: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Path to locally extracted dataset."),
    tag: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--tag", help="Name for sessions/dataset (default: pretrain-<adapter>)."),
    geometry: str = typer.Option("warp", "--geometry", help="warp (recommended, no intrinsics) | box3d."),
    photometry: str = typer.Option("none", "--photometry", help="none | clahe | grayworld | gamma — must match the finetune dataset."),
    board_size: int = typer.Option(900, "--board-size", help="Warp resolution (px). Keep moderate (phone source), otherwise upscale blur."),
    limit: int | None = typer.Option(None, "--limit", help="Only the first N images (quick test)."),
    debug_overlay: int = typer.Option(0, "--debug-overlay", help="Warp N frames + overlay FEN labels (visual check against label swapping)."),
    no_build: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-build", help="Only slice, don't build a dataset."),
) -> None:
    """Ingest external dataset (chesscog/ChessReD2K) into our crop format -> pretrain dataset.

    Afterwards: `chesslab train --dataset <tag> --head twostage --backbone mobilenet_v3_small`, then on
    your own sessions `train --dataset <yours> --resume <pretrain-run>`. IMPORTANT: before the big
    run with `--debug-overlay 8` check orientation (wrong corners silently swap all labels)."""
    from . import ingest as ingest_mod

    t = tag or f"pretrain-{adapter.lower()}"
    try:
        summary = ingest_mod.run_ingest(
            adapter, root, tag=t, geometry=geometry, photometry=photometry, board_size=board_size,
            limit=limit, debug_overlay_n=debug_overlay, build=not no_build)
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
        print(f"[FAIL] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    print(f"[OK] {summary['adapter']}: {summary['items']} images, {summary['sessions']} sessions, "
          f"{summary['crops']} crops -> {summary['manifest']}")
    if summary.get("overlays"):
        print(f"[OK] Visual check: {len(summary['overlays'])} overlay PNGs in "
              f"{Path(summary['overlays'][0]).parent} — please review BEFORE starting the big pretrain.")
    if summary.get("dataset"):
        print(f"[OK] Dataset '{summary['dataset']}' built: {summary.get('dataset_counts')}")
    raise typer.Exit(0)


@dataset_app.command("build")
def dataset_build_cmd(
    name: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Name of the dataset."),
    sessions: str = typer.Option(..., "--sessions", help="Comma-separated session IDs."),
    per_cell_cap: int = typer.Option(config.DEDUP.per_cell_cap, "--cap", help="Max. crops per (session,square,piece)."),
    no_phash: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-phash", help="Disable perceptual hash dedup."),
    hamming: int = typer.Option(config.DEDUP.phash_hamming, "--hamming"),
    rotate: bool = typer.Option(True, "--rotate/--no-rotate", help="90/180/270°-Augmentation (default on)."),
    allow_degenerate: bool = typer.Option(False, "--allow-degenerate", help="Allow degenerate dataset (class only in one session etc.)."),
) -> None:
    """Build named dataset from session selection (filter -> dedup -> rotation -> split)."""
    from . import dataset_build as db

    sids = [s.strip() for s in sessions.split(",") if s.strip()]
    try:
        res = db.build_dataset(name, sids, per_cell_cap=per_cell_cap, phash_enabled=not no_phash,
                               phash_hamming=hamming, rotations=(config.DEDUP.rotations if rotate else (0,)),
                               allow_degenerate=allow_degenerate)
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"[FAIL] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    c = res["counts"]
    print(f"[OK] Dataset '{res['name']}': raw {c['raw']} -> dedup {c['after_dedup']} -> "
          f"final {c['final']}. Split: {res['split_counts']}.")
    for w in res["warnings"]:
        print(f"  ! {w}")


@dataset_app.command("list")
def dataset_list_cmd() -> None:
    """List existing datasets."""
    from . import dataset_build as db

    for d in db.list_datasets():
        print(f"{d['name']}: {d['n_sessions']} sessions, {d['counts'].get('final', '?')} crops, "
              f"split {d.get('split_counts', {})}")


@dataset_app.command("delete")
def dataset_delete_cmd(name: str = typer.Argument(...)) -> None:
    """Delete dataset (raw material/sessions remain)."""
    from . import dataset_build as db

    db.delete_dataset(name)
    print(f"[OK] Dataset '{name}' deleted.")


@app.command("train")
def train_cmd(
    backbone: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_BACKBONE, "--backbone", help="smallcnn | mobilenet_v3_small"),
    epochs: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_EPOCHS, "--epochs"),
    batch_size: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, "--batch-size"),
    lr: float = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_LR, "--lr"),
    no_amp: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-amp", help="Disable AMP/autocast."),
    seed: int = typer.Option(config.SEED, "--seed"),
    out: str = typer.Option(None, "--out", help="Run directory (default: data/models/run-<ts>)."),
    patience: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_PATIENCE, "--patience", help="Early stopping patience."),
    num_workers: int | None = typer.Option(None, "--num-workers", help="DataLoader workers (default: 0 on Windows, 4 otherwise)."),
    norm: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--norm", help="batchnorm | groupnorm | none (default: groupnorm on Windows, otherwise batchnorm)."),
    dataset: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--dataset", help="Named dataset (otherwise global manifest/split)."),
    resume: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--resume", help="Run name whose weights are loaded as warm-start (continue training)."),
    head: str = typer.Option("combined", "--head", help="combined | factored | twostage (two-stage Occupancy→Piece)."),
) -> None:
    """Train per-square CNN on the ROCm GPU (board accuracy = checkpoint metric)."""
    from .training.train import run_train

    raise typer.Exit(run_train(backbone=backbone, epochs=epochs, batch_size=batch_size, lr=lr,
                               no_amp=no_amp, seed=seed, out=out, patience=patience,
                               num_workers=num_workers, norm=norm, dataset=dataset, resume=resume,
                               head=head))


@app.command("eval")
def eval_cmd(
    run: str = typer.Option(..., "--run", help="Run directory from `train`."),
    split: str = typer.Option("test", "--split", help="train | val | test"),
) -> None:
    """Board accuracy, per-class recall and confusion matrix (text + PNG)."""
    from .training.evaluate import run_eval

    raise typer.Exit(run_eval(run=run, split_name=split))


@app.command("export")
def export_cmd(
    run: str = typer.Option(..., "--run", help="Run directory from `train`."),
    fmt: str = typer.Option("torchscript", "--format", help="torchscript | onnx | all"),
) -> None:
    """Export best.pt to TorchScript/ONNX + model_card.json (handoff to inference app)."""
    from .training.evaluate import run_export

    raise typer.Exit(run_export(run=run, fmt=fmt))


@app.command("web")
def web_cmd(
    host: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_WEB_HOST, "--host"),
    port: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_WEB_PORT, "--port"),
    source: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--source",
        help="Camera source as URL instead of local index (e.g. IP/phone cam "
             "https://host:4444/video/m.jpeg). Overrides the UI index for ALL camera paths. "
             "Use the MJPEG stream for smooth preview."),
    capture_source: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--capture-source",
        help="Optional HIGH-RESOLUTION snapshot URL for saving (e.g. "
             "https://host:4444/video/snapshot). Preview stays on the smooth --source stream, "
             "saved frames come sharp from the snapshot (corners re-detected on it)."),
) -> None:
    """Local web UI: browse dataset, relabel, control training (requires `--extra web`)."""
    import os

    from .web.camera import CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENV, CAMERA_SOURCE_ENV

    if source:
        os.environ[CAMERA_SOURCE_ENV] = source   # read by web camera path (effective_source)
        print(f"Camera source (preview): {source}")
    if capture_source:
        os.environ[CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENV] = capture_source
        print(f"Capture source (save, high-resolution): {capture_source}")

    from .web.app import run as run_web

    raise typer.Exit(run_web(host=host, port=port))


@app.command("track")
def track_cmd(
    profile: str = typer.Option("phone", "--profile", help="chesslab calibration profile."),
    source: str = typer.Option("0", "--source", help="Camera: 0=Webcam, URL=IP-Cam."),
    host: str = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_TRACK_HOST, "--host"),
    port: int = typer.Option(config.DEFAULT_TRACK_PORT, "--port"),
    motion_thr: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["motion_thr"], "--motion-thr",
                                     help="Motion threshold for motion gating."),
    z_thr: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["z_thr"], "--z-thr",
                                help="z-score threshold above which a square counts as changed."),
    ambiguity_margin_ll: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["ambiguity_margin_ll"],
                                              "--ambiguity-margin",
                                              help="Minimum distance best−second (LL units)."),
    reanchor_ll_floor: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["reanchor_ll_floor"],
                                            "--reanchor-floor",
                                            help="Re-anchor only when best move LL is below it."),
    nudge_timeout_s: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["nudge_timeout_s"], "--nudge-timeout",
                                          help="Seconds until nudge reference patch (without CNN)."),
    drift_window_s: float = typer.Option(config.TRACK_DEFAULTS["drift_window_s"], "--drift-window",
                                         help="Seconds until drift patch of empty squares (without CNN)."),

@synth_app.command("render")
def synth_render(
    out: str = typer.Option(..., "--out", help="Target directory (required)."),
    blend: str = typer.Option(None, "--blend", help="Blender scene (default: synth_assets/Chess Scene.blend)."),
    pieces_dir: str = typer.Option(None, "--pieces-dir", help="Scanned piece templates (default: synth_pieces/)."),
    board_texture: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--board-texture",
                                             help="Rectified board photo texture (default: synth_pieces/board_texture.png"
                                                  " if present, otherwise procedural wood)."),
    n: int = typer.Option(200, "--n", help="Number of positions to render."),
    seed: int = typer.Option(42, "--seed"),
    fens: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--fens", help="FEN list (otherwise fallback starting position)."),
    res: int = typer.Option(1024, "--res", help="Render resolution (px)."),
    views_per_scene: int = typer.Option(1, "--views-per-scene",
                                        help="Views (camera+light) per piece setup. >1 = scene reuse: "
                                             "render same scene multiple times -> significantly faster."),
    samples: int = typer.Option(24, "--samples", help="EEVEE TAA render samples (lower = faster)."),
    max_obliqueness: float = typer.Option(0.20, "--max-obliqueness",
                                          help="Max camera obliqueness (offset/height). Matched to real ~0.06 top-down "
                                               "camera; image is reprojected to top-down via homography during ingest."),
    blender: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--blender", help="Blender executable (default: blender, via CHESSLAB_BLENDER)."),
) -> None:
    """Generate synthetic board renderings with Blender/EEVEE (v2: board texture + procedural fallback)."""
    import subprocess

    from .config import SYNTH, build_blender_cmd

    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    script = repo_root / "synth" / "render_board_v2.py"

    b = Path(blend) if blend else SYNTH.blend
    p = Path(pieces_dir) if pieces_dir else SYNTH.pieces_dir if SYNTH.pieces_dir.exists() else None
    o = Path(out).resolve()
    fe = Path(fens).resolve() if fens else None
    bl = blender or SYNTH.blender_cmd()

    # Board texture: explicit --board-texture > default path (if present) > None (= procedural)
    bt: Path | None = None
    if board_texture:
        bt = Path(board_texture).resolve()
    elif SYNTH.board_texture.exists():
        bt = SYNTH.board_texture

    cmd = build_blender_cmd(bl, b, script, o, n=n, seed=seed, fens=fe, pieces=p, res=res,
                            board_texture=bt, views_per_scene=views_per_scene,
