@synth_app.command("prepare")
def synth_prepare_cmd(
    in_dir: str = typer.Option(..., "--in", help="Scans: each subfolder <piece>/ with .obj/.glb + texture."),
    out_dir: str = typer.Option(None, "--out", help="Target directory (default: synth_pieces/)."),
    target_tris: int = typer.Option(20000, "--target-tris", help="Target triangle count (0 = no decimation)."),
    smooth_iters: int = typer.Option(10, "--smooth-iters", help="Smoothing iterations (0 = none)."),
    fill_holes: bool = typer.Option(True, "--fill-holes/--no-fill-holes",
                                    help="Close open edges/base."),
) -> None:
    """Batch-prepare scanned pieces: upright, decimate, quality report + preview.

    Runs completely in-process (Open3D + PyMeshLab) — no Blender needed.
    Then check <out>/<piece>_preview.png and review the [WARN] hints."""
    from .config import SYNTH
    from .meshprep import prepare_scan
    from .scan_discover import assess_report, discover_scans

    out = Path(out_dir).resolve() if out_dir else SYNTH.pieces_dir

    items, warnings = discover_scans(Path(in_dir))
    for w in warnings:
        print(f"[WARN] {w}")
    if not items:
        print("[FAIL] no scans found (expected: <in>/<piece>/*.glb/.obj + texture).")
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    results: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
    for item in items:
        pid = f"{item.name}/{item.variant}"
        print(f"--- {pid}: {item.obj.name}" + (f" + {item.tex.name}" if item.tex else " (texture embedded)"))
        try:
            report = prepare_scan(item, out, make_preview=True)
        except Exception as e:
            results.append((pid, "fail", [str(e)]))
            continue
        level, msgs = assess_report(report)
        results.append((pid, level, msgs))
        print(f"    {report.get('tris', '?')} triangles, "
              f"holes/open: {report.get('boundary_edges', '?')}, height_ratio: {report.get('height_ratio', '?')}")

    print("\nSummary:")
    for pid, level, msgs in results:
        glyph = {"ok": "[OK]  ", "warn": "[WARN]", "fail": "[FAIL]"}[level]
        print(f"{glyph} {pid}" + ("" if not msgs else " — " + "; ".join(msgs)))
    print(f"\nView previews at: {out}\\<piece>\\<variant>_preview.png — then `chesslab synth render ...`")
    raise typer.Exit(1 if any(lv == "fail" for _, lv, _ in results) else 0)


@synth_app.command("board-texture")
def synth_board_texture(
    image: str = typer.Option(..., "--image", help="Board photo (JPG/PNG) with 4 ArUco markers at the corners."),
    out: str = typer.Option(None, "--out", help="Target path (default: synth_pieces/board_texture.png)."),
    size: int = typer.Option(1024, "--size", help="Square output size (px)."),
    dict_name: str = typer.Option("DICT_4X4_50", "--dict", help="ArUco-Dictionary."),
    margin: float = typer.Option(0.04, "--margin", help="Marker-to-grid inset (fraction)."),
) -> None:
    """Rectify board photo to rectified square texture (for `synth render --board-texture`)."""
    import sys as _sys

    from .config import _REPO_ROOT, SYNTH

    # synth/ lives in repo root (not an installed package) — retrofit for CLI invocation.
    if str(_REPO_ROOT) not in _sys.path:
        _sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))
    from synth.board_texture import rectify

    out_path = Path(out) if out else SYNTH.board_texture
    try:
        result = rectify(image, str(out_path), size=size, dict_name=dict_name, margin=margin)
        print(f"[OK] board-texture: {result}")
    except SystemExit as e:
        raise typer.Exit(e.code)


@synth_app.command("preview")
def synth_preview(
    obj: str = typer.Option(..., "--obj", help="Prepared piece (.obj, Z-up from `synth prepare`)."),
    out: str = typer.Option(..., "--out", help="Target PNG."),
    tex: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--tex", help="Texture PNG (default: <obj>.png alongside; --clay ignores it)."),
    clay: bool = typer.Option(False, "--clay", help="Render without texture (geometry only — bumps/holes most visible)."),
    blender: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--blender", help="Blender executable (default: auto-detected)."),
) -> None:
    """Render a single piece nicely (orthographic 3/4 view, upright, two light sources)."""
    import subprocess

    from .config import SYNTH

    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    script = repo_root / "synth" / "render_piece.py"
    obj_p = Path(obj).resolve()
    tex_p = None if clay else (Path(tex).resolve() if tex else obj_p.with_suffix(".png"))
    if tex_p is not None and not tex_p.exists():
        print(f"[WARN] Texture {tex_p} missing — rendering clay.")
        tex_p = None
    bl = blender or SYNTH.blender_cmd()
    cmd = [bl, "--background", "--python-exit-code", "1", "--python", str(script), "--",
           str(obj_p), str(Path(out).resolve()), str(tex_p) if tex_p else "-"]
    print(" ".join(cmd))
    try:
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"[FAIL] Blender not found ('{bl}'). Set CHESSLAB_BLENDER.")
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print("[FAIL] Render failed:\n" + "\n".join((e.stdout or "").splitlines()[-6:]))
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    print(f"[OK] synth preview: {out}")


def main() -> None:
    # Ensure non-ASCII report glyphs (—, umlauts) render on Windows consoles too.
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - best effort; default encoding is fine elsewhere
            pass
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    app()

# Architektur-Überblick — chess-vision / chesslab

Stand: 2026-07-02 · ~11.000 Zeilen Python (src + move_tracker + synth + tests) · Review-Basis: 4 parallele Subsystem-Analysen

## Mission & Systemkontext

`chesslab` ist ein **Datentool-Ökosystem** für Per-Square-Schachfigurenerkennung (14 Klassen inkl.
`occluded`) aus einer fest montierten Kamera. Labels entstehen automatisch aus dem bekannten
Spielzustand (FEN). Um den Kern haben sich drei Satelliten gebildet, die im ursprünglichen
Spec-Layout (CLAUDE.md) nicht vorgesehen waren:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Präsentation                                                      │
│  ├── CLI (typer, cli.py — ein Entrypoint `chesslab`)               │
│  ├── Web-UI (FastAPI + React/Vite SPA, src/chesslab/web/)          │
│  ├── OpenCV-Dashboard (collect_ui.py)                              │
│  └── move_tracker/ (eigenes FastAPI + HTML, PROTOTYP, außerhalb src)│
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Fachlogik (Kern-Pipeline, src/chesslab/)                          │
│  Stufe 0  doctor.py          Env-/ROCm-/Kamera-Validierung        │
│  Stufe 1  calibration.py     Homographie, ArUco, MarkerTracker    │
│  Stufe 2  state.py           Spielzustand (python-chess)          │
│  Stufe 3  collect.py, labeling.py, geometry3d.py, photometric.py  │
│  Stufe 4  dataset.py, dataset_build.py, sessions.py               │
│  Stufe 5  training/ (model, train, engine, evaluate, torch_data)  │
│  Stufe 7  experiment.py      Bake-off-Grids (Geometrie×Photometrie)│
│  NEU      ingest.py + ingest_adapters/ (chesscog, chessred, synth)│
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Daten / Infrastruktur                                             │
│  config.py (Klassenliste, Crop-/Augment-Policy, Paths)             │
│  data/ (sessions JSONL+YAML, squares, manifests JSONL, models)     │
│  synth/ (Blender-Renderpipeline) + synth_assets/ + synth_pieces/   │
│  wheels/ (gepinnte ROCm-Torch-Wheels für Windows)                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Datenfluss (Haupt-Contract-Kette)

```
Kamera ──► calibration (Profil-YAML: Homographie, Ecken, Crop-Params)
       ──► collect (Session: log.jsonl {frame, ply, fen, corners?, labels?} + session.yaml)
       ──► labeling.slice (Warp → 64 Crops → Label aus FEN) ──► manifest.jsonl
       ──► dataset (Stats, Balance, session-basierter Split → split.json)
       ──► training (SquareDataset → SmallCNN/MobileNetV3 → best.pt + config.json)
       ──► Konsumenten: web/inference.predict_arrays · move_tracker (geplant: CNN-Resync)

Parallel:  synth/ (RealityScan→Blender→PNG+JSON) ─┐
           chesscog / ChessReD (extern)          ─┼─► ingest_adapters → ingest.synthesize_sessions
                                                  ┘   → Pseudo-Sessions → gleicher slice-Pfad
```

Die Contracts sind **dateibasiert** (JSONL/YAML/JSON) — gut für Reproduzierbarkeit und Re-Slicing,
aber die Schemata sind nirgends formal dokumentiert (nur implizit in Writer-/Reader-Code).

## Subsysteme im Detail

**Kern-Pipeline** — sauber gestufte, weitgehend funktionale Module. `config.py` ist die einzige
Quelle für Klassenliste, Crop-Geometrie, Augment-Policy, Pfade (Prinzip „Konfig vor Code" wird
eingehalten). Headless-Kern (Geometrie, State, Stats) ist pur und testbar; Kamera/GUI-Kopplung
ist auf collect/calibration-Ränder beschränkt.

**Training** — SmallCNN (~100k Params) oder MobileNetV3-small (pretrained), drei Kopf-Varianten
(combined / factored / twostage mit explizitem Occupancy-Zweig), CrossEntropy mit Klassengewichten,
AdamW + Cosine, Early-Stopping auf `(macro_recall, board_acc)`. Split strikt pro Session.
Metriken: square_acc, macro_recall, board_acc (alle 64 Felder korrekt) plus Diagnose-Achsen
(occ_acc, piece_acc, type_err, color_err).

**Web-Layer** — FastAPI mit ~30 Endpoints (Kalibrieren, Sammeln, Scan, Manuell, Datensätze,
Training-Subprozess, Inference, MJPEG-Streams), React/Vite-SPA mit 8 Tabs, gebaute Assets werden
nach `web/static/` committet. Zustand liegt in vier modulglobalen Dicts (`_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`,
`_INFER`, `_MANUAL`) ohne Locks — funktioniert für den Single-User-Lokalbetrieb, ist aber die
größte strukturelle Schwäche des Layers.

**move_tracker/** — Prototyp auf Repo-Root-Ebene (bewusst außerhalb des Pakets). Sauberer
Konsument der chesslab-Library (calibration, web.camera), keine Logik-Duplikation. Erkennung:
Warp (live ArUco-nachgeführt) → Motion-Gate → Rolling-Average → Per-Feld-Diff mit
Median-Normalisierung → Scoring über alle legalen Züge → Ambiguitäts-Check →
Multi-Frame-Voting. Threading: Daemon-Capture-Loop + ein Lock um den geteilten Zustand.
Kein Test, keine Paketierung, kein Abstraktions-Seam für einen zweiten (CNN-)Beobachter.

**synth/** — vierstufige, manuell orchestrierte Blender-Pipeline (Turntable-Fotos → RealityScan →
isolate_piece → render_chessboard) mit hartkodierten relativen Pfaden; Ausgabe fließt über den
`synthetic`-Ingest-Adapter in die normale Slice-Pipeline.

## Test-Landschaft

13 Testdateien, ~89 Tests. Gut abgedeckt: Kern-Pipeline (calibration-Geometrie, state, collect,
labeling, dataset, dataset_build, doctor, ingest chesscog/chessred), Web-Routen teilweise
(TestClient). **Dunkel:** move_tracker (0 Tests), synth/synthetic-Adapter (0 Tests,
Datenintegritätsrisiko Ecken-Reihenfolge), web.camera/Streaming, CLI-Dispatch, GPU-Trainingsloop
(bewusst torch-gated).

## Gesamturteil

Die Kern-Pipeline ist für ein Ein-Personen-Datentool **überdurchschnittlich sauber** strukturiert
(Config-zentrisch, session-basierter Split, getrenntes collect/slice, Adapter-Pattern für Ingest).
Die Risiken konzentrieren sich an den **Rändern**: (1) Crop-/Photometrie-Geometrie ist über
Labeling-, Training- und Inference-Pfad dupliziert → Train/Serve-Skew, (2) Web-Layer-Globalzustand
und Fehlerverschlucken, (3) ungetestete neue Subsysteme (move_tracker, synth). Details in
[issues-and-concerns.md](issues-and-concerns.md), Verbesserungen in [recommendations.md](recommendations.md),
Training/Genauigkeit in [training-accuracy-improvements.md](training-accuracy-improvements.md).

# Architecture Overview — chess-vision / chesslab

Status: 2026-07-02 · ~11,000 lines Python (src + move_tracker + synth + tests) · Review basis: 4 parallel subsystem analyses

## Mission & System Context

`chesslab` is a **data-tool ecosystem** for per-square chess piece recognition (14 classes including
`occluded`) from a fixed-mounted camera. Labels are generated automatically from the known
game state (FEN). Around the core, three satellites have formed that were not foreseen in the original
spec layout (CLAUDE.md):

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Presentation                                                      │
│  ├── CLI (typer, cli.py — a single entrypoint `chesslab`)          │
│  ├── Web-UI (FastAPI + React/Vite SPA, src/chesslab/web/)          │
│  ├── OpenCV Dashboard (collect_ui.py)                              │
│  └── move_tracker/ (own FastAPI + HTML, PROTOTYPE, outside src)    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Domain Logic (Core Pipeline, src/chesslab/)                       │
│  Level 0  doctor.py          Env-/ROCm-/Camera Validation          │
│  Level 1  calibration.py     Homography, ArUco, MarkerTracker      │
│  Level 2  state.py           Game State (python-chess)             │
│  Level 3  collect.py, labeling.py, geometry3d.py, photometric.py   │
│  Level 4  dataset.py, dataset_build.py, sessions.py                │
│  Level 5  training/ (model, train, engine, evaluate, torch_data)   │
│  Level 7  experiment.py      Bake-off Grids (Geometry×Photometry)  │
│  NEW      ingest.py + ingest_adapters/ (chesscog, chessred, synth) │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Data / Infrastructure                                             │
│  config.py (class list, crop/augment policy, paths)                │
│  data/ (sessions JSONL+YAML, squares, manifests JSONL, models)     │
│  synth/ (Blender render pipeline) + synth_assets/ + synth_pieces/  │
│  wheels/ (pinned ROCm Torch wheels for Windows)                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Data Flow (Main Contract Chain)

```
Camera ──► calibration (profile YAML: homography, corners, crop params)
       ──► collect (session: log.jsonl {frame, ply, fen, corners?, labels?} + session.yaml)
       ──► labeling.slice (Warp → 64 Crops → Label from FEN) ──► manifest.jsonl
       ──► dataset (Stats, Balance, session-based split → split.json)
       ──► training (SquareDataset → SmallCNN/MobileNetV3 → best.pt + config.json)
       ──► Consumers: web/inference.predict_arrays · move_tracker (planned: CNN resync)

Parallel:  synth/ (RealityScan→Blender→PNG+JSON) ─┐
           chesscog / ChessReD (external)        ─┼─► ingest_adapters → ingest.synthesize_sessions
                                                  ┘   → Pseudo-Sessions → same slice path
```

The contracts are **file-based** (JSONL/YAML/JSON) — good for reproducibility and re-slicing,
but the schemas are nowhere formally documented (only implicitly in writer/reader code).

## Subsystems in Detail

**Core Pipeline** — cleanly staged, largely functional modules. `config.py` is the single
source for the class list, crop geometry, augment policy, and paths (the "config before code" principle is
followed). The headless core (geometry, state, stats) is pure and testable; camera/GUI coupling
is limited to the collect/calibration edges.

**Training** — SmallCNN (~100k params) or MobileNetV3-small (pretrained), three head variants
(combined / factored / twostage with explicit occupancy branch), CrossEntropy with class weights,
AdamW + Cosine, early stopping on `(macro_recall, board_acc)`. Split strictly per session.
Metrics: square_acc, macro_recall, board_acc (all 64 squares correct) plus diagnostic axes
(occ_acc, piece_acc, type_err, color_err).

**Web Layer** — FastAPI with ~30 endpoints (calibrate, collect, scan, manual, datasets,
training subprocess, inference, MJPEG streams), React/Vite SPA with 8 tabs, built assets are
committed to `web/static/`. State lives in four module-global dicts (`_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`,
`_INFER`, `_MANUAL`) without locks — works for single-user local operation, but is the
biggest structural weakness of the layer.

**move_tracker/** — prototype at repo-root level (deliberately outside the package). Clean
consumer of the chesslab library (calibration, web.camera), no logic duplication. Detection:
warp (live ArUco-tracked) → motion gate → rolling average → per-square diff with
median normalization → scoring over all legal moves → ambiguity check →
multi-frame voting. Threading: daemon capture loop + one lock around shared state.
No test, no packaging, no abstraction seam for a second (CNN) observer.

**synth/** — four-stage, manually orchestrated Blender pipeline (turntable photos → RealityScan →
isolate_piece → render_chessboard) with hardcoded relative paths; output flows through the
`synthetic` ingest adapter into the normal slice pipeline.

## Test Landscape

13 test files, ~89 tests. Well covered: core pipeline (calibration geometry, state, collect,
labeling, dataset, dataset_build, doctor, ingest chesscog/chessred), web routes partially
(TestClient). **Dark:** move_tracker (0 tests), synth/synthetic adapter (0 tests,
data integrity risk due to corner ordering), web.camera/streaming, CLI dispatch, GPU training loop
(deliberately torch-gated).

## Overall Assessment

The core pipeline is, for a single-person data tool, **above-average in cleanliness** of structure
(config-centric, session-based split, separate collect/slice, adapter pattern for ingest).
The risks are concentrated at the **edges**: (1) crop/photometry geometry is duplicated across
the labeling, training, and inference paths → train/serve skew, (2) web-layer global state
and error swallowing, (3) untested new subsystems (move_tracker, synth). Details in
[issues-and-concerns.md](issues-and-concerns.md), improvements in [recommendations.md](recommendations.md),
training/accuracy in [training-accuracy-improvements.md](training-accuracy-improvements.md).

    21│ │  Level 0  doctor.py          Env-/ROCm-/Camera Validation          │
    22│ │  Level 1  calibration.py     Homography, ArUco, MarkerTracker      │
    23│ │  Level 2  state.py           Game State (python-chess)             │
    24│ │  Level 3  collect.py, labeling.py, geometry3d.py, photometric.py   │
    25│ │  Level 4  dataset.py, dataset_build.py, sessions.py                │
    26│ │  Level 5  training/ (model, train, engine, evaluate, torch_data)   │
    27│ │  Level 7  experiment.py      Bake-off Grids (Geometry×Photometry)  │
    28│ │  NEW      ingest.py + ingest_adapters/ (chesscog, chessred, synth) │
    29│ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    30│ │  Data / Infrastructure                                             │
    31│ │  config.py (class list, crop/augment policy, paths)                │
    32│ │  data/ (sessions JSONL+YAML, squares, manifests JSONL, models)     │
    33│ │  synth/ (Blender render pipeline) + synth_assets/ + synth_pieces/  │
    34│ │  wheels/ (pinned ROCm Torch wheels for Windows)                    │
    35│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    36│ ```
    37│ 
    38│ ## Data Flow (Main Contract Chain)
    39│ 
    40│ ```
    41│ Camera ──► calibration (profile YAML: homography, corners, crop params)
    42│        ──► collect (session: log.jsonl {frame, ply, fen, corners?, labels?} + session.yaml)
    43│        ──► labeling.slice (Warp → 64 Crops → Label from FEN) ──► manifest.jsonl
    44│        ──► dataset (Stats, Balance, session-based split → split.json)
    45│        ──► training (SquareDataset → SmallCNN/MobileNetV3 → best.pt + config.json)
    46│        ──► Consumers: web/inference.predict_arrays · move_tracker (planned: CNN resync)
    47│ 
    48│ Parallel:  synth/ (RealityScan→Blender→PNG+JSON) ─┐
    49│            chesscog / ChessReD (external)        ─┼─► ingest_adapters → ingest.synthesize_sessions
    50│                                                   ┘   → Pseudo-Sessions → same slice path
    51│ ```
    52│ 
    53│ The contracts are **file-based** (JSONL/YAML/JSON) — good for reproducibility and re-slicing,
    54│ but the schemas are nowhere formally documented (only implicitly in writer/reader code).
    55│ 
    56│ ## Subsystems in Detail
    57│ 
    58│ **Core Pipeline** — cleanly staged, largely functional modules. `config.py` is the single
    59│ source for the class list, crop geometry, augment policy, and paths (the "config before code" principle is
    60│ followed). The headless core (geometry, state, stats) is pure and testable; camera/GUI coupling
    61│ is limited to the collect/calibration edges.
    62│ 
    63│ **Training** — SmallCNN (~100k params) or MobileNetV3-small (pretrained), three head variants
    64│ (combined / factored / twostage with explicit occupancy branch), CrossEntropy with class weights,
    65│ AdamW + Cosine, early stopping on `(macro_recall, board_acc)`. Split strictly per session.
    66│ Metrics: square_acc, macro_recall, board_acc (all 64 squares correct) plus diagnostic axes
    67│ (occ_acc, piece_acc, type_err, color_err).
    68│ 
    69│ **Web Layer** — FastAPI with ~30 endpoints (calibrate, collect, scan, manual, datasets,
    70│ training subprocess, inference, MJPEG streams), React/Vite SPA with 8 tabs, built assets are
    71│ committed to `web/static/`. State lives in four module-global dicts (`_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`,
    72│ `_INFER`, `_MANUAL`) without locks — works for single-user local operation, but is the
    73│ biggest structural weakness of the layer.
    74│ 
    75│ **move_tracker/** — prototype at repo-root level (deliberately outside the package). Clean
    76│ consumer of the chesslab library (calibration, web.camera), no logic duplication. Detection:
    77│ warp (live ArUco-tracked) → motion gate → rolling average → per-square diff with
    78│ median normalization → scoring over all legal moves → ambiguity check →
    79│ multi-frame voting. Threading: daemon capture loop + one lock around shared state.
    80│ No test, no packaging, no abstraction seam for a second (CNN) observer.
    81│ 
    82│ **synth/** — four-stage, manually orchestrated Blender pipeline (turntable photos → RealityScan →
    83│ isolate_piece → render_chessboard) with hardcoded relative paths; output flows through the
    84│ `synthetic` ingest adapter into the normal slice pipeline.
    85│ 
    86│ ## Test Landscape
    87│ 
    88│ 13 test files, ~89 tests. Well covered: core pipeline (calibration geometry, state, collect,
    89│ labeling, dataset, dataset_build, doctor, ingest chesscog/chessred), web routes partially
    90│ (TestClient). **Dark:** move_tracker (0 tests), synth/synthetic adapter (0 tests,
    91│ data integrity risk due to corner ordering), web.camera/streaming, CLI dispatch, GPU training loop
    92│ (deliberately torch-gated).
    93│ 
    94│ ## Overall Assessment
    95│ 
    96│ The core pipeline is, for a single-person data tool, **above-average in cleanliness** of structure
    97│ (config-centric, session-based split, separate collect/slice, adapter pattern for ingest).
    98│ The risks are concentrated at the **edges**: (1) crop/photometry geometry is duplicated across
    99│ the labeling, training, and inference paths → train/serve skew, (2) web-layer global state
   100│ and error swallowing, (3) untested new subsystems (move_tracker, synth). Details in
   101│ [issues-and-concerns.md](issues-and-concerns.md), improvements in [recommendations.md](recommendations.md),
   102│ training/accuracy in [training-accuracy-improvements.md](training-accuracy-improvements.md).
</file>

# Architektur-Issues & Bedenken

Konsolidiert aus vier Subsystem-Analysen (Kern-Pipeline, Training, Web, move_tracker/synth/tests),
dedupliziert und nach Schweregrad geordnet. Schweregrade sind auf den realen Einsatzkontext
kalibriert (lokales Single-User-Tool) — „Critical" heißt: gefährdet Datenintegrität oder das
Projektziel (verlässliches Move-Tracking), nicht „Server brennt".

---

## CRITICAL

### C1 — Crop-/Photometrie-Geometrie ist über Label- und Inference-Pfad dupliziert (Train/Serve-Skew)

- **Issue:** Dieselbe Crop-Berechnung existiert mehrfach: `calibration.square_to_crop_box`,
  `labeling.crop_square`/`crops_for_frame`, implizit in `training/torch_data.py`, und im
  Inference-Pfad. Konkret bereits schlagend: `web/inference.predict_arrays()` wendet **keine
  Photometrie** an — ein mit `clahe`/`gamma`-Photometrie trainiertes Modell liefert darüber
  nahezu zufällige Vorhersagen, obwohl seine val_acc 0.6–0.7 beträgt. Genau dieser Effekt wurde
  live beim move_tracker-CNN-Test beobachtet.
- **Impact:** Stiller Label↔Inference-Mismatch. Jeder neue Konsument (move_tracker-CNN-Resync!)
  muss die exakte Slice-Parität von Hand nachbauen; ein Parameter-Drift ist unsichtbar und äußert
  sich nur als „Modell ist schlecht".
- **Location:** `src/chesslab/calibration.py:170`, `src/chesslab/labeling.py:74–134`,
  `src/chesslab/training/torch_data.py`, `src/chesslab/web/inference.py:54–76`
- **Recommendation:** Eine gemeinsame Funktion „Frame + Profil + Run-Config → 64 modellfertige
  Crops", die Geometrie **und** Photometrie aus der Run-`config.json` anwendet; alle Konsumenten
  (slice, web-inference, move_tracker) rufen nur noch diese. Siehe recommendations.md R1.
- **Severity:** Critical

### C2 — Evaluations-Design erlaubt Positions-Overfitting (Datensatz-Architektur)

- **Issue:** In den Bake-off- und frühen Datensätzen steht jede Figurenart pro Session immer auf
  derselben Linie („a=König, b=Dame, …"), und mehrere Klassen kommen nur in **einer** Session vor
  (split.json warnt 12×, Test-Split leer). Das Modell kann „Linien-Index → Figurentyp" lernen
  statt visueller Merkmale; Train- und Val-Sessions teilen dieselbe Geometrie.
- **Impact:** val_acc überschätzt die echte Generalisierung massiv; board_acc kollabiert auf 0;
  Bake-off-Vergleiche (Geometrie×Photometrie×Kopf) messen teilweise Rauschen. Das ist die
  **Hauptursache der schwachen Move-Tracking-Genauigkeit** (Details:
  training-accuracy-improvements.md).
- **Location:** Datensatz-Design; sichtbar in `data/manifests/*/split.json`, `REPORT.md`
- **Recommendation:** Neue Sessions mit **zufälliger Figur-auf-Linie-Zuordnung** pro Session;
  Split-Validierung sollte hart fehlschlagen (nicht nur warnen), wenn eine Klasse nur in einer
  Session vorkommt.
- **Severity:** Critical (für das Projektziel)

### C3 — move_tracker und synthetic-Adapter komplett ungetestet (Datenintegrität)

- **Issue:** Kein einziger Test für `move_tracker/` (Diff-Normalisierung, Legal-Move-Scoring,
  Voting, Thread-Lifecycle) und keiner für den `synthetic`-Ingest-Adapter bzw. das
  JSON-Format von `render_chessboard.py` — insbesondere die Ecken-Reihenfolge `[a8,h8,h1,a1]`
  wird nirgends validiert.
- **Impact:** Eine vertauschte Ecken-Reihenfolge rotiert/spiegelt **alle** synthetischen Labels
  stillschweigend — das Modell trainiert dann auf systematisch falschen Daten. Beim move_tracker
  gibt es keinerlei Regressionsschutz für den gerade stark umgebauten Erkennungsalgorithmus.
- **Location:** `tests/` (fehlende Dateien), `tests/test_ingest.py` (Lücke),
  `synth/render_chessboard.py`
- **Recommendation:** `test_move_tracker.py` (reine Logik-Tests: `normalize_diffs`,
  `best_legal_move` mit synthetischen Diffs, Voting) und ein Schema-/Ecken-Reihenfolge-Test für
  den synthetic-Adapter (ohne Blender, gegen Beispiel-JSON).
- **Severity:** Critical (synthetic) / High (move_tracker)

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Web-Layer: unsynchronisierter Modul-Globalzustand

- **Issue:** `_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`, `_INFER`, `_MANUAL` (`web/app.py:36–57`) und
  `_STATE["tracker"]` (`move_tracker/app.py:19,35–41`) werden aus Request-Handlern und
  MJPEG-Generatoren ohne Lock gelesen/beschrieben. `BoardTracker.last_corners`
  (`web/camera.py:227–245`) ebenso.
- **Impact:** Im Single-User-Betrieb selten, aber real: ein laufender MJPEG-Generator liest
  `_COLLECT`, während `collect_finish()` es zurücksetzt → `None`-Zugriffe; zwei schnelle
  `/api/start` im move_tracker können zwei Capture-Threads hinterlassen.
- **Recommendation:** Ein `threading.Lock` pro Zustands-Dict; Generatoren kopieren den Zustand
  einmal pro Frame unter Lock (move_tracker/tracker.py macht das intern bereits vor — dasselbe
  Muster auf app-Ebene übernehmen).
- **Severity:** High

### H2 — Stilles Fehlerverschlucken im Web-Layer

- **Issue:** ~9 Stellen mit `except Exception: pass`-Charakter; prominent: Auto-Slice nach
  Collect-Finish (`web/app.py:794,1008`) meldet bei Fehler `sliced=0`, ohne den Fehler zu nennen.
  Kein Logging im gesamten Web-Layer (ein einzelnes `print`).
- **Impact:** Nutzer glaubt, es gäbe keine Crops / alles sei ok; Debugging nur per Raten.
- **Recommendation:** Fehler mindestens als Feld zurückgeben (`{"sliced": 0, "sliced_error": …}`)
  und per `logging` auf stderr protokollieren.
- **Severity:** High

### H3 — Training-Logdatei-Handle-Leak (Windows)

- **Issue:** `web/app.py:476–478` öffnet `web_train.log` und übergibt es an `subprocess.Popen`,
  schließt das Handle aber nie explizit.
- **Impact:** Unter Windows kann die Datei beim nächsten Trainingsstart gesperrt sein;
  Schließen hängt am nichtdeterministischen GC.
- **Recommendation:** Handle nach Popen sofort schließen (das Kind hält sein eigenes Duplikat)
  oder in `train_status()` beim Prozessende schließen.
- **Severity:** High

### H4 — Web importiert privates `_load_run` aus dem Training

- **Issue:** `web/inference.py:20` nutzt `training.evaluate._load_run` — privates Symbol als
  Layer-Contract.
- **Impact:** Kein stabiler Vertrag zwischen Training und Konsumenten; Refactoring im Training
  bricht Web/move_tracker stillschweigend.
- **Recommendation:** Öffentliche Funktion `training.load_run(run_dir) -> (model, cfg)`
  exportieren; alle Konsumenten umstellen.
- **Severity:** High

### H5 — synth-Pipeline: hartkodierte Pfade, keine Orchestrierung, hartkodierte Auflösung

- **Issue:** `render_chessboard.py` erwartet cwd-relative Pfade (`data/synth_raw`,
  `synth_assets/Chess Scene.blend`, `synth_pieces/`), Auflösung 1024px fest; die vierstufige
  Pipeline (capture → isolate → fens → render → ingest) ist nur im Kopf des Operators dokumentiert.
- **Impact:** Nicht reproduzierbar außerhalb des Repo-Roots; Fehlbedienung produziert stumm
  falsche Daten (siehe C3).
- **Location:** `synth/render_chessboard.py:301,315`, fehlendes `synth/README.md` bzw.
  Orchestrierungs-Skript
- **Recommendation:** Pfade über `config.Paths`/CLI-Args; ein `chesslab synth`-Subcommand oder
  Pipeline-Skript, das die Stufen verkettet.
- **Severity:** High

### H6 — MJPEG-Generator-Lebenszyklus

- **Issue:** Alle Stream-Endpoints nutzen `while True`-Generatoren ohne `try/finally`; sie lesen
  globalen Zustand pro Iteration und behandeln Kamerafehler nicht. Starlette schließt Generatoren
  bei Client-Disconnect zwar, aber synchrone Generatoren im Threadpool können verzögert abgeräumt
  werden und halten derweil `CAMERA.read()`-Polling am Leben.
- **Location:** `web/app.py:599–905`, `web/camera.py:210–224`, `move_tracker/app.py:88–98`
- **Recommendation:** `try/finally` um die Loops (Aufräumen/Logging), Zustand einmal pro Frame
  defensiv kopieren, `None`-Frames mit Fehlerbild statt Endlos-Retry beantworten.
- **Severity:** High → Medium (durch Starlette-Cleanup abgemildert)

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — Zirkuläre Kopplung `geometry3d ↔ labeling`

`labeling.py:21` importiert `geometry3d` direkt; `geometry3d.py:159` importiert lazy
`labeling._resize_keep_aspect` zurück. Der Lazy-Import kaschiert eine unvollständige
Refaktorierung. → `_resize_keep_aspect` in ein Utility-Modul (oder nach geometry3d) ziehen.

### M2 — Kein Request-Schema (Pydantic) im Web-Layer

POST-Endpoints nehmen rohe `Body(...)`-Parameter (z. B. `/api/train` mit 10+ Parametern,
`web/app.py:439–452`). Typfehler erst zur Laufzeit, OpenAPI-Schema unbrauchbar für Client-Generierung.
→ Pydantic-Request-Modelle, beginnend bei `/api/train` und `/api/datasets`.

### M3 — move_tracker: monolithischer Erkennungspfad, kein Observer-Seam

`_loop()`/`_try_detect()` (`tracker.py:200–289`) verdrahten Frame-Diff-Beobachtung, Scoring und
Voting fest. Der geplante CNN-Resync (zweiter Beobachter) muss sich heute „danebenquetschen".
→ Minimaler Seam: `_try_detect` konsultiert eine Liste von Beobachtern (frame-diff, optional CNN),
die je `(move, score)`-Kandidaten liefern.

### M4 — move_tracker: Paketierung & Lifecycle

Liegt außerhalb `src/`, nicht in `pyproject.toml`, kein CLI-Subcommand, `stop()` ohne
`join()` (`tracker.py:198`), Defaults nur im `__main__`-Pfad gesetzt (`app.py:121`).
Für einen Prototyp ok; vor Integration: nach `src/chesslab/move_tracker/` verschieben,
`chesslab track`-Subcommand, `join(timeout=2)` im stop().

### M5 — Schema-/Reader-Duplikation

Crop-Parameter als zwei Dataclasses (`config.CropDefaults` + `calibration.CropParams`),
JSONL-Manifest-Parsing 3× (dataset, labeling, training/data), Label→FEN-Logik lokal in
`web/app.py:60–84` statt aus `labeling`/`config` importiert. → je eine kanonische Stelle.

### M6 — board_acc als Steuermetrik zu hart / Checkpoint-Wahl instabil

board_acc (alle 64 Felder korrekt) ist bei 8–70 Val-Frames extrem varianzbehaftet und für
Early-Stopping/Vergleiche wenig informativ; Stopp-Epochen schwanken 31–163.
→ occupancy-gewichtete Metrik für Checkpoint-Wahl (siehe training-accuracy-improvements.md).

### M7 — Kein strukturiertes Logging projekt­weit

Pipeline nutzt konsistente `print`-Glyphen (`[OK]/[FAIL]`), Web-Layer fast gar nichts.
Für ein CLI-Tool akzeptabel; für die Web-/Tracker-Daemons lohnt `logging` mit Modul-Loggern.

---

## LOW

- **L1** Frontend pollt (1–2.5 s Intervalle) statt SSE/WebSocket — für lokalen Betrieb fein.
- **L2** Handgeschriebener `fetch`-Client, Typen im Frontend dupliziert — OpenAPI-Client-Generierung
  wäre möglich (FastAPI liefert das Schema schon), lohnt erst bei API-Wachstum.
- **L3** Gebaute Frontend-Assets werden committet — bewusste Entscheidung (kein Node nötig zum
  Ausführen), erfordert Disziplin (`npm run build` vor Commit).
- **L4** DHash-Größe (dataset_build.py:47) und Overlay-Zeichenkonstanten hartkodiert.

  den synthetic-Adapter (ohne Blender, gegen Beispiel-JSON).

### H1 — Web-Layer: unsynchronisierter Modul-Globalzustand

- **Issue:** `_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`, `_INFER`, `_MANUAL` (`web/app.py:36–57`) und
  `_STATE["tracker"]` (`move_tracker/app.py:19,35–41`) werden aus Request-Handlern und
  MJPEG-Generatoren ohne Lock gelesen/beschrieben. `BoardTracker.last_corners`
  (`web/camera.py:227–245`) ebenso.
- **Impact:** Im Single-User-Betrieb selten, aber real: ein laufender MJPEG-Generator liest
  `_COLLECT`, während `collect_finish()` es zurücksetzt → `None`-Zugriffe; zwei schnelle
  `/api/start` im move_tracker können zwei Capture-Threads hinterlassen.
- **Recommendation:** Ein `threading.Lock` pro Zustands-Dict; Generatoren kopieren den Zustand
  einmal pro Frame unter Lock (move_tracker/tracker.py macht das intern bereits vor — dasselbe
  Muster auf app-Ebene übernehmen).
- **Severity:** High

### H2 — Stilles Fehlerverschlucken im Web-Layer

- **Issue:** ~9 Stellen mit `except Exception: pass`-Charakter; prominent: Auto-Slice nach
  Collect-Finish (`web/app.py:794,1008`) meldet bei Fehler `sliced=0`, ohne den Fehler zu nennen.
  Kein Logging im gesamten Web-Layer (ein einzelnes `print`).
- **Impact:** Nutzer glaubt, es gäbe keine Crops / alles sei ok; Debugging nur per Raten.
- **Recommendation:** Fehler mindestens als Feld zurückgeben (`{"sliced": 0, "sliced_error": …}`)
  und per `logging` auf stderr protokollieren.
- **Severity:** High

### H3 — Training-Logdatei-Handle-Leak (Windows)

- **Issue:** `web/app.py:476–478` öffnet `web_train.log` und übergibt es an `subprocess.Popen`,
  schließt das Handle aber nie explizit.
- **Impact:** Unter Windows kann die Datei beim nächsten Trainingsstart gesperrt sein;
  Schließen hängt am nichtdeterministischen GC.
- **Recommendation:** Handle nach Popen sofort schließen (das Kind hält sein eigenes Duplikat)
  oder in `train_status()` beim Prozessende schließen.
- **Severity:** High

### H4 — Web importiert privates `_load_run` aus dem Training

- **Issue:** `web/inference.py:20` nutzt `training.evaluate._load_run` — privates Symbol als
  Layer-Contract.
- **Impact:** Kein stabiler Vertrag zwischen Training und Konsumenten; Refactoring im Training
  bricht Web/move_tracker stillschweigend.
- **Recommendation:** Öffentliche Funktion `training.load_run(run_dir) -> (model, cfg)`
  exportieren; alle Konsumenten umstellen.
- **Severity:** High

### H5 — synth-Pipeline: hartkodierte Pfade, keine Orchestrierung, hartkodierte Auflösung

- **Issue:** `render_chessboard.py` erwartet cwd-relative Pfade (`data/synth_raw`,
  `synth_assets/Chess Scene.blend`, `synth_pieces/`), Auflösung 1024px fest; die vierstufige
  Pipeline (capture → isolate → fens → render → ingest) ist nur im Kopf des Operators dokumentiert.
- **Impact:** Nicht reproduzierbar außerhalb des Repo-Roots; Fehlbedienung produziert stumm
  falsche Daten (siehe C3).
- **Location:** `synth/render_chessboard.py:301,315`, fehlendes `synth/README.md` bzw.
  Orchestrierungs-Skript
- **Recommendation:** Pfade über `config.Paths`/CLI-Args; ein `chesslab synth`-Subcommand oder
  Pipeline-Skript, das die Stufen verkettet.
- **Severity:** High

### H6 — MJPEG-Generator-Lebenszyklus

- **Issue:** Alle Stream-Endpoints nutzen `while True`-Generatoren ohne `try/finally`; sie lesen
  globalen Zustand pro Iteration und behandeln Kamerafehler nicht. Starlette schließt Generatoren
  bei Client-Disconnect zwar, aber synchrone Generatoren im Threadpool können verzögert abgeräumt
  werden und halten derweil `CAMERA.read()`-Polling am Leben.
- **Location:** `web/app.py:599–905`, `web/camera.py:210–224`, `move_tracker/app.py:88–98`
- **Recommendation:** `try/finally` um die Loops (Aufräumen/Logging), Zustand einmal pro Frame
  defensiv kopieren, `None`-Frames mit Fehlerbild statt Endlos-Retry beantworten.
- **Severity:** High → Medium (durch Starlette-Cleanup abgemildert)

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — Zirkuläre Kopplung `geometry3d ↔ labeling`

`labeling.py:21` importiert `geometry3d` direkt; `geometry3d.py:159` importiert lazy
`labeling._resize_keep_aspect` zurück. Der Lazy-Import kaschiert eine unvollständige
Refaktorierung. → `_resize_keep_aspect` in ein Utility-Modul (oder nach geometry3d) ziehen.

### M2 — Kein Request-Schema (Pydantic) im Web-Layer

POST-Endpoints nehmen rohe `Body(...)`-Parameter (z. B. `/api/train` mit 10+ Parametern,
`web/app.py:439–452`). Typfehler erst zur Laufzeit, OpenAPI-Schema unbrauchbar für Client-Generierung.
→ Pydantic-Request-Modelle, beginnend bei `/api/train` und `/api/datasets`.

### M3 — move_tracker: monolithischer Erkennungspfad, kein Observer-Seam

`_loop()`/`_try_detect()` (`tracker.py:200–289`) verdrahten Frame-Diff-Beobachtung, Scoring und
Voting fest. Der geplante CNN-Resync (zweiter Beobachter) muss sich heute „danebenquetschen".
→ Minimaler Seam: `_try_detect` konsultiert eine Liste von Beobachtern (frame-diff, optional CNN),
die je `(move, score)`-Kandidaten liefern.

### M4 — move_tracker: Paketierung & Lifecycle

Liegt außerhalb `src/`, nicht in `pyproject.toml`, kein CLI-Subcommand, `stop()` ohne
`join()` (`tracker.py:198`), Defaults nur im `__main__`-Pfad gesetzt (`app.py:121`).

JSONL-Manifest-Parsing 3× (dataset, labeling, training/data), Label→FEN-Logik lokal in
`web/app.py:60–84` statt aus `labeling`/`config` importiert. → je eine kanonische Stelle.

board_acc (alle 64 Felder korrekt) ist bei 8–70 Val-Frames extrem varianzbehaftet und für
Early-Stopping/Vergleiche wenig informativ; Stopp-Epochen schwanken 31–163.
→ occupancy-gewichtete Metrik für Checkpoint-Wahl (siehe training-accuracy-improvements.md).

### M7 — Kein strukturiertes Logging projekt­weit

Pipeline nutzt konsistente `print`-Glyphen (`[OK]/[FAIL]`), Web-Layer fast gar nichts.
Für ein CLI-Tool akzeptabel; für die Web-/Tracker-Daemons lohnt `logging` mit Modul-Loggern.

---

## LOW

- **L1** Frontend pollt (1–2.5 s Intervalle) statt SSE/WebSocket — für lokalen Betrieb fein.
- **L2** Handgeschriebener `fetch`-Client, Typen im Frontend dupliziert — OpenAPI-Client-Generierung
  wäre möglich (FastAPI liefert das Schema schon), lohnt erst bei API-Wachstum.
- **L3** Gebaute Frontend-Assets werden committet — bewusste Entscheidung (kein Node nötig zum
  Ausführen), erfordert Disziplin (`npm run build` vor Commit).
- **L4** DHash-Größe (dataset_build.py:47) und Overlay-Zeichenkonstanten hartkodiert.

# Architecture Issues & Concerns

Consolidated from four subsystem analyses (Core Pipeline, Training, Web, move_tracker/synth/tests),
deduplicated and ordered by severity. Severity levels are calibrated to the real deployment context
(local single-user tool) — "Critical" means: endangers data integrity or the
project goal (reliable move tracking), not "server is on fire".

---

## CRITICAL

### C1 — Crop/Photometry Geometry Duplicated Across Label and Inference Paths (Train/Serve Skew)

- **Issue:** The same crop calculation exists in multiple places: `calibration.square_to_crop_box`,
  `labeling.crop_square`/`crops_for_frame`, implicitly in `training/torch_data.py`, and in the
  inference path. This has already manifested concretely: `web/inference.predict_arrays()` applies **no
  photometry** — a model trained with `clahe`/`gamma` photometry produces
  near-random predictions through it, despite its val_acc being 0.6–0.7. This exact effect was
  observed live during the move_tracker CNN test.
- **Impact:** Silent Label↔Inference mismatch. Every new consumer (move_tracker CNN resync!)
  must manually reconstruct the exact slice parity; parameter drift is invisible and manifests
  only as "the model is bad".
- **Location:** `src/chesslab/calibration.py:170`, `src/chesslab/labeling.py:74–134`,
  `src/chesslab/training/torch_data.py`, `src/chesslab/web/inference.py:54–76`
- **Recommendation:** A single function "Frame + Profile + Run-Config → 64 model-ready
  Crops" that applies geometry **and** photometry from the run `config.json`; all consumers
  (slice, web-inference, move_tracker) call only this. See recommendations.md R1.
- **Severity:** Critical

### C2 — Evaluation Design Allows Positional Overfitting (Dataset Architecture)

- **Issue:** In the bake-off and early datasets, each piece type always appears on the
  same rank per session ("a=King, b=Queen, …"), and multiple classes appear in only **one** session
  (split.json warns 12×, Test-Split empty). The model can learn "rank index → piece type"
  instead of visual features; Train and Val sessions share the same geometry.
- **Impact:** val_acc massively overestimates true generalization; board_acc collapses to 0;
  bake-off comparisons (Geometry×Photometry×Head) partially measure noise. This is the
  **main cause of poor move tracking accuracy** (details:
  training-accuracy-improvements.md).
- **Location:** Dataset design; visible in `data/manifests/*/split.json`, `REPORT.md`
- **Recommendation:** New sessions with **random piece-to-rank assignment** per session;
  split validation should hard-fail (not just warn) when a class appears in only one
  session.
- **Severity:** Critical (for the project goal)

### C3 — move_tracker and synthetic Adapter Completely Untested (Data Integrity)

- **Issue:** Not a single test for `move_tracker/` (diff normalization, legal move scoring,
  voting, thread lifecycle) and none for the `synthetic` ingest adapter or the
  JSON format of `render_chessboard.py` — in particular the corner order `[a8,h8,h1,a1]`
  is never validated anywhere.
- **Impact:** A swapped corner order silently rotates/mirrors **all** synthetic labels —
  the model then trains on systematically wrong data. For move_tracker,
  there is zero regression protection for the recently heavily refactored detection algorithm.
- **Location:** `tests/` (missing files), `tests/test_ingest.py` (gap),
  `synth/render_chessboard.py`
- **Recommendation:** `test_move_tracker.py` (pure logic tests: `normalize_diffs`,
  `best_legal_move` with synthetic diffs, voting) and a schema/corner-order test for
  the synthetic adapter (without Blender, against example JSON).
- **Severity:** Critical (synthetic) / High (move_tracker)

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Web Layer: Unsynchronized Module Global State

- **Issue:** `_TRAIN`, `_COLLECT`, `_INFER`, `_MANUAL` (`web/app.py:36–57`) and
  `_STATE["tracker"]` (`move_tracker/app.py:19,35–41`) are read/written from request handlers and
  MJPEG generators without a lock. `BoardTracker.last_corners`
  (`web/camera.py:227–245`) as well.
- **Impact:** Rare in single-user operation, but real: a running MJPEG generator reads
  `_COLLECT` while `collect_finish()` resets it → `None` accesses; two rapid
  `/api/start` calls in move_tracker can leave two capture threads behind.
- **Recommendation:** One `threading.Lock` per state dict; generators copy the state
  once per frame under lock (move_tracker/tracker.py already does this internally — adopt the same
  pattern at the app level).
- **Severity:** High

### H2 — Silent Error Swallowing in the Web Layer

- **Issue:** ~9 locations with `except Exception: pass` character; prominent: auto-slice after
  collect-finish (`web/app.py:794,1008`) reports `sliced=0` on error without naming the error.
  No logging in the entire web layer (a single `print`).
- **Impact:** User believes there are no crops / everything is ok; debugging only by guessing.
- **Recommendation:** At minimum return errors as a field (`{"sliced": 0, "sliced_error": …}`)
  and log via `logging` to stderr.
- **Severity:** High

### H3 — Training Log File Handle Leak (Windows)

- **Issue:** `web/app.py:476–478` opens `web_train.log` and passes it to `subprocess.Popen`,
  but never explicitly closes the handle.
- **Impact:** On Windows, the file may be locked on the next training start;
  closing depends on non-deterministic GC.
- **Recommendation:** Close the handle immediately after Popen (the child holds its own duplicate)
  or close it in `train_status()` when the process ends.
- **Severity:** High

### H4 — Web Imports Private `_load_run` from Training

- **Issue:** `web/inference.py:20` uses `training.evaluate._load_run` — private symbol as a
  layer contract.
- **Impact:** No stable contract between training and consumers; refactoring in training
  silently breaks web/move_tracker.
- **Recommendation:** Export a public function `training.load_run(run_dir) -> (model, cfg)`;
  migrate all consumers.
- **Severity:** High

### H5 — synth Pipeline: Hardcoded Paths, No Orchestration, Hardcoded Resolution

- **Issue:** `render_chessboard.py` expects cwd-relative paths (`data/synth_raw`,
  `synth_assets/Chess Scene.blend`, `synth_pieces/`), fixed resolution 1024px; the four-stage
  pipeline (capture → isolate → fens → render → ingest) is only documented in the operator's head.
- **Impact:** Not reproducible outside the repo root; misoperation silently produces
  wrong data (see C3).
- **Location:** `synth/render_chessboard.py:301,315`, missing `synth/README.md` or
  orchestration script
- **Recommendation:** Paths via `config.Paths`/CLI args; a `chesslab synth` subcommand or
  pipeline script that chains the stages.
- **Severity:** High

### H6 — MJPEG Generator Lifecycle

- **Issue:** All stream endpoints use `while True` generators without `try/finally`; they read
  global state every iteration and do not handle camera errors. Starlette does close generators
  on client disconnect, but synchronous generators in the thread pool may be cleaned up with
  a delay and meanwhile keep `CAMERA.read()` polling alive.
- **Location:** `web/app.py:599–905`, `web/camera.py:210–224`, `move_tracker/app.py:88–98`
- **Recommendation:** `try/finally` around the loops (cleanup/logging), defensively copy state
  once per frame, respond to `None` frames with an error frame instead of endless retry.
- **Severity:** High → Medium (mitigated by Starlette cleanup)

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — Circular Coupling `geometry3d ↔ labeling`

`labeling.py:21` imports `geometry3d` directly; `geometry3d.py:159` lazy-imports
`labeling._resize_keep_aspect` back. The lazy import masks an incomplete
refactoring. → Move `_resize_keep_aspect` into a utility module (or into geometry3d).

### M2 — No Request Schema (Pydantic) in the Web Layer

POST endpoints take raw `Body(...)` parameters (e.g. `/api/train` with 10+ parameters,
`web/app.py:439–452`). Type errors only surface at runtime, OpenAPI schema is useless for client generation.
→ Pydantic request models, starting with `/api/train` and `/api/datasets`.

### M3 — move_tracker: Monolithic Detection Path, No Observer Seam

`_loop()`/`_try_detect()` (`tracker.py:200–289`) hardwire frame-diff observation, scoring and
voting. The planned CNN resync (second observer) currently has to "squeeze in sideways".
→ Minimal seam: `_try_detect` consults a list of observers (frame-diff, optional CNN),
each providing `(move, score)` candidates.

### M4 — move_tracker: Packaging & Lifecycle

Lives outside `src/`, not in `pyproject.toml`, no CLI subcommand, `stop()` without
`join()` (`tracker.py:198`), defaults only set in the `__main__` path (`app.py:121`).
Fine for a prototype; before integration: move to `src/chesslab/move_tracker/`,
`chesslab track` subcommand, `join(timeout=2)` in stop().

### M5 — Schema/Reader Duplication

Crop parameters as two dataclasses (`config.CropDefaults` + `calibration.CropParams`),
JSONL manifest parsing 3× (dataset, labeling, training/data), Label→FEN logic locally in
`web/app.py:60–84` instead of imported from `labeling`/`config`. → one canonical location each.

### M6 — board_acc as Control Metric Too Strict / Checkpoint Selection Unstable

board_acc (all 64 squares correct) is extremely high-variance with 8–70 Val frames and
poorly informative for early stopping/comparisons; stop epochs fluctuate 31–163.
→ occupancy-weighted metric for checkpoint selection (see training-accuracy-improvements.md).

### M7 — No Structured Logging Project-Wide

Pipeline uses consistent `print` glyphs (`[OK]/[FAIL]`), Web layer almost nothing.
Acceptable for a CLI tool; for the web/tracker daemons `logging` with module loggers is worthwhile.

---

## LOW

- **L1** Frontend polls (1–2.5 s intervals) instead of SSE/WebSocket — fine for local operation.
- **L2** Hand-written `fetch` client, types duplicated in the frontend — OpenAPI client generation
  would be possible (FastAPI already serves the schema), only worthwhile when the API grows.
- **L3** Built frontend assets are committed — deliberate decision (no Node needed to
  run), requires discipline (`npm run build` before commit).
- **L4** DHash size (dataset_build.py:47) and overlay drawing constants hardcoded.

"""CNN-assisted occupancy recovery for the Move-Tracker (specs/rework/09-cnn-recovery.md).

No full-FEN resync: The CNN only provides **occupancy** per square (empty / occupied /
occluded) — piece identity is known to the tracker from the move history. This lets it
(a) find the move whose resulting occupancy best explains the observation when frame-diff
detection is stuck (structurally covers captures, castling, en passant), and
(b) periodically check whether the believed state and the board still match.

Runs entirely through the serving facade (`chesslab.serving`) — no own crop/preprocessing
logic is created here. torch stays unimported until actually observed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import chess

from .. import config

log = logging.getLogger("chesslab.move_tracker")

_FILES = "abcdefgh"
_ALL = [f"{f}{r}" for r in range(1, 9) for f in _FILES]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OccupancyObservation:
    """CNN view of the board. Carries occupancy (p_occupied/empty/occluded) AND — when
    available — the full piece identity per square (`label` = predicted class,
    `conf` = top-class confidence). Occupancy is derived from identity; identity
    makes it possible to distinguish captures/promotions/"which piece moved" and to
    reliably separate shadows (identity unchanged) from real moves."""

    p_occ: dict[str, float]
    p_empty: dict[str, float]
    p_occluded: dict[str, float]
    label: dict[str, str] | None = None       # predicted class per square (e.g. 'wP','bK','empty')
    conf: dict[str, float] | None = None       # top-class confidence per square

    def occupied(self, sq: str) -> bool:
        return self.p_occ[sq] > self.p_empty[sq]

    def confident(self, thr: float) -> dict[str, bool]:
        """Squares whose occupancy statement is reliable. IMPORTANT: occluded-dominant squares
        are NEVER confident and NEVER count as occupied — a hand over the board must neither
        trigger recovery nor "occupy" squares."""
        return {sq: (max(self.p_occ[sq], self.p_empty[sq]) >= thr
                     and self.p_occluded[sq] < (1.0 - thr))
                for sq in self.p_occ}

    def label_confident(self, thr: float) -> dict[str, bool]:
        """Squares whose IDENTITY statement is reliable: top confidence ≥ thr and not
        `occluded` (hand/covering). Empty when the run provides no identity."""
        if self.label is None or self.conf is None:
            return dict.fromkeys(self.p_occ, False)
        return {sq: (self.conf[sq] >= thr and self.label[sq] != "occluded")
                for sq in self.label}


def observation_from_probs(per_square_probs: dict[str, list[float]],
                           classes: list[str]) -> OccupancyObservation:
    """Full softmax per square → occupancy + identity. Class indices ALWAYS derived from the
    `classes` list of the run config (13- and 14-class runs, never guess positions)."""
    i_empty = classes.index("empty")
    i_occl = classes.index("occluded") if "occluded" in classes else None
    p_occ: dict[str, float] = {}
    p_empty: dict[str, float] = {}
    p_occluded: dict[str, float] = {}
    label: dict[str, str] = {}
    conf: dict[str, float] = {}
    for sq, probs in per_square_probs.items():
        pe = float(probs[i_empty])
        po = float(probs[i_occl]) if i_occl is not None else 0.0
        p_empty[sq] = pe
        p_occluded[sq] = po
        p_occ[sq] = max(0.0, 1.0 - pe - po)     # sum of the 12 piece classes
        top = max(range(len(probs)), key=lambda i: probs[i])   # identity = argmax class
        label[sq] = classes[top]
        conf[sq] = float(probs[top])
    return OccupancyObservation(p_occ=p_occ, p_empty=p_empty, p_occluded=p_occluded,
                                label=label, conf=conf)


def _move_touched_squares(board: chess.Board, move: chess.Move) -> set[str]:
    """Squares physically changed by a move: from, to, + rook on castling, + captured
    pawn on en passant. (Mirrors tracker.move_touched_squares, without circular import.)"""
    sqs = {chess.square_name(move.from_square), chess.square_name(move.to_square)}
    if board.is_castling(move):
        rank = chess.square_rank(move.from_square)
        if chess.square_file(move.to_square) > chess.square_file(move.from_square):
            sqs |= {chess.square_name(chess.square(7, rank)), chess.square_name(chess.square(5, rank))}
        else:
            sqs |= {chess.square_name(chess.square(0, rank)), chess.square_name(chess.square(3, rank))}
    if board.is_en_passant(move):
        sqs.add(chess.square_name(chess.square(chess.square_file(move.to_square),
                                               chess.square_rank(move.from_square))))
    return sqs


def expected_occupancy(board: chess.Board) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Occupancy per square as expected from the game state."""
    return {sq: board.piece_at(chess.parse_square(sq)) is not None for sq in _ALL}


def expected_labels(board: chess.Board) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Expected piece class per square according to the game state ('wP','bK','empty', …) in
    model vocabulary (uses `config.label_from_piece`)."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for sq in _ALL:
        piece = board.piece_at(chess.parse_square(sq))
        out[sq] = config.label_from_piece(piece.symbol() if piece else None)
    return out


class CnnRecovery:
    """Observes the board via CNN (occupancy) and suggests moves or conflicts.

    `observe` is the expensive step (~100–300 ms CPU) and must NEVER run under the tracker lock.
    `score_moves`/`resync_check` are pure evaluations on the observation.
    """

    def __init__(self, run_dir: Path, profile, device: str = "cpu",
                 conf_thr: float = 0.85, min_agreement: float = 0.97,
                 margin_squares: int = 1, min_confident_board: int = 32,
                 min_confident_recovery: int = 8) -> None:
        self.run_dir = Path(run_dir)
        self.profile = profile
        self.device = device
        self.conf_thr = conf_thr
        self.min_agreement = min_agreement       # best move must explain this many confident squares
        # Margin in SQUARES, not a fraction: a capture differs from a non-capture
        # at the occupancy level by exactly ONE square (only the from-square empties; the target
        # was already occupied) — a fractional margin would falsely discard captures as ambiguous.
        # margin_squares=1: strictly better is enough; 0 squares difference (promotion variants) ⇒ None.
        self.margin_squares = margin_squares
        # min_confident SPLIT (Spec 10, part 6): the whole-board match may only update the reference
        # with plenty of clear sight (otherwise re-anchor against a covered board);
        # the recovery, on the other hand, must remain operable even under partial occlusion.
        self.min_confident_board = min_confident_board
        self.min_confident_recovery = min_confident_recovery
        self._classes: list[str] | None = None   # lazy from run_spec (once, not per observe)
        if not (self.run_dir / "config.json").exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Model run not found: {self.run_dir}")

    # -- Observation (torch, expensive — never under lock) --
    def observe(self, frame, corners) -> OccupancyObservation:
        from .. import serving  # lazy: torch stays out as long as not observed

        preds = serving.predict_frame(self.run_dir, frame, corners, self.profile,
                                      device=self.device, return_probs=True)
        if self._classes is None:
            self._classes = serving.run_spec(self.run_dir).classes
        return observation_from_probs({p["square"]: p["probs"] for p in preds}, self._classes)

    # -- Pure evaluation --
    def score_moves(self, board: chess.Board,
                    obs: OccupancyObservation) -> tuple[chess.Move | None, float, float]:
        """For each legal move: push board copy → expected occupancy → agreement
        with the observation over the confident squares. (None, best, second) when nothing
        is clear enough (min_agreement / margin / too few confident squares)."""
        conf = obs.confident(self.conf_thr)
        conf_squares = [sq for sq, ok in conf.items() if ok]
        n = len(conf_squares)
        if n < self.min_confident_recovery:
            return None, 0.0, 0.0
        best_mv, best_hits, second_hits = None, -1, -1
        for mv in board.legal_moves:
            b2 = board.copy(stack=False)
            b2.push(mv)
            hits = sum(1 for sq in conf_squares
                       if obs.occupied(sq) == (b2.piece_at(chess.parse_square(sq)) is not None))
            if hits > best_hits:
                best_hits, second_hits, best_mv = hits, best_hits, mv
            elif hits > second_hits:
                second_hits = hits

        second = second_hits / n if second_hits >= 0 else 0.0
        if best_mv is None or best < self.min_agreement \
           or (best_hits - second_hits) < self.margin_squares:
            # margin in squares: promotion variants (e7e8q vs. e7e8r) are occupancy-identical
            # (0 squares difference) → intentionally None (user hint instead of guessing).
            return None, best, second
        return best_mv, best, second

    def verify_move(self, board: chess.Board, move: chess.Move,
                    obs: OccupancyObservation) -> tuple[float, int]:
        """Pre-commit check of a concrete candidate move — LOCAL instead of whole-board:
        Only the occupancy of squares physically changed by the move counts (from becomes empty,
        to becomes occupied; + rook on castling, + captured pawn on en passant). This is exactly
        the definition of a move and is robust against shadows/occlusion on the rest of the board.

        Returns (agreement, n): fraction of touched & confident squares whose observed
        occupancy matches the position AFTER the move. Both endpoints must be confident —
        if, e.g., the target square is still covered by a hand, the move is (still) considered
        unconfirmed (agreement 0.0), and the multi-frame check waits for a clear view."""
        conf = obs.confident(self.conf_thr)
        touched = _move_touched_squares(board, move)
        b2 = board.copy(stack=False)
        b2.push(move)
        checked = [sq for sq in touched if conf.get(sq)]
        if len(checked) < 2:                      # at least FROM and TO squares must be reliable

    @staticmethod
    def _label_at(board: chess.Board, sq: str) -> str:
        piece = board.piece_at(chess.parse_square(sq))
        return config.label_from_piece(piece.symbol() if piece else None)

        """Does the CNN see the SAME pieces on all confident squares as believed?
        The reliable "no move / shadow" detector: a shadow changes no identity.
        {match, conflicts, n, inconclusive}. Too few confident squares → inconclusive."""
        lc = obs.label_confident(self.conf_thr)
        exp = expected_labels(board)
        checked = [sq for sq in _ALL if lc.get(sq)]
        if len(checked) < self.min_confident_board:
            return {"match": False, "conflicts": [], "n": len(checked), "inconclusive": True}
        conflicts = [sq for sq in checked if obs.label[sq] != exp[sq]]
        return {"match": not conflicts, "conflicts": conflicts,
                "n": len(checked), "inconclusive": False}

    def derive_moves_identity(self, board: chess.Board, obs: OccupancyObservation,
                              max_plies: int = 1) -> tuple[list[chess.Move], float, float]:
        """Choose the legal move SEQUENCE (1 or — with max_plies=2 — 2 half-moves) whose
        resulting identities best match the CNN observation. Single moves are preferred;
        move pairs rescue the case "reply came before commit" (blitz). The order in a
        pair is fixed by side-to-move (first the side to move, then the reply) —
        no order ambiguity. ~35×35 ≈ 1200 pair candidates are pure evaluation, not critical.

        Returns ([], best, second) when nothing is clear enough (min_agreement /
        margin_squares / too few confident squares)."""
        lc = obs.label_confident(self.conf_thr)
        conf_squares = [sq for sq, ok in lc.items() if ok]
        n = len(conf_squares)
        if n < self.min_confident_recovery:
            return [], 0.0, 0.0

        def _hits(b: chess.Board) -> int:
            return sum(1 for sq in conf_squares if obs.label[sq] == self._label_at(b, sq))

        def _pick(candidates) -> tuple[list[chess.Move], int, int]:
            best_seq, best_hits, second_hits = [], -1, -1
            for seq, b in candidates:
                h = _hits(b)
                if h > best_hits:
                    best_hits, second_hits, best_seq = h, best_hits, seq
                elif h > second_hits:
                    second_hits = h
            return best_seq, best_hits, second_hits

        singles = []
        for mv in board.legal_moves:
            b2 = board.copy(stack=False)
            b2.push(mv)
            singles.append(([mv], b2))
        seq, best_hits, second_hits = _pick(singles)
        best = best_hits / n if best_hits >= 0 else 0.0
        second = second_hits / n if second_hits >= 0 else 0.0
        if seq and best >= self.min_agreement and (best_hits - second_hits) >= self.margin_squares:
            return seq, best, second

        if max_plies >= 2:
            pairs = []
            for mv1, b2 in ((s[0][0], s[1]) for s in singles):
                for mv2 in b2.legal_moves:
                    b3 = b2.copy(stack=False)
                    b3.push(mv2)
                    pairs.append(([mv1, mv2], b3))
            pseq, p_hits, p_second = _pick(pairs)
            p_best = p_hits / n if p_hits >= 0 else 0.0
            # The pair must be unambiguous: margin against the second-best pair AND against the
            # best single move (otherwise the single move would be the more parsimonious explanation).
            if pseq and p_best >= self.min_agreement \
               and (p_hits - max(p_second, best_hits)) >= self.margin_squares:
                return pseq, p_best, max(p_second, best_hits) / n
        return [], best, second

    def derive_move_identity(self, board: chess.Board,
                             obs: OccupancyObservation) -> tuple[chess.Move | None, float, float]:
        """1-ply wrapper around `derive_moves_identity` (pre-commit verify needs exactly one move).
        Resolves capture (target identity), "which piece" and promotion (promo piece from the
        target label). (None, best, second) when not clear enough."""
        seq, best, second = self.derive_moves_identity(board, obs, max_plies=1)
        return (seq[0] if seq else None), best, second

    def verify_move_identity(self, board: chess.Board, move: chess.Move,
                             obs: OccupancyObservation) -> tuple[float, int]:
        """Pre-commit check of a candidate move via the IDENTITY of the touched squares
        (from is vacated/empty, to carries the expected piece; + rook/en-passant). Both
        endpoints must be confident, otherwise (still) unconfirmed (0.0)."""
        lc = obs.label_confident(self.conf_thr)
        touched = _move_touched_squares(board, move)
        b2 = board.copy(stack=False)
        b2.push(move)
        checked = [sq for sq in touched if lc.get(sq)]
        if len(checked) < 2:
            return 0.0, len(checked)
        hits = sum(1 for sq in checked if obs.label[sq] == self._label_at(b2, sq))
        return hits / len(checked), len(checked)

    def resync_check(self, board: chess.Board, obs: OccupancyObservation) -> dict:
        """Diff believed vs. observed occupancy (confident squares only).

        {"match": bool, "conflicts": [squares], "move": uci|None, "agreement": float}
        — `move` only if exactly one legal move sufficiently explains the observation."""
        conf = obs.confident(self.conf_thr)
        believed = expected_occupancy(board)
        conflicts = [sq for sq in _ALL if conf.get(sq) and obs.occupied(sq) != believed[sq]]
        if not conflicts:
            return {"match": True, "conflicts": [], "move": None, "agreement": 1.0}
        mv, best, _second = self.score_moves(board, obs)
        return {"match": False, "conflicts": conflicts,
                "move": mv.uci() if mv else None, "agreement": max(best, 0.0)}
